KS-1305.desc:
## BLUF

**No fresh clone or worktree of this repository can run a** `withTenant` **integration cell in single-tenant mode.** The generated Prisma client does not exist, and `prisma generate` cannot produce it from the obvious invocation.

Measured 2026-09-25 against a real disposable PostgreSQL:

```
Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default' from 'node_modules/@prisma/client/default.js'
  at getPrismaClient (src/db.ts:116)
  at withTenant (src/db.ts:329)
```

The callback never runs, so the cell reports a **module** error where a reader expects a database result. In one cell `{ code: "MODULE_NOT_FOUND" }` arrived where `{ code: "SHARE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND" }` was expected — **that reads as a product defect and is not one.**

## The mechanism, each part measured

1. `@prisma/client` **and the** `prisma` **CLI are declared and installed ONLY in** `services/originate` (`^7.8.0`). `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` declares none of them; `Blockchain/Dev/node_modules/@prisma/client` is **absent**.
2. **The generated client is never produced:** `npm ci` here runs with `ignore-scripts`, so the `postinstall` that would run `prisma generate` never runs. `node_modules/.prisma` is absent.
3. **Schema and package sit in different** `node_modules` **roots.** Schema: `Blockchain/Dev/prisma/schema.prisma`. Client: `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/node_modules`. From `services/originate`, `prisma generate --schema ../../prisma/schema.prisma` fails with `Error: Could not resolve @prisma/client` — generate resolves the client relative to the **schema's** directory. From `Blockchain/Dev` it fails earlier: `sh: prisma: command not found`.
4. **Node resolves** `@prisma/client` **fine** from `services/originate`. So this is generate's resolution rule meeting the layout, not a broken install.

## Why it matters now

`MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` picks the branch: **false** (the local-compose default) takes the **Prisma** branch of `withTenant`; **true** takes the pg-pool branch. So every `withTenant` integration cell is unrunnable in the **local default** mode. It stayed invisible because the existing integration suites (`ks597*`) use raw `pg` clients and never call `withTenant`.

**Not one bad tree:** a second, independently created worktree also has no generated client, and its suite passed only because it never touches `withTenant`.

## NOT claimed

Nothing about deployed environments — service images are built by their own Dockerfiles and were not examined. No claim any runtime is affected. This is about running these tests in a developer or agent worktree.

## Fix shapes, not chosen here

1. Make the layout resolvable — declare `@prisma/client` at the `Blockchain/Dev` root, or set an explicit generator `output`.
2. Add a discoverable `generate` script, rather than relying on a `postinstall` that `ignore-scripts` disables.
3. Regardless of 1/2: make `getPrismaClient()` fail with a sentence naming the cause and the command, as `run-shell-suites.sh` does for a missing `packages/shared` build. That is the difference between a module error and a diagnosis.

## Board search before filing (1294 issues incl. archived, literal match on titles, descriptions and comments)

* `.prisma/client` -> 1 total / 0 open \[\]
* `prisma generate` -> 3 / 1 \['KS-763'\] · `Could not resolve @prisma/client` -> 0 / 0
* `ignore-scripts` -> 16 / 7 \['KS-1290', 'KS-1216', 'KS-918', 'KS-763', 'KS-729', 'KS-664', 'KS-530'\] · `@prisma/client` -> 9 / 1 \['KS-664'\]
* Control, a nonsense token -> **0**. So the search discriminates.

## Provenance

Found running #1239 KS-1263's shipped cells against a disposable PostgreSQL built from `docker/init` + `scripts/run-migrations.sh`. Filed on the coordinator's ruling (b): round 2 ships proven in MODE T with MODE F a named residual, and this gap gets its own ticket rather than repo-tooling work inside a test PR.

KS-1284.desc:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/transaction.ts:107` attaches every anchor's metadata with `txBuilder.add_json_metadatum_with_schema(label, JSON.stringify(metadataPayload), CSL.MetadataJsonSchema.BasicConversions)`. With the lockfile-pinned `@emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib-nodejs` **15.0.3** (`Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json`), that call **throws for ANY string value over 64 bytes**: `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64`. This is Cardano's own metadata rule (text strings and byte strings in transaction metadata are capped at 64 bytes each), surfaced by CSL at tx build.

**Consequence for KS-721:** the `identityCommitment` accepted since 2026-08-31 (#763, `436f37bed`) has the form `<label>.v<N>:<64 lowercase hex>`, whose regex minimum is **69 bytes** (`a.v1:` + 64). Platform-S's real value (`identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>`) is **90 bytes**. So every non-mock anchor carrying a commitment would fail at `buildAnchorTransaction` before submission — **the field has never been anchorable on a real chain through this code.** Nothing has hit it yet because: (a) the mock branch (`cardano/index.ts:234-238`) hands `JSON.stringify(payload)` to the mock provider and never touches CSL, which is why KS-721 could only be proven in mock mode ("no chain write was possible", history.md); (b) S ships `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity = false` (PS-870), so S has never sent the field; (c) K's own originate→anchoring hops forward only `documentId`/`contentHash`/`network`. Every real preview anchor confirmed to date is all-short (64-hex hash, doc ids, ISO timestamps, verbs), so the demo's 194 confirmed anchors are unaffected.

**Consequence for KS-1175:** `actorDid`/`orgDid` (≤512 bytes) inherit the same limit. The KS-1175 PR fixes this at the tx-build boundary (see below) and `Refs` this ticket; this ticket is filed separately because it is a separate fix (KS-721's latent defect), per the one-ticket-per-fix rule.

## Measurement (2026-09-20, Seat A 15th, at develop `dc061f2bb6dff9180a0724b1d1d5c50b9a0173fa`)

Instrument: `5_Project_History/2026-09-20_seatA-15th/boot/csl_probe.cjs` — pure wasm against the worktree's hoisted CSL 15.0.3; no chain, no port, no wallet. Both directions:

| input | `encode_json_str_to_metadatum(…, BasicConversions)` |
| -- | -- |
| 64-char string | OK (78 bytes) |
| 65-char string | THROWS `Max metadata string too long: 65, max = 64` |
| minimal KS-721 commitment `a.v1:<64 hex>` (69) | THROWS |
| S's `identity-commitment-l2.v1:<64 hex>` (90) | THROWS |
| 512-char `did:web:…` | THROWS |
| array of 2 × 45-char strings | OK (107 bytes) |
| an all-short realistic anchor payload (hash/documentType/occurredAt/timestamps) | OK (305 bytes) |

And through the exact call `transaction.ts:107` makes — a `TransactionBuilder` built from fabricated protocol params: 69-byte commitment THROWS, 64-byte string OK. Wednesday reproduced the same table independently at 22:00 AEST (her `csl_probe2.js`).

`transaction.ts:107` is the **single** attach point for BOTH labels (674 single, 675 batch); `index.ts:744` (`json_metadata.secuura` off Blockfrost) is the single chain reader. No other encoder/decoder exists under `services/anchoring/src` (grep, non-test).

## Fix (shipping in the KS-1175 PR, as its own named test block)

A pure helper `services/anchoring/src/cardano/cardanoMetadatum.ts`: `toCardanoMetadatum(payload)` replaces any string > 64 UTF-8 bytes with an ARRAY of ≤64-byte chunks split on character boundaries (byte count, never `.length`); `fromCardanoMetadatum(md)` joins an all-string array back. Applied ONLY at `transaction.ts:106` and at the chain read `index.ts:744` (before the hash compare). `metadata_payload` in the DB and `buildFlatAnchorMetadataPayload`'s output stay in the logical (unchunked) form. Controls: an all-short payload encodes to a `to_bytes()`-identical metadatum with and without the helper (proves a no-op for every anchor made to date); `from(to(x))` deep-equals `x`; a multibyte string splits with no chunk over 64 BYTES. Consequence to document: an independent chain reader (Cardanoscan / raw Blockfrost) sees a long value as an array — the standard Cardano convention for >64-byte metadata strings.

## Not in scope here

A CSL version bump (it changes the on-chain encoder for every anchor — its own ticket if ever). KS-721 itself stays archived (`Deployed to UAT`); this ticket `Refs KS-721`.

## Checklist

- [ ] helper + tests merged (KS-1175 PR)
- [ ] §5f live sweep on kintsugi: one real preview anchor carrying a ≥69-byte commitment confirms and reads back joined on `GET /api/anchors/verify/:hash` (chain source) — Kam's deploy/anchor step, not the PR's

KS-1269.desc:
## Finding

`POST /api/status/0/revoke` with body `{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": {}}` answered **HTTP 200** `{"statusListId":"0","credentialId":"example-credentialId","revoked":true,"revokedAt":"2026-09-18T11:28:19.243Z"}` — the revoke side effect ran with an `index` that is an **object**, where the published schema declares an integer.

Surfaced by `by_design_input_tolerance_guard` ([KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)) in the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) after-sweep — `full-2026-09-18T11-19-19Z-slot1`, Schemathesis 4.27.2, coverage phase, head `52df64f84`, slot 1. The guard's own message: *"accepted a schema-violating request with HTTP 200, and the violation is NOT the one ruled by-design for this operation (*[KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) */* [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)*)."* That is the guard doing exactly what it was built for: the [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the) ruling tolerates **only** `index` below the declared `minimum` on this operation; a wrong-typed `index` is a different violation and must still be rejected.

Two things make this worse than "permissive input":

* The handler **performed the revoke** and reported `revoked: true` for an index it cannot have resolved as an integer — compare [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the)'s note that `GET /api/status/{id}/check/{index}` silently coerces a float to a different index. Which entry (if any) was actually flipped is unknown from the response.
* It is a **write** on a revocation status list, i.e. a legally significant record.

## Why it appeared now

Schemathesis 4.27.2 generates a different coverage-phase case set for this op (32 → 58 cases; `POST /api/status/{id}/unrevoke` 50 → 68) — the `allOf`/`additionalProperties` and example-completion fixes in that release. The platform behaviour is not new; the question had not been asked in this shape before. [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data)'s original repro set only exercised `index: -1`.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"<ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD>"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"credentialId": "example-credentialId", "index": {}}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/status/0/revoke
```

Expected **400/422**. Actual **200** with `revoked: true`.

Artefacts: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/full-2026-09-18T11-19-19Z-slot1/` (NDJSON `ScenarioFinished` for `POST /api/status/{id}/revoke`, check `by_design_input_tolerance_guard`).

## Fix direction

Validate `index` as an integer at the handler boundary (the Zod schema the spec is generated from already declares it) and refuse with a mapped 4xx before any list mutation. Per [KS-662](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-662/negative-data-rejection-scope-the-by-design-input-tolerance-to-the), do **not** widen the harness exception — the guard is the arbiter; if the ruling is to be widened, that is a deliberate decision on this ticket, not a config edit.

Same class as [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) (Done, by-design for `index < minimum` only). Found by the [KS-1268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1268/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4271-4272-retargeted-from-4273-whose) bump sweep, 2026-09-18.

KS-1262.desc:
## BLUF

**A caller whose** `userId` **is** `platform-settings` **can replace the platform-wide** `platform-settings` **record through the per-user notification-settings endpoint, bypassing** `requireAdmin` **and KS-1230's validation.** Measured with a test token. **Production refuses test tokens. Whether kintsugi or demo accept them is UNMEASURED.**

## Recommendation

Give per-user notification settings their own key space (for example `notif:user:<userId>`), or refuse reserved ids at that writer. Regression cell: a role-`user` principal whose `sub` is `platform-settings` PUTs `/api/settings/notifications`, and `platform-settings` is untouched.

## Detail

* **Two writers, one namespace.** Both write through `setNotificationSettings(key, data)` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:680`), which stores `notif:<key>`:
  * `PUT /api/admin/settings` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1123`, `requireAdmin`) writes `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', merged)` (`:1141`);
  * `PUT /api/settings/notifications` (`:1478`, `authenticateToken(true)`, no role gate) writes `setNotificationSettings(userId, body)` (`:1489`).
* **Measured by the #1045 batch gate** (`evidence/probe1045d.out`). The setup: the real `authenticateToken` and `parseTestToken`, with `configureAuth({enableTestTokens:true})`.
  * A role-`user` test token with `sub: "platform-settings"` PUT `/api/settings/notifications`. It got **200, and** `platform-settings` **was replaced** (with a malformed allow-list, or with an object container).
  * The same principal gets **403** at the admin door.
  * Control: `sub: "someone-else"` writes its own key, and platform-settings is untouched.
  * Control: `NODE_ENV=production` gives **401** (test tokens refused, `auth.ts:118-126`).
  * develop = head (pre-existing).
* **What it breaks:** the connector allow-list that KS-1204 and KS-1230 enforce can be replaced by anyone who can hold that `userId`. It can fail open, or lock every connector out. The rest of the platform settings are overwritten with it.
* **Severity (the gate):** Major where test tokens are enabled (dev/test with `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`; the compose default is false). Minor otherwise.
  * In production the attack needs a real JWT whose `userId` is `platform-settings`. That is READ only; nothing was measured.
  * Whether kintsugi or demo run with test tokens enabled is **UNMEASURED**. KS-623 records that the auth service's test-token guard fails OPEN on an unset `NODE_ENV`.
* Line references are at develop `52df64f84`.
* Found by the batch gate `/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-batch1042-1045-tier1-r1/report.md` (finding N45-2), on the #1045 / KS-1230 sibling-writer census.
* Refs KS-1230. Related: KS-1231 (the `integrations` container fails open), KS-1256 (the allow-list fails open on a Redis close), KS-623 (the test-token env guard).

KS-1256.desc:
**From the #1038 / KS-1233 batch gate, finding N38-1: Major, pre-existing. Not #1038's regression.**

## What's wrong

KS-1233 (#1038, merged `e51686bed`) stops `platform-settings` expiring on a TTL. But a **missing** key is still read as "no restriction". The allow-list therefore still **fails open** on every other way the key can go missing or unreadable:

* a runtime Redis close or error (the gate's row R6, measured over a stateful fake);
* a read error swallowed by a bare `catch {}`;
* LRU eviction of the key.

In each case every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

## Why it matters

It is the same fail-open class KS-1233 fixed for the TTL trigger. A connector allow-list should fail **closed** when the configuration cannot be read.

## What to do

Make the reader fail closed. A missing or unreadable `platform-settings` should refuse restricted connector operations (or fall back to a persisted source), not grant everything. Add cells for the close, error and eviction paths. Check the other readers in the gate's reader census (section C) for the same class.

KS-1244.desc:
Sending **two** `x-api-key` **headers** — in either order — **defeats key authentication**.

## Mechanism

Node joins the repeated header's values into one string; the joined string fails key validation; the request then **falls through to the anonymous / JWT principal**, which on an optional mount answers **200**.

## Measured

Identical at the #1034 head and at develop `34cdcfb26`, so it is **pre-existing** and not #1034's. The gate listed it as a ticket candidate without assigning a severity; filed here as High because it is an authentication-bypass shape.

This is **KS-736 / KS-1207 territory** — whoever picks it up should read those first, since the fall-through-to-anonymous pattern is the same one they cover.

## What to do

Reject a repeated `x-api-key` outright rather than validating the joined value, and make the failure a refusal rather than a fall-through.

---

KS-1240.desc:
**The sharpest of the four candidates the gate surfaced, and the only one that is request-reachable today.**

The api-gateway's connector-token exchange / key-validate `fetch` carries **no timeout**. A slow or non-answering upstream turns into a gateway request with no bound on how long it hangs, while the process carries on serving everything else.

## Measured on BOTH trees (head and develop) — so it is pre-existing

* an exchange that **never answers** → the request hangs;
* an exchange whose body arrives **2.5 s late** → the request hangs for that long.

Graded **Major**. Request-reachable, unlike T-1.

## What to do

Give the fetch an explicit timeout (AbortSignal / `AbortController`) and decide the refusal shape — a 503 on timeout is consistent with how the connector branch already answers a refused exchange.

---

KS-1233.desc:
## BLUF

**In Redis mode the gateway stores platform-settings with a 24 h TTL, and nothing refreshes it.** So, by reading the code: 24 h after the last admin settings write, every connector allow-list disappears and every restricted connector becomes unrestricted.

* **Major, pending measurement.** This is READ ONLY: no Redis was run.
* The same fail-open class as the container fail-open ticket filed alongside it.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-A).

## Recommendation

An escalation candidate (the gate's grading). Not built here.

1. **Measure first**, read-only, in a non-production gateway running in Redis mode: store an allow-list, `EXPIRE` the key (or wait out the TTL), then create as the restricted connector. The code reading predicts 201.
2. **If confirmed**, the owner decides the fix. Either platform-settings must not expire (no TTL, or a refresh), or a missing platform-settings must not read as "no restriction" for a connector that had one. It may be sequenced with the container fail-open read-side fix.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**:**
  * `services/api-gateway/src/services/redis.ts:27`: `privacy: 86400` (24 hours);
  * `redis.ts:680-687`: `setNotificationSettings` writes `notif:<key>` with `setex(…, TTL.privacy, …)` when Redis is available;
  * after expiry, `getNotificationSettings('platform-settings')` returns null, and `routes/verification.ts:1214-1216` turns that into `integrations []`, which means no restriction;
  * the only `setNotificationSettings('platform-settings', …)` call is `routes/admin.ts:1127` (`PUT /api/admin/settings`), so nothing re-writes the key.
* **Why local runs never show it:** the in-memory fallback (no Redis) is a Map with no TTL.
* **It also affects KS-1204's migration-residual reading.** A key past its TTL reads as absent, which means "no restriction stored anywhere", not "no malformed list". So a reading must quote the key's TTL beside the shapes.
* **Not measured:** Redis mode was not run (KS-535).
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `TTL.privacy`: 0 of 114 scanned.
  * `setNotificationSettings`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `platform-settings`: 3 (KS-1230, KS-1176, KS-37); none covers expiry.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-A: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1204.

KS-1231.desc:
## BLUF

**A connector restricted by a document-type allow-list becomes UNRESTRICTED whenever the stored platform-settings** `integrations` **container is not a clean array of object entries. One ordinary save on the admin portal's Settings page produces exactly such a container.**

* Major, pre-existing: the same at develop before PR #1035, at #1035's head and on the merged tree.
* It widens authorisation through the product's own UI, and it is silent: `GET /api/connector/info` then tells the connector `[]`.
* Found by the #1035 tier-1 QA gate (finding N-1, D1). Filed as its own ticket, not folded into KS-1230, per Wednesday's ruling.

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here. An escalation candidate (the gate's grading).

* **Read side, fail closed, in both readers:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1212-1219` (the create path) and `services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:45-52` (the info reader). For the calling connector, any of these should refuse instead of reading as no restriction:
  * a non-array `integrations`;
  * a non-object entry;
  * a duplicate id;
  * a non-object `config`.
* **Portal:** `frontend/admin/src/pages/Settings.tsx` must not regroup `integrations`, or any array, through `key.split('.')`. It flattens every category into `category.key` form values on load (`:37-42`) and splits them back on save (`:66`), which turns an array into `{"0": entry}`.
* **Regression cells:** each container shape below × {typed, untyped} → 403. A Settings-save round trip keeps `integrations` an array.

## Detail

* **Repro** (measured at runtime by the gate: the real route, both boots):
  1. As SYSTEM_ADMIN, `PUT /api/admin/settings` with `integrations: [{ id: "c1", config: { allowedDocumentTypes: ["SSD_DOCUMENT"] } }]` and a `general.platformName`.
  2. Connector `c1` sends `POST /api/documents` with `documentType: "DOCUMENT"` → 403.
  3. On the admin portal Settings page, change the platform name and save. The PUT body carries `integrations` as `{"0": {...}}`. The portal transform was PROBED by emulation and confirmed by reading `Settings.tsx`; no browser was driven.
  4. The same create → **201, forwarded to originate**.
* **Stored containers measured fail-open.** Each gives typed `DOCUMENT` → 201 forwarded, and info tells `[]`:
  * `{"0": entry}`;
  * `[null, entry]` (`.find` throws on `null.id`);
  * `[{id, config: {}}, entry]` (duplicate id, first wins);
  * `[{id, config: "SSD_DOCUMENT"}]`;
  * `"x"` (`.find` is not a function);
  * `null`.
  * Control: `[entry]` → 403.
* **Mechanism:** the container parse sits inside `try { … } catch {}`. A throw or a miss leaves `connectorConfig = {}`, which reads as no restriction. The same parse is in the info reader.
* **Related:**
  * KS-1204: PR #1035 made the leaf value fail closed, but the container above it still fails open;
  * KS-1230: write-side validation of the value, a different defect;
  * the 24 h platform-settings TTL expiry, the same fail-open class, filed separately.
* **Searched before filing:** Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term (2026-09-17 \~16:00Z):
  * `Settings.tsx`: 0 of 118 scanned.
  * `connectorConfig`: 0, but the fuzzy search returned only 1 result, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `integrations`: 15, none about the container parse (the security-review umbrellas KS-485, KS-488 and KS-492, harness tickets and m365 redirect tickets).
  * `platform-settings`: 3. KS-1230 (write-side validation of the allow-list value), KS-1176 (comments) and KS-37 (admin SPA tests); none covers the container.
* **Evidence:** #1035 gate report, finding N-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1204-1035-4b1fb0621-tier1-r1/report.md`. Line references re-read at develop `34cdcfb26`.
* Refs KS-1204.

KS-1223.desc:
## BLUF

**A client-sent** `x-wallet-address` **reaches the upstreams, and the referral service trusts it.** The header is outside the gateway's edge strip pattern (`services/api-gateway/src/utils/trustHeaders.ts`), so it is forwarded on every proxied route. `services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55` then uses it as the wallet address when the authenticated principal has none, directly under a comment saying direct header reads are spoofable. Pre-existing. Found by the tier-1 gate on PR #1028 (KS-744) as finding N-3. **Reachability and severity are UNMEASURED**, and so is the priority set here: the referral mount was not probed.

## Recommendation

Owners measure it, then decide:

1. probe `POST /api/referrals/generate` through the real gateway with a token that carries no `walletAddress` plus a client `x-wallet-address`, and read what the wallet address on a referral code drives;
2. if reachable, drop the header fallback (read the wallet from the authenticated principal only) and/or add `x-wallet-address` to the edge strip, with a cell proving a client value never reaches the handler.

## Detail

* **Measured at runtime by the gate** at the gateway on 3 mount kinds: a client `x-wallet-address` is forwarded on every forwarded http-proxy cell, on develop `19f1e5475`, the PR head and the merged tree (624 cells at develop, 714 at head; the 90 extra are exactly the cells KS-744's fix now forwards).
* **Read at develop** `0a2b1603f`**:**
  * `referrals.ts:51-55`: the comment reads "Pen-test F-04: read from authenticated req.user … NOT from raw headers. Direct header reads are spoofable.", and the next line is `const walletAddress = (authUser?.walletAddress as string) || (req.headers['x-wallet-address'] as string);`.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1286` hand-forwards a client `x-wallet-address` onward.
* **Not measured:** the referral mount itself; whether any real token lacks `walletAddress`; what a referral code's wallet address controls.
* **Searched before filing** (Linear, literal, archived included): `x-wallet-address` (0); `referrals.ts` (1: KS-202, input trimming, Done). No ticket covers this.
* **Related:** KS-744 (the gate that found it).

## Status: NOT fixed. Reachability UNMEASURED. Priority set to Medium (3) pending that measurement (Seat J 4th, L12, 2026-10-13; Wednesday's ruling 2026-10-12 14:39Z).

**BLUF:** a client-supplied `x-wallet-address` header still decides the referrer wallet in the code on develop and in the running code. Both linked PRs only pin that behaviour in tests. Whether a request can actually reach the route with the header intact has not been measured.

- **Linked PRs #1111 and #1125** are test-only characterisation pins. In their own words, whether a caller-supplied header should decide the wallet at all is this ticket's question for the owners.
- **Code, read not driven:** `TRUST_HEADER_PATTERN` has no wallet entry; `referrals.ts:55` still reads `authUser.walletAddress || req.headers['x-wallet-address']`. The compiled `referrals.js` and `trustHeaders.js` in the running containers hash equal to a local build of develop.
- **What the value drives:** it is stored as `svc_referral_codes.owner_wallet_address` (`referralService.ts:62-65`, `:353`) and read back as `referrerWallet` at `:455-456`. The reward claim takes its own `walletAddress` from the request BODY (`rewards.ts:21`, `:111`). I did not trace the consumer at `:455`.
- **Next:** after the #1497 fix round, measure in-process through the gateway's `trustHeaders` on develop (a request carrying `x-wallet-address` through the real middleware chain into the referral route, no live box). If reachable, raise to High and tell Wednesday: it then needs an owner decision (Kam) on whether a header may decide the wallet at all.
- **Priority:** it already read Medium (3) when I checked on 2026-10-13, so no change was needed.

## MEASURED: it IS reachable. Priority raised to High (2). It needs an owner decision (Kam): may a request header decide the wallet at all?

**BLUF.** On develop `425ad3e00ae4`, a verified access token with NO `walletAddress` claim, plus a client `x-wallet-address`, sent through the REAL gateway to `POST /api/referrals/generate`, produces a referral code whose `owner_wallet_address` is the client's header value. Every token the auth service mints lacks that claim, so the header is the ONLY source of the wallet today, not a rare fallback. What the stored value drives, measured: ONLY the `WALLET_COLLISION` fraud flag on a later apply. It does not drive a payout.

**How it was measured (in-process, no live box; Seat J 4th, 2026-10-13).** One scratch vitest file (not committed) boots the real gateway app (`../index`: the edge strip, the auth, the proxy routes) in front of the real referral route stack (`express.json`, the shared `authenticate()` doing a real RS256 verify, `routes/referrals.ts`, the real `referralService` and `fraudDetection`) over a throwaway Postgres 15 (the referral tables from `docker/init`). Tokens carry exactly the claim set `generateAccessToken` signs. File and output: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-4th/evidence/ks1223/`.

**Results**
- **Forwarded:** the referral upstream received `x-wallet-address: addr_header_one`. Control that the strip works: a client `x-user-id: spoofed-user` reached the upstream as the token's own userId.
- **Stored:** 201, and the code row's `owner_wallet_address` = `addr_header_one`. Without the header: null. With a token that DOES carry a `walletAddress` claim and a different header: the claim wins (`addr_claim`), as the existing pin says.
- **Unauthenticated:** the same request without a token: 401, never reaches the handler.
- **What the stored wallet drives:** applying the code with a referred wallet equal to the stored one: the referral is `INVALID`, `fraud_check_passed` false, `fraud_flags = ["WALLET_COLLISION"]`. Control, same referred wallet on a code created WITHOUT the header: `PENDING`, flags `[]` (the check is skipped when the referrer wallet is absent). A header wallet that differs from the referred wallet: `PENDING`, flags `[]`.

**Reading (mine, from the code and the numbers).**
- The only consumer of `ownerWalletAddress` is the fraud context's `referrerWallet`. Rewards are claimed to the wallet in the CLAIM body (`rewards.ts:21`, `:111`), so the header does not redirect a payout.
- Evasion gain for a fraudster: none beyond omitting the wallet, because an absent referrer wallet already skips the check (measured).
- Griefing: a header can attribute a code to another person's wallet; if that person then applies that code with that wallet, their referral is flagged. Narrow.
- The control the fallback was meant to feed cannot fire from the authenticated principal today: no token carries the claim (`walletAddress` is a field of the `User` row; `generateAccessToken` builds the claims explicitly without it, and wallet login, OAuth and email login all call `generateTokenPair`). It fires only when a client volunteers the header. No client in this repo sends it and the published spec does not mention it (0 hits).

**Decision for the owners (Kam):** where should a referrer's wallet come from? Dropping the header fallback is a one-line change, but it makes the wallet-collision check dead for every code, so the real fix is a trustworthy source (the user's linked wallet from the `User` row, or the wallet from a verified wallet login) read by the referral service, not a header. Until decided, the existing pin tests (`ks1223-wallet-header-fallback`, `ks1223-wallet-forwarded-to-originate`) characterise today's behaviour.

**Not measured:** a deployed environment or whatever sits in front of the gateway in production (an ingress or WAF that might strip unknown headers); Platform S or any other external client that may send the header on purpose; what happens to the `fraud_flags` of codes created before this ticket; the `/api/documents` create path (`verification.ts:1382`) beyond the existing pin.

KS-1533.desc:
## BLUF

**In** `services/security`**, the API-key mint is bounded by TENANT only. An** `ORG_ADMIN` **or** `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of organisation A can mint a key that carries organisation B's** `organizationId`**, and any** `connectorId`**, inside the same tenant.** KS-764 put an organisation arm on **revoke**; the **mint** never got one. Because the connector-erasure path in KS-695 trusts the key row it is called with, that minted key erases B.

**This must land before KS-695 deploys** — same status as KS-1508. Merging KS-695 does not deploy it, so the harm is after deploy, and the data destroyed (titles, descriptions, an organisation name) is another organisation's and the erasure is irreversible.

Found by the round 4 Opus gate on PR #1497 (verdict sha256/16 `df3bc694b6b41094`, section M-1). **The security-service half below is the gate's reading of the code, which I re-read at source myself; the originate half is the gate's measurement on real Postgres. Neither the mint nor the gateway half has been measured at runtime — that is the first task here.**

## The two paths

**Path 1 — a key for another organisation.**

* `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49` — `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN` are in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`.
* `provisioningPolicy.ts:95-98` — `decideMint` returns `{allow: true, via: 'admin'}` **at once** for any of those roles, before any tenancy or organisation question.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:477-491` — the body's `organizationId` and `connectorId` are free strings.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:1017` — the route calls `decideTenantAccess((req as any).user, tenantId)` **without** the third `organisationScope` argument.
* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:161-164` says that arm is engaged *"ONLY when the caller supplies* `organisationScope`*, so the two existing callers (KS-742's list and mint) keep exactly today's behaviour"*. That was deliberate in KS-764 and is exactly the gap.
* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1189-1192` — `/api/security` is mounted behind `authenticateToken(true)` only, so the gateway adds no organisation check.

**Measured by the gate on the originate side (cell P8, real Postgres, both modes):** a key row for org B carrying a forged `connector_id` — which is what the mint above writes — gives `200 completed documentsBlanked:1`, B's name and document `[erased]`, and B's own provisioned key still active.

**Path 2 — a key for A's own organisation carrying B's connector id.**

* `svc_api_keys.connector_id` has **no uniqueness constraint** (the gate read the live indexes: pkey, org, prefix, tenant only).
* The erasure matches `versionedById = 'connector:' + connectorId` **by value**.
* **Measured by the gate (cell P6, both modes):** two organisations whose keys share one `connector_id`; A erases and gets `200 documentsBlanked:4`, taking B's unissued connector root and B's connector derivatives.
* Not hypothetical: `register-connector` writes `connectorId: platform-s:${externalRef}` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:702`), so the id is a predictable function of a value an org admin can read, and the tenant metering key already uses a constant `platform-s` id (`tenant-provisioning/src/meteringKey.ts:56`).

**Path 2 is not closed by the organisation arm alone.** Both arms are needed.

## What this ticket asks for

1. **The organisation arm of the mint.** An organisation-scoped admin may mint only for its own organisation. The shape already exists — pass `organisationScope` at `index.ts:1017` as the revoke path does at `keyRevokePolicy.ts:243` — and `decideMint`'s early return for `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` must stop short-circuiting past it. Platform roles keep their current reach.
2. **The connector-id binding.** A connector id belongs to exactly one organisation; a mint naming one already bound to another organisation in the same tenant is refused. The org-less tenant metering key must keep working.
3. **It lands before KS-695 deploys.** Tracked like KS-1508.

## Acceptance

A mint request from an `ORG_ADMIN`/`ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A naming organisation B, **or** naming a `connectorId` already bound to B, is refused **on the running service over real HTTP** — not only in a unit file — with the caller's own organisation unaffected, and a control proving the same admin may still mint for its own organisation.

## Dedupe before filing

Literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description across Secuura-PK, **archived included**: `organisationScope` **0**, `organizationScope` **0**, `connector_id has no unique` **0**, `provisioningPolicy` 2 (KS-742 tenancy, KS-835 OAuth consent), `decideMint` 2 (KS-742, KS-486), `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` 5 (KS-742, KS-643, KS-642, KS-486, KS-1514 — all either the tenant boundary or a response-shape issue), `ORG_ADMIN` 33 (so the scan can see). **The nearest neighbours are the tenant boundary (KS-742) and the revoke-only organisation arm (KS-764, Done); neither covers the mint's organisation arm or the connector-id binding.** KS-1107 is the same class on a different surface (`POST /api/auth/register` accepting a client-supplied `organizationId`) and is not this.

## Not measured, and whose it is

Counts of existing keys that already share a `connector_id` across organisations on Kintsugi are **not** measured here — that is the J lane's to run, per Wednesday. Nothing in this ticket was run against a live box.

Filed by Seat V 5th from the PR #1497 round 4 Opus gate, 2026-10-12.

KS-1508.desc:
## BLUF

`metadata.versionedById` is meant to be set by the server (`user.id`), but any writer can set it, and KS-695 part (ii) now uses it to decide which documents an organisation's erasure irreversibly blanks. Reserve it as a server-set key.

## Recommendation

Strip `versionedById` from caller-supplied `data` on create, and make the three version paths ignore a caller's value, so it can only come from `user.id`. Review the neighbouring keys that share the same spread (`versionAction`, `versionedAt`, `parentDocumentId`) in the same change.

## Detail (read by me in the tree at develop `8d34fbf0890a`, 2026-10-12)

* **Create:** `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:600` builds `data` as `{ ...rawData, ... }` from the request. `stripReservedMetadataKeys` (`repositories/documentRepo.ts:158`) removes only `blockchain`, `signatures` and `walletAddress`, so a caller-supplied `versionedById` is stored as metadata.
* **/version, /sign-cert, /sign-wallet:** `documents.ts:2106`, `:2840` and `:3034` set `versionedById: user.id` and then spread the caller's `...metadata` AFTER it, so the caller's value wins.
* **Why it matters now:** the Opus gate on PR #1497 reproduced it through the real create route and the real erase route as `secuura_app`: organisation A's connector created a document with `data.versionedById = "connector:platform-s:<B's GUID>"` (201), B's erase answered `completed`, and A's title read `[erased]` (irreversible). Gate verdict: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1497/verdict.md`, finding M1. PR #1497 bounds the selector by the issuer, which stops that outcome, but that is a seatbelt on one consumer; this ticket is the root.
* The connector id is `platform-s:<Organisation GUID>`, which is the externalRef, so it is knowable.

## Done when

- [ ] A caller-supplied `versionedById` is not stored by create and is overridden by `user.id` on the three version paths; one red-first cell per route (four routes, four claims).
- [ ] Platform S does not rely on sending it (confirm with Stuart; a round-trip of a K document's `data` into a new create must not carry it).
- [ ] Measured: how many existing documents carry a `versionedById` that is not the creating connector's (a read-only count), and a recorded decision on them.

## Sequencing (Wednesday's ruling, 2026-10-12, after the second Opus gate on #1497)

**This ticket must LAND BEFORE KS-695 DEPLOYS.** With PR #1497's selector bounded by the issuer, a NULL-issuer document can still be claimed for another organisation by any writer through `versionedById` (a create without `organizationUuid`, or any `/version`, whose metadata is spread after `versionedById` and whose source has no organisation check), so the erasure's reach is only as trustworthy as this field. The gate's evidence: A's `/version` of A's own document with `metadata.versionedById` = B's connector is blanked by B's erasure and is not reached by A's.

## Not claimed

That any caller has done this. Exploiting it needs organisation A's own writer to plant B's id (a bug in a round-trip, or on purpose); B cannot do it alone. Raised by the Opus gate on #1497; filed by Seat J 3rd on Wednesday's instruction.

KS-1503.desc:
## BLUF

**Action (owner: the K lane): pin the front door's fall-through for an unverifiable Bearer, then decide three smaller gaps.** The connector-Bearer guard from PR 1495 (KS-1470) is correct today. But nothing tests what it does with a token that does NOT verify: if its `catch` block ever rethrows, every expired, forged, `alg:none` or malformed Bearer answers **500 on every route**, and all 1060 tests stay green. The Opus gate proved it with its own mutation (G10) on the merged head.

## Recommendation

1. **Do now (one or two lines):** in cell J of `ks1470-a-connector-bearer-is-refused-before-every-mount.test.ts`, add a POSITIVE assertion that a forged type:connector token reaches the recording upstream on the sig-json mount (or gets `authenticateToken`'s `Invalid or expired token` 401 on an `authenticateToken` mount), and add an expired-token case. Show the new assertion red under the gate's G10 mutation (the guard's `catch` rethrows) and restore byte-identical.
2. **Decide (small):** Notes 2, 3 and 5 below. Note 3 is the cheapest and removes a coupling: make the guard's Bearer scheme match case-insensitive. The gate showed it stays green (G14).

## Detail

Source: the Opus gate on PR 1495, head `89c1b9388638`, verdict `GO WITH NOTE`, 0 Major; verdict file sha256/16 `72ea63d45058c59d` (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1495/verdict.md`).

**Minor 1 (the action above).** Cell J asserts only "not the connector refusal", so it passes whether the unverifiable token is forwarded, answered 401, or answered 500. Under G10 the gate's probe file showed altered-signature, expired, `alg:none` and double-space Bearers all answering 500. Not a product bug today; a guard on a future edit.

**Note 2: audit attribution of a refusal.** The refusal is audited for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE on `/api/*`, but the row has `user_id` null and the platform default tenant; the connector id and tenant exist only in the `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER_REFUSED` warning, because `audit.ts` reads `req.user`, which this path never sets. GET refusals are never audited (a property of the audit middleware). KS-1198's existing refusals behave the same. Correlate on `requestId` if needed. Decide: accept, or attribute the row.

**Note 3: the guard and the upstreams agree on the Bearer scheme only by convention.** The guard uses the literal `startsWith('Bearer ')` plus `split(' ')[1]`, as every upstream does today, so `bearer x` is "no credential" on both sides. If an upstream ever adopts case-insensitive schemes (RFC 7235), the guard needs the same change. A case-insensitive guard costs nothing now (G14).

**Note 5: a cold JWKS cache.** From `packages/shared/src/crypto/jwks.ts`: an unknown-kid refetch is limited to once per 10 s, and concurrent fetches collapse onto one in-flight fetch with a 3 s timeout. That holds on a warm cache. On a COLD cache (`keyCache.size === 0`: JWKS configured but unreachable or empty) the cooldown is bypassed, so each sequential Bearer request starts a fetch and can wait up to 3 s. This is pre-existing in `verifyJwtRs256`; PR 1495 extends it to routes that never verified before (`/health`, docs, public verify, `/api/auth/*`). Bounded at one outstanding fetch, and not an oracle. Decide whether a cold cache should also honour the cooldown.

**Not ticketed on purpose.** Note 1 (gateway-served routes now answer a connector Bearer with 401) is named in the squash body. Note 4 (a `test_token_` carrying type:connector is not refused when `ENABLE_TEST_TOKENS=true`) matches KS-1198 and is never active in demo or production.

**Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, title and description): `unverifiable`, `fall-through`, `front door`, `rejectConnectorBearer`, `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER`, `case-insensitive scheme`, `cold JWKS`, `JWKS cooldown`, `audit row`, `user_id null`. No duplicate. Nearest: **KS-1471** (the refusal warning logs a mount-relative `req.path` inside `authenticateToken`; after PR 1495 the front door logs the full canonical path, the inner site still logs the mount-relative one). Related, not the same.

Related: KS-1470, KS-1198, KS-1471.

KS-1477.desc:
## BLUF

Gate finding on #1473 (KS-1018 item 3, GO WITH NOTE), residual and **inside the ruling's carve-out**, filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. With a database configured, a verification request filed while `isDbAvailable()` is false lives only in the process-local map, and a read that SUCCEEDS with no row still consults that map. So after the database recovers, the request is still visible to some reads and can be acted on. It is the same hazard class #1473 closes for failed reads, reachable only through a degraded-boot request.

## Recommendation

Small PR after #1473: stop consulting the map when a database is configured and the read succeeded (an empty DB answer is the answer), and make "memory-only" mean "no `DATABASE_URL`", not "the pool is not ready yet". Decide how a request filed during the KS-377 boot window should behave: refuse it with 503 (preferred: nothing is silently kept in a place the next replica cannot see) rather than store it in memory.

## Detail (gate probe on head `2026b2e6d0c8`, `logs/probe_head.txt`)

* `isDbAvailable()` is false both with no `DATABASE_URL` AND during the KS-377 boot window of a configured database, so "no-database mode" in the comments is broader than the name says.
* Effect measured on the head: list answers 200 without the request; a second `POST /me/verification` answers 200, so there are now two PENDING requests (one in memory, one in the database); approving answers 200 and the user's verification level is RAISED.

KS-1470.desc:
## BLUF

KS-1198 (PR #1470) refuses a verified connector JWT (`type: 'connector'`) presented as a Bearer credential, but **only inside** `authenticateToken`. Gateway mounts that do not use it still forward a connector Bearer upstream verbatim. The Opus gate on #1470 measured each of these with one forward carrying the Bearer. **Exploiting it needs a signed connector JWT**, which only the gateway mints from a validated `x-api-key`; nothing client-side holds one. So this is a defence-in-depth gap on the same class as KS-1198, not an open door. Not caused by #1470.

## Recommendation

One fix, one PR, tests first: refuse a signed `type: 'connector'` Bearer at **one earlier point** that every mount passes through (a small middleware mounted before the proxies, or in the shared bearer parse), with the same 401 body and the same structured warning as KS-1198, instead of repeating the check per mount. Pin it with a cell per mount below plus a no-regression control for the gateway's own `x-api-key` flow (which sets `Authorization: Bearer <connector JWT>` itself after the check and must keep working). Rollout as for KS-1198: Kintsugi first, read the `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER_REFUSED` lines for a cycle, then consider demo. **Decision for the owner:** `/api/v2/verification` is public-by-design and originate accepts a connector principal there via `authenticate({required:false})`; refusing the Bearer there is a behaviour change for any connector that calls it that way (none found in this repository).

## Detail

Measured by the gate (each: the stub upstream saw the Bearer):

* `/api/v2/verification` (originate `authenticate({required:false})` accepts it as a connector principal), `/api/verification`, `/api/presentations/verify`, `/api/documents/:id/sig-json`, `/api/auth/*`, `/api/sessions`.
* The gateway-internal `/originate/` mount (`proxy.ts:1201`) forwards `POST /originate/api/documents` to originate `POST /api/documents`, which is KS-1198's original endpoint (measured 200, 1 forward). **Mitigation in place:** nginx closes `/originate/` with a 404 in all three confs (KS-1041) and the api-gateway has no published ports in `docker-compose.production.yml`.
* Reads or intra-cluster only, per the gate.

**Related observation (pre-existing, same file):** the gateway Bearer path accepts `type: 'refresh'` tokens as principals: `authenticateToken` is a denylist on `type`, not an `access`-only allowlist. The gate called it a ticket candidate and out of scope for #1470. Left here so it is tracked; split it out if the owner prefers a ticket of its own.

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1470 (KS-1198), 2026-10-12, defect 2 and its notes (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1470/verdict.md`).
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `CONNECTOR_JWT_AS_BEARER`, `connector JWT`, `authenticateToken`, `type: refresh`, `sig-json`: nothing tracks the unauthenticated mounts.

Related: KS-1198, KS-1205.

KS-1469.desc:
## BLUF

The Opus gate on PR #1466 (KS-1461) measured four gaps on base that the PR did not cause. **I reproduced all three runtime ones in my own harness on develop** `b4a245fba1ca` **(which contains #1466), on the real app over real HTTP, with a recording stub for every upstream.** O1 is the one that matters: **a trailing slash skips the gateway's spec method and auth gate.**

|  | canonical | variant | reading |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **O1** unauthenticated `GET` of a `bearerAuth` operation | `/api/credentials/abc` → **401**, 0 upstream hits | `/api/credentials/abc/` → **200, 1 hit** (also `/API/credentials/abc/`, `/api/v1/credentials/abc/`, `//` at the end) | gate skipped |
| **O1** method gate | `DELETE /api/auth/login` → **405**, 0 hits; `PUT` → 405 | `DELETE /api/auth/login/` → **200, 1 hit**; `PUT` → 200, 1 hit | gate skipped |
| **O3** per-IP verification limiter, cap lowered to 3 | `/api/verification/verify` ×5 → `200,200,200,429,429`; `/api/v2/verification/verify` ×5 → same | `/api/v1/verification/verify` ×5 → `200,200,200,200,200` | not counted |
| **O2** `POST` with a cookie and no token (`NODE_ENV=development`) | `/api/auth/login` → 200; `/api/verification/verify` → 200 | `/api/v1/auth/login` → **403 CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING**; `/api/v1/verification/verify` → **403** | alias not excluded |

Controls in the same run: `/api/zzz-not-in-spec/` → 404 with 0 hits (the gate has no opinion on a path outside the spec, as designed); the canonical v1 requests sent first did not consume the canonical allowance (the canonical five came back `200,200,200,429,429` after them), so the v1 requests really are uncounted rather than counted somewhere else.

**What this does and does not show.** The gateway's own gate is skipped, so the request reaches the upstream. I did **not** measure whether the real upstream or the per-route `authenticateToken` then refuses it (the stub answers 200), so this is a skipped layer, not a measured data exposure. I rate it High on the instruction that O1 is High once reproduced; the per-route check is the only thing standing between the variant and the upstream.

## Recommendation

One ticket, one PR, tests first, built next (ahead of KS-1464 and KS-1457, as the same front-door class):

* **O1** — the spec route regexes are anchored `^…$` while Express routing is non-strict, so `/x/` is routed as `/x`. Let the spec match tolerate one trailing `/`, and pin it with canonical-vs-variant parity cells (GET 401, DELETE 405, in `/api/`, `/API/` and `/api/v1/` spellings) plus the not-in-spec control.
* **O3** — mount the verification limiter on `/api/v1/verification` too. It sits above the `/api/v1/` rewrite in `index.ts`, so the alias is a third spelling it never sees. By code reading (not measured in a production boot) the alias is then counted only by the global limiter, 300 per minute per IP in production, against the dedicated 60: five times looser, not unlimited.
* **O2** — the exclusion list answers for `/api/x` but not for `/api/v1/x`, though the alias is the same route by definition. Make the exclusion check judge the path the alias gives it. **This overlaps KS-1177**, which waits on an owner decision about the v1/v2 verify difference in production; the alias-equivalence reading widens nothing beyond what the canonical spelling already has, but KS-1177's owner should see it.
* **m1** — `csrf.ts` carries a `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` exclusion that nothing pins (deleting it keeps all 936 tests green), and no live route exists at it in v1 or v2. Either a cell that pins it, or drop both verify-batch entries; decide on evidence (does the spec or the proxy declare the route?).

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1466, 2026-10-12 (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1466/verdict.md`, findings O1, O2, O3 and m1; its probe file is in the same folder). Reproduction here is independent of the gate's: my own harness, on the merged tree.
* The gate measured all four on base and on the merged tree identically, so none is caused by #1466 (squash `c78c13d5f2eb6a8c840e7bc75bdb4a054ffd5d7e`).
* Production note for O2: the production-only 307 sends `/api/x` to `/api/v1/x`, so a cookie-bearing browser call to an excluded path may meet the 403 on the re-POST. The gate did not measure this in production and neither did I.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `trailing slash` (KS-519, 548, 861, 1016: none about the gateway gate), `verification limiter`, `api/v1/verification`, `spec auth gate`, `specRouteMap`, `CSRF exclusion`, `verify-batch`. Nearest: **KS-1177** (O2 on the verify family, Backlog), **KS-946** (limiter spelling class: its eight mounts do not name `/api/v1/verification`), **KS-1358** (405 before authentication), **KS-1165** (Done: the v2 CSRF entries).

Related: KS-1461, KS-801, KS-1177, KS-946, KS-1165.

KS-1410.desc:
**BLUF:** **28 handlers across six services put a thrown error's own message straight into a 500 response body, and none of the six files carries a** `NODE_ENV` **guard.** That is a production information leak. KS 1334 and KS 1341 are the same defect, already fixed per-file; this ticket covers the remaining six files as one pass.

Measured by me at develop `f01c1da5717fdcb80a5e1aeeaa8ff9f0f00edd80`. Instrument: a per-line regex `\b(?:err|error)\.message\b` for the message expression, then a separate check that the enclosing statement answers 500. Positive control: `originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts` at the same sha reads `NODE_ENV` **1** time, so a zero below is a measurement and not a broken reader.

## Sites, by file

`api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts` (blob `7945e1b01837`) — **6**: :126 :147 :176 :204 :234 :290
`api-gateway/src/routes/batch.ts` (blob `f2f48dca32e5`) — **3**: :166 :214 :262
`api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts` (blob `d87c04979e2b`) — **1**: :196
`transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (blob `33dd1f110f66`) — **1**: :283
`tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` (blob `82a6f8d4b623`) — **7**: :311 (500 at :330) :353 :392 :422 :483 :544 :564
`mcp-server/src/http-server.ts` (blob `fce4a31793b3`) — **10**: nine `INTERNAL_ERROR` envelopes at :61 :76 :110 :169 :182 :192 :202 :212 :265, plus :134, which is a non-envelope 500 body (`res.status(500).json({ verified: false, error: message })`)

`NODE_ENV` **occurrences in all six files: 0.**

## Four more leaks that are NOT in a 500 and are NOT counted above

Listed so the count is not mistaken for the whole surface:

`api-gateway/src/routes/batch.ts:118` — returned into a per-item result inside a 200
`api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:163` — a **502** body, `Failed to reach security service: ${err.message}`
`mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:104` and `:163` — pushed into a `results` array that is returned with 200

## UNMEASURED

* **Which errors actually reach these handlers in production.** Whether any carries a database string, a file path, an internal hostname or a credential fragment is not measured here, and settling it needs a running system, not a source read.
* No live reach. No request was issued against any of these routes.

## Why one ticket and not six

One test pass, one ticket. The per-file precedents (KS 1334 for adminConfig, KS 1341 for the webhooks routes) each closed a single file because each was found on its own; this set was found in one screening pass over the same class.

## Scope note on the neighbouring tickets, each read before filing

* KS 730 is the **guarded** remainder — its own wording is "71 response-side sites still return `err.message` verbatim **unless** `NODE_ENV === 'production'`". The sites above have **no** guard at all, so they are a different class and do not belong on it.
* KS 1346 is a **logging** defect (a non-Error throw logged as `[object Object]`), not a response-body leak.
* KS 1214 covers the mcp-server `POST /hash` route specifically, as an authentication defect; it overlaps one file here but not this class.

Searched before filing: all 522 open Secuura-PK issues, title and description, by exact substring on each of the six paths and on the message expression. Controls: a must-hit probe for the webhooks routes returned KS 1341, a must-hit probe for adminConfig returned KS 1334, and a deliberately absent string returned 0. No open ticket covers this set.

KS-1407.desc:
## BLUF

A successful password change does not revoke the account's other sessions, and neither does the reset
flow. Raised from gate59's review of PR #1382 (KS 1005). **Pre-existing — not introduced by that PR.**

## N-1382-1 — no session revocation on a successful password change

A successful change makes **zero** `revokeAllUserSessions` calls. The reset flow does not revoke
either. So after a password change — including a change prompted by suspected compromise — every
other authenticated session on that account stays live.

Scope of the evidence, stated so it is not over-read: this was **measured on mocked calls only**, not
against a running stack. The count of zero is a count of calls the handler makes, not a live
observation of a surviving session.

## N-1382-2 — the e2e test for this can never fail

- [ ] Fix the e2e case so it can fail. Case 12.5.3, "other sessions should be invalidated", POSTs to
      `/api/auth/change-password` — **a route that does not exist** — and asserts only inside
      `if (status === 200)`. Because the request cannot return 200, the assertion body never runs, so
      the test passes unconditionally. It has therefore never tested the behaviour in N-1382-1, and
      the correct route is the one KS 1005 fixes.

## Adjacent, and deliberately not merged into this ticket

KS 257 ("Session revocation only enforced at the auth service") is adjacent but different — it is
about *where* revocation is enforced, not *whether* a password change triggers it — and it is
archived. Noted here so the connection is not lost.

## BLUF
**N-1382-1 is BUILT and raised as PR #1655 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1655), head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`, READY FOR GATE, tier 1.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions. **The behaviour change a reviewer must agree to: change-password revokes the caller's OWN session, so the client must sign in again.** Nothing is deployed. N-1382-2 stays open, so this is `Refs`, not a close.

## Recommendation
Gate it as tier 1 — it is a session and credential surface, and it does not merge on a green run alone. Merge on a GO naming head `8e5308a87e14d4a4796e5f838de30dae0838a5bf`; then an auth deploy, which has not happened.

## What changed
| door | file | placement | why there |
|---|---|---|---|
| change-password | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` (+3/-0) | after `updateUserOrThrow` | the write throws if it did not land, so a revocation can never follow a non-write |
| reset-password | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` (+4/-1) | after the write, **before** `consumeResetToken` | a revocation that throws leaves the single-use token **unburned**, so the user can retry instead of holding a changed password and a dead token |

`revokeAllUserSessions` is account-wide and nothing spares `req.sessionId`, so the caller's own access token stops validating after a successful change. That is deliberate. The alternative (`getUserSessions` + `revokeSession` minus the caller's own) needs two functions the existing session mock does not provide; it was neither built nor ruled.

If the revocation throws (a Redis fault) **after** the password was written, the request answers an error although the password did change. Reset: the token is unburned, so a retry works. Change-password: the user retries with the new password as the current one.

## Evidence
- **Red-first, reproduced here rather than quoted: 6 failed / 14 run** — 3 of 7 in each new cell file, the three RED assertion cells, with all 8 CONTROL cells green and 0 load-failure signatures. Green after: **14 passed / 14 run, 0 skipped**. `tsc --noEmit -p services/auth` rc 0.

- **13 mutation arms, 13 killed, 0 survivors, so no cell was added.** Including two that pin *which* account is revoked (revoke a different account id reds R1 on both doors). Each arm proved its anchor unique before tampering, type-checked (a mutant that will not compile is inadmissible, not a survivor), and restored by content with a sha256 equality assertion.
- **Who this breaks: nobody, measured.** No in-repo client calls either route. `me/change-password` has 8 hits, every one the route, the generated spec, the OpenAPI registration or a test; `auth/reset-password` has **zero** call sites under `frontend/` or `sdk/`. Controls: the same search shape finds `auth/login` in 6 files under `frontend/` and 105 repo-wide. `frontend/admin/src/pages/Profile.tsx:49` `handleChangePassword` posts to `/api/auth/password/reset-request` — it emails a reset link and never calls this route. Both SDKs expose no password or session surface. **Equally: no in-repo client exercises this behaviour at all.**

Quoting it as the gate printed it, including its own line *"This is NOT a pass."* Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files against the ratchet baseline: **152 files examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.

**Gate BO1 returned NO GO on the first head with one blocker, and it was right. Round 2 is pushed to the same PR #1655, head `893506989ae7c656e69408d4a6489b052b728e33`, READY FOR DELTA GATE, tier 1.** The reset route failed OPEN when the session store could not revoke: `revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0 with no throw** when Redis is unreachable, so the route wrote the password, burned the single-use token and answered 200 — and the old sessions validated again once Redis recovered. Both routes now fail closed on **both** sides of the write. Three tickets filed from the gate's notes. Nothing deployed.

## The blocker, and why my first body under-stated it
I had documented the case where the revocation **throws**. The real failure is quieter: `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318` is `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;` — a silent zero. The route logged `sessionsRevoked: 0`, indistinguishable from an account that had no sessions. **The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere** (`createSession`, `:156`), and that inconsistency is the root.

## The fix
Route-local, fail closed before the write **and** re-asserted after the revoke:
- **before the write** — store unavailable → 503, nothing written, the reset token **not** burned;
- **after the revoke** — re-assert, because the pre-write check alone is a check-then-act and the store dropping inside that window reproduces the defect exactly. Reset leaves the token **unburned** so a retry finishes the job; change-password says the password **WAS** changed, because telling that caller it failed would send them back to a password that no longer works.

`isRedisAvailable()` was already exported and `ServiceUnavailableError` already existed, so **`services/session.ts` is untouched** — deliberately. `revokeAllUserSessions` has exactly two other product callers (the user-erasure subscriber at `userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` and the admin status change at `routes/users.ts:838`), and changing its contract changes both; that is a wider ruling and is filed as KS-1692.

- **Whole `services/auth` suite: 103 files / 1119 tests / 0 failed, 0 skipped.** Baseline on a clean checkout of the base: 99 files / 1096 tests / 0 failed. +23 cells, **0 vanished**. `tsc` rc 0.
- **Four cell files now declare a healthy session store, one line each, with no assertion changed** — proved by identical `expect(` and cell counts before and after. Two of them (`ks1005`, `ks1052`) **predate this PR** and were found by running the whole suite rather than by reading the route: 6 cells there pin the happy path of both doors without declaring the store's state. Neither is a defect in those tests; the product now has a precondition it did not have.
- Preflight, quoted as printed: `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` Legs 3, 4, 8 need a local stack. Leg 16 type-checks auth's test files: **154 examined, 42 errors, 42 baselined, 0 new**.

- Landing on live develop predicted **`2346900a5105fe24f8b3777a73123dd6df80a2a5`**, merge-tree rc 0, exactly 8 files. Develop moved 6 commits during the round; its advance is 9 files with **0 overlap** with mine (negative control 9).

## Tickets filed from the gate's notes
- **KS-1690** (Bug, High) — the OAuth `refresh_token` grant never reads `decoded.sessionId`, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a new session (gate measured 200 twice, 2 live sessions). Scoped to the origin-session half: **KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of that branch and is still open.** Overlapping but distinct; neither should be closed as a duplicate of the other.
- **KS-1691** (Bug, Medium) — an in-flight request resurrects a revoked session, which is then missing from `user_sessions:<id>` so a second revoke returns 0 and cannot reach it.
- **KS-1692** (Bug, High) — the silent zero as it reaches the erasure subscriber and the admin path.

## Still not covered

**MERGED to `develop` as `86df4f5a52cc36b40276b441900627bf0a4c5de5` (squash of PR #1655), verified at source.** Both password doors now revoke the account's sessions and both fail closed when the session store cannot revoke. Gate BS1 (Opus, tier 1, DELTA round 2 of 2) returned GO WITH NOTE, 0 blockers, 5 notes. **KS-1407 stays OPEN: N-1382-2 is untouched, and gate note N1 is a real residual gap.** Not deployed.

Both routes now confirm the revocation is possible **before** the write and **re-assert after** it, because a pre-write check alone is a check-then-act.

KS-1402.desc:
## BLUF

**No Platform-S rights-assign or rights-reassign reaches** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` **successfully.** originate resolves `newHolderEmail` by calling auth's `GET /api/users/lookup` with the **caller's** `Authorization` header, and `/lookup` accepts only access tokens (`authenticate()`). Platform-S authenticates per Organisation with a **connector** token, so auth answers 401 *"Invalid token"*, originate passes it through ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s 4xx rule), and S degrades to a flat `/api/anchors` anchor. No `custody_events` row is written and `documents.owner_user_id` never moves.

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived) ruled 2026-09-02 that *"Platform S provisions* `users:read` *on its connector key; K does not widen* `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES`*"*. That ruling cannot take effect: the scope check sits behind an authenticator that rejects the token type before any scope is read. A missing scope would answer **403**; what S receives is **401 Invalid token**.

## Code (platform-k `develop` `0736d8b78`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1665-1671` — email-only path: `fetch(${AUTH_SERVICE_URL}/api/users/lookup?email=…, { headers: { Authorization: <caller's header> } })`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1708-1730` — a 4xx from the lookup is passed through; 401 → *"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry."* ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)).
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` — `userRoutes.get('/lookup', authenticate(), …)` — access tokens only.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:357-359` — "[KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) *(Option A): this ONE route also accepts a connector token — see authenticateAccessOrConnector. Every other route keeps plain authenticate()."* — `/stub` was widened; `/lookup` was not.
* Platform-S side: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `TransferCustodyAsync` sends `{ newHolderEmail, reason }` + `onBehalfOf` with `Authorization: Bearer <connector access token>` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1527`).

## Measured — local pair, slot 3, 2026-10-01

platform-s `f370236c` (+ [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) systemTest changes only) ↔ platform-k `0736d8b78`, fresh databases, 33/33 K containers up, `/health/deep` 200, S provisioning key accepted, 10/0/0 organisations registered.

**4 of 4** transfer-custody calls refused, identical body, under Organisation 3's connector key:

```
transfer-custody status=401 body={"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry. Upstream said: Invalid token"}} … using /api/anchors fallback.
```

* 09:21:55Z — 2 calls ([PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914)'s date-sort seed: two documents delegated to a same-org colleague).
* 09:22:55–09:31:06Z — 2 calls during `npm run test:k-live` (`verb_matrix.spec.ts` rights-assign + rights-reassign on K document `7af2374a-dd61-47e7-be50-122dcb5e412b`).

In the same window, Organisation 3's connector token **succeeded** on `originate` (201) and on lifecycle events (`rights-unassign`, `delete`) — so the key is valid; only the auth-service lookup refuses it.

## Why nothing went red

The platform-s `@k-live` cell "rights-assign and rights-unassign each reach K" asserted only that the S edge carries an anchor K resolves as not-failed — which the flat fallback also satisfies. It passed (17 passed / 1 skipped) while both custody calls 401'd. [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) tightens that cell to assert the custody transfer K records — `GET /api/documents/{id}` `owner.id` must move off its pre-assign value (measured: it reads `""` before and after today's refused transfers). The cell is **red until this ticket ships**, deliberately, and turns green once K records the transfer. Platform-S's `TransferCustodyAsync` carries a comment naming this ticket.

## Options (Kamil's call — no K code changed)

1. **Widen** `/lookup` **to** `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, as [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) did for `/stub` — makes [KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s `users:read` ruling effective (the connector key then needs that scope).
2. **originate resolves the holder with its own service credential**, not the caller's header — removes the dependency on the caller's token type.
3. **Platform-S sends** `newHolderId` — requires S to know the K user id of the recipient (S-side; it does not today).

Whichever is chosen, a recipient with no K account still gets the typed 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) measurement A) — worth confirming the S holder exists in K once the 401 is gone.

## Related

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived — ruling this ticket shows cannot take effect) · [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) (Option A connector scoping) · [PS-681](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-681/systemtest-k-live-every-share-and-rights-verb-times-out-waiting-for) (Done — Stuart's original 502 report) · [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) (platform-s: the k-live cell that hid this).

KS-1387.desc:
## Seen (2026-09-29, develop `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching governance)

Starting a fresh stack slot with no cached images (`Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` via platform-s's `up-slot.sh 4`) fails at the governance image:

```
docker compose -p secuura_slot4 build --progress=plain governance
#19 1.611 src/routes/governance.ts(19,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'router' cannot be
      named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'.
      This is likely not portable. A type annotation is necessary.
#19 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c npm run build" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

Reproducible: the same `docker compose build governance` fails the same way on a second run. Slots 1–3 on this machine start only because they hold `secuura_slot{1,2,3}-governance` images built up to two weeks ago; slot 4 had no image and could not be built. A new developer machine, or a slot torn down with `--rmi all` (the test-discipline teardown), hits this.

The first attempt on the same slot failed one image earlier — `nft-certificate` at `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — and that one built cleanly on retry, so it was transient; governance is not.

## Suggested fix

`services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts:19` — give `router` an explicit type (`const router: Router = express.Router()`), the usual TS2742 remedy when a workspace package (`@secuura/shared`) carries its own `@types/express-serve-static-core`. Worth a `tsc --noEmit` over every service in the PR gate so a non-portable inferred type cannot land again.

## Impact on platform-s

Blocks pairing an S slot with a fresh K slot for the gate run on platform-s PR #889 (the S↔K remediation branch); recorded there and on [PS-928](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-928/k-live-goes-red-on-the-second-full-run-on-a-slot-the-anchor-refresher). Related: [KS-955](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-955/a-fresh-clone-cannot-run-the-four-platform-suites-and-fails-in-a-way) (a fresh clone cannot run the suites).

KS-1385.desc:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-k `0aa9b52c6`, platform-s `477eb57`).

## The gap

[KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (merged `cbae988db`, `910687394`) accepts the `identity` block on `POST /api/anchors` and anchors it beside `documentType` / `occurredAt` (`services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts:128-151, 261-315`). Platform-S sends that block on **every** write once `CardanoAnchor:AnchorIdentity` is on — flat anchors, originate, version, certifications, share, transfer-custody and lifecycle-events (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:1606-1631`).

On K, three of those routes never carry it to the anchor:

* `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` reads only `action` and `payload`; an `identity` key in the body is ignored (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2440-2545`).
* `POST /{id}/share` and `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` likewise.
* All three anchor through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, whose body is `{documentId, contentHash, network}` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `identity` (`documents.ts:1275-1297`).

Result: for every non-mutating verb (delete, share-revoke, the share-\* edits, rights-unassign, note, certified, verified, share, rights-assign/reassign) the chain record has no verb and no actor/organisation identity, whatever S sends. Only `upload` (originate) and the flat-anchor fallback carry them.

## Ask

1. Carry `identity` (and the verb as `metadata.documentType`) from the share / transfer-custody / lifecycle-events request bodies into the `emitLifecycleAnchor` call, so the anchor records them — subject to the per-document-anchor ruling on the companion ticket (a reset row would not keep them anyway).
2. Declare `identity` on `DocumentShareRequest`, `TransferCustodyRequest` and `LifecycleEventRequest` in `originate.openapi.ts` so S's [PS-614](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614/check-ss-verb-vocabulary-against-platform-ks-openapi-enum-at-gate-time) gate can see it (today S's `k_openapi_vocabulary.test.ts` only checks `onBehalfOf` placement).
3. Echo what was anchored on the lifecycle-event response, so S's read-back ([PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb) item 5) works on these verbs too.

## Verify

Paired slot with `AnchorIdentity=true` on S: a `share-revoke` on an originated document → the anchor read (`GET /api/anchors/{id}`) returns `identity.actorDid` and `metadata.documentType = share-revoke`. Today it returns neither.

Related: [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb), [PS-864](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-864/epic-id-status-stored-and-shown-throughout-the-system-actor-and), the [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) companion ticket (one anchor per document).

## What changed
- **The four fields hold.** When the anchor guard admits an update for anyone other than the issuer's organisation (today the custodian's organisation, Kam's (c)), `issuerOrgId`, `orgDid`, `orgTrust` and `orgVerified` keep their first-anchored values, and the rest of the holder's payload applies.
