- **It is not a refusal:** `POST /api/anchors` still answers 202 with the same body, and the server logs one info line.
- **The chain carries the same values,** because the Cardano submitter encodes the stored row.
- **Who the guard admits is unchanged,** byte for byte.
- **No migration and no trigger.** A trigger cannot see the caller, so it would have frozen the issuer too.

KS-1384.desc:
## Found by

The S↔K compatibility review of 2026-09-29 (platform-s `477eb57`, platform-k `0aa9b52c6`; origin/develop `b4461d1e2` is three commits ahead, none touching this). Companion to [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one), which asked the question from the S side after seeing six lifecycle events on one document share one External Ref, and one on-chain transaction for register + declare on dev-ps.

## What the code does

`dbPersistAnchor` upserts on the composite key and rewrites the chain columns from the **new** request:

```
services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1334-1372
  INSERT INTO anchor_store (...)
  ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET
    status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash,
    block_hash/block_number/slot/fee/confirmations/confirmed_at = EXCLUDED.…,
    error_message, retry_count, simulated, updated_at = EXCLUDED.…
  RETURNING id
```

`metadata_payload` and `content_hash` are **not** in the update list, so the first event's label and hash stay on the row. Every `POST /api/anchors` builds the anchor with `status: 'pending'` and a null hash (`index.ts:463-560`), so on a conflict the existing row goes back to `pending` with `transaction_hash = NULL`, and `processAnchor(persistedId)` runs again (`:535`).

K's own share, transfer-custody, revoke and lifecycle-event routes all go through `emitLifecycleAnchor`, which posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to that same flat endpoint (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1275-1297`). So every non-mutating verb S records re-enters the same row for the document.

Migration 031 records the one-row-per-(document, network) decision. `anchorSubmission.ts:383-386` (guard 1) reads the row's `transaction_hash` to avoid a second fee-paying transaction — the upsert has just nulled it.

## What this means for the S↔K contract

* Platform-S's user-facing promise (`docs/USER-MANUAL.md` §1, §7) is that every declare, sign and share event is anchored. K anchors **one row per document version per network**; later events reset and re-process it.
* For every verb S routes through `/lifecycle-events`, `/share` or `/transfer-custody`, the chain record carries **no** `documentType` **and no** `identity` — `emitLifecycleAnchor` sends neither, and the lifecycle-events handler reads only `action` and `payload` (`documents.ts:2440-2545`). That is a [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) gap; filed separately.

## Decisions needed (Kamil)

1. Is one anchor per (document, network) the intended contract? If yes, S will label its External Ref column "anchor for version X" and group events ([PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) item 2), and the USER-MANUAL wording changes.
2. If events should each anchor, the upsert key needs an event dimension and `emitLifecycleAnchor` needs the verb.
3. Either way: **what happens on the reset.** Trace whether `processAnchor` after a conflict mints a second Cardano transaction for the same document (guard 1 cannot see the previous hash any more), or is caught by another guard. Not verified live in the review; [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one)'s dev-ps observation was one transaction for two events.

## Verify

* Unit: a second `POST /api/anchors` for the same `(documentId, network)` returns the existing id **and** either leaves a confirmed row's `transaction_hash` intact (per-document contract) or creates a distinct row (per-event contract) — whichever is ruled.
* Live on a paired slot: originate → declare → share on one document; count anchor rows and Cardano transactions; quote both on this ticket.

Related: [PS-895](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-895/question-in-simulated-anchoring-six-distinct-lifecycle-events-on-one) (the S-side question), [KS-1175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1175/anchor-originate-lifecycle-event-schemas-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss) (identity block), [PS-870](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-870/6-send-the-identity-record-to-platform-k-on-every-anchored-verb).

* `confirmed` is terminal in the database: a conditional write never writes over it, and a failure is pinned to the anchor it fails.
* The retry route (`POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor`) first asks the anchoring service whether this document's create already landed on chain (a new `POST /api/anchors/own-create`).
  * If it did, the route answers 409 naming the transaction instead of paying again.
  * If the service cannot answer, the route answers 503 (Retry-After 60).
  * Only "none" goes on to submit.
* The landed rule no longer compares networks (QA gate 68, G68-F1). Where originate and anchoring were configured with different `CARDANO_NETWORK` values, every landed anchor read as "another network" and was paid for again.

Known limits: a verify without a bearer shows the stored state until the GET reconcile or the poller heals it (KS 1918). Older documents with nothing to bind to wait for the operator path (KS 1907, KS 1908).

It deploys only with F0, F-b, R1 and R2a, after the census, box by box, each box Kam's own step. The deploy seat must also read `CARDANO_NETWORK` of originate and of anchoring on each box and find them equal.

Its evidence is in the pull request's Test Evidence block. Each step merges only on its own gate GO, one at a time in stack order; merging is not deploying. QA gate 70's G70-F1 (KS 1920) keeps the CARDANO_NETWORK equality check in the train's deploy hold.

KS-1382.desc:
## BLUF

Five `Blockchain/Testing` entry points fall back to `http://localhost:6882` **— slot 1's gateway — when** `TARGET_BASE` **is not passed**, instead of deriving it from `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. On a slot-N worktree, forgetting the variable points ZAP (active scan), the tenant-isolation job and the internal audit at whichever stack owns slot 1, which on this host is usually someone else's. That is the [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) failure shape (a run named for one slot reaching another), in the shell harness rather than the Schemathesis Python readers [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) fixed.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`)

| File:line | Default |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh:37` | `TARGET_BASE="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh:23` | same |
| `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/05-dast-zap.sh:23` | `TARGET="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Testing/jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh:31` | same |
| `Blockchain/Testing/run-internal-audit.sh:30` | `TARGET_BASE="${TARGET_BASE:-http://localhost:6882}"` |

## Verified from the code (29 Sep, re-read)

None of the five sources `stack_env.sh`, `slot-target.sh` or reads `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT`. The only callers that set `TARGET_BASE` are `.github/workflows/nightly-platform-suites.yml:558` and `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml:351` (CI, unslotted, explicit) plus two script unit tests with fixture values; `orchestrate.sh:138/159` and `run-internal-audit.sh:103` just forward whatever they resolved. `Blockchain/Testing/README.md` and `ci/README.md` never mention slots — their only `TARGET_BASE` example is `TARGET_BASE=https://secuura.com ./run-internal-audit.sh 05` — so a local run following the docs on a slot-N worktree takes the `:6882` default.

## Fix (Internal Audit Harness — Kamil's call)

Source `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/stack_env.sh` (with `PROJECT_ROOT` set — it refuses otherwise) and default `TARGET_BASE` to `http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}`; locally, refuse to start with no slot named (the [KS-1016](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1016/test-anchor-read-honesty-hardcodes-docker-exec-secuura-postgres-fails) rule), so a missing variable is an error, not a silent slot-1 run. CI stays unslotted and passes `TARGET_BASE` explicitly. Add a static check that no `Blockchain/Testing` script carries a literal slot port.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. These five scripts run ZAP active scans, tenant-isolation probes and the audit — aimed at the wrong slot they attack another session's stack, silently. That makes this a high-risk area; `Blockchain/Testing` has no slot tests today (its only test is `ci/aggregate.test.mjs`), so the PR is not done without them:

* For each of the five entry points and `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4: with no `TARGET_BASE`, the resolved target is that slot's gateway (`6882 + 100*(N-1)` from `stack_env.sh`, not a copy of the arithmetic).
* Locally with no slot named: the script refuses with the example command — it never falls back to any slot. With an explicit `TARGET_BASE` (the CI path): it is used unchanged.
* `TARGET_BASE` and the named slot disagreeing (the [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) split-target shape) refuses.
* A static guard over `Blockchain/Testing/**` failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

## Not in this ticket

`Blockchain/Testing/` is the Internal Audit Harness (its README: "standalone, free-tools-only security and compliance harness"), not the `systemTest/` test estate — every commit to it in the last 90 days is Kamil's, hence the assignment. Product-code and template slot-1 values → [KS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381/slot-1-urls-hard-coded-outside-ks-1355s-four-spots-the-three-frontends) (Kamil) and [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a). Schemathesis Python readers → [KS-1373](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1373/schemathesis-full-run-named-slot-3-but-871-of-its-requests-incl) (done in [KS-1353: Schemathesis 4.27.5 → 4.28.0, every floor to latest, harness fixes red→green, and KS-1373 one-run-one-stack guard](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1353-schemathesis-4275-4280-every-floor-to-latest-harness-fixes-45629328f369)).

## Environment

Found 29 Sep 2026 auditing platform-k for fixed-slot URLs while pairing slot 2 for platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views).

## Shared acceptance — slot derivation group (added 6 Oct 2026)

This ticket is one of five platform-k tickets that must all take slot values from `stack_env.sh` and never fall back to slot 1: [KS-1355](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355>), [KS-1381](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1381>), [KS-1389](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389>), [KS-1382](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382>), [KS-1162](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162>). None of them is done until these hold, in addition to its own acceptance above:

1. **One guard.** A single static guard in `check-stack-safety.sh` fails on any literal published port of any slot 1–4 outside `stack_env.sh`. The first ticket to land creates it; the others extend it; nobody adds a second guard. Bite-checked: plant a literal, see it red, remove it.
2. **No silent default.** A local run with no slot named refuses and prints an example command; it never falls back to slot 1 (preflight, `slot-target.sh`, the `Blockchain/Testing` entry points, the smoke scripts). Any change to `stack_env.sh`'s own slot-1 default re-runs every test in this group.
3. **One preflight change.** [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (spot 4, `preflight.sh:94`) and [KS-1389](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1389/sourcing-systemtestslot-targetsh-with-no-slot-named-silently-exports) (leg 13, `preflight.sh:589-630`) land in one PR, or one after the other, each re-running the other's checks.
4. **The workflow question.** [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals) decides first whether the three workflows are deleted or made to derive their ports. If deleted, [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default)'s "explicit `TARGET_BASE` is used unchanged" criterion has no CI caller left; if derived, their `TARGET_BASE` comes from `stack_env.sh` too.
5. **Tests cover every slot.** Slots 1–4, hermetic: identical results unslotted and under each slot's environment.

**This ticket's part:** points 1, 2 and 4 — the `Blockchain/Testing/**` guard in this ticket's acceptance is the point-1 guard extended over this tree, not a second one; and the CI-path criterion follows [KS-1162](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1162/three-retired-github-workflows-bake-slot-234-port-literals)'s decision.

KS-1381.desc:
## BLUF

On a slot-N stack, **platform-k's M365 integration builds its Entra OAuth redirect URI on slot 1's gateway** (`http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback`) unless someone sets `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` by hand — the compose default and three fallbacks in `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` all name `:6882`. And `bootstrap-env.sh` **derives only** `DATABASE_URL` **/** `REDIS_URL` **per slot**, so a fresh slot-N `.env` keeps slot 1's `FRONTEND_URL`, has no gateway origin in `CORS_ORIGINS`, and keeps `LLM_BASE_URL` on slot 1's Ollama — all three had to be edited by hand on slot 2 today. This is the remainder after [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a) (compose `FRONTEND_URL` / `CORS_ORIGINS` defaults, `preflight.sh:94`, `start-local.sh`, `dev-reload.sh` — excluded here). Slots are dynamic; each value should derive from `stack_env.sh`'s exported ports.

## The spots (platform-k `develop` `0aa9b52c6`, tracked files, re-read line by line 29 Sep)

**Runtime — the M365 callback points at slot 1**

| File:line | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:888` | `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI=${ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI:-http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback}` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:481, 595` | `process.env.ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI \|\| \`${process.env.FRONTEND_URL || '[http://localhost:6882](<http://localhost:6882>)'}/api/m365/callback\`\` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:993` | `… \|\| 'http://localhost:6882/api/m365/callback'` |

**Bootstrap — derives two URLs per slot, not the rest** (`scripts/bootstrap-env.sh:229` `DATABASE_URL`, `:240` `REDIS_URL`; nothing writes these)

| Template (`env.example` is canonical since [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap); `.env.example` is its fallback) | Key | Slot-1 value |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:146` | `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6100–:6102` only — no gateway / website origin on any slot |
| `Blockchain/Dev/env.example:372` | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `:11434` (Ollama is offset per slot in `stack_env.sh`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example:117` | `FRONTEND_URL` | `:6882` (lines 23–63 also document every social-login callback on `:6882`) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example:92, 95, 190` (fallback template) | `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` | `:6882`, `:6881` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/*/.env.example`, `services/billing/env.example` — **20 files** | `DATABASE_URL` `:6432`, `REDIS_URL` `:6379`; api-gateway `CORS_ORIGINS`; m365 `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`; billing `API_GATEWAY_URL` | slot 1 |

**Scripts — default to slot 1**

| File:line |  |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/auth-matrix-smoke.sh:31` | `API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:6882}"` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh:15` | `GATEWAY="http://localhost:6882"` — no override |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/setup-dev-environment.sh:323–324`, `start-environment.sh:241` | print slot-1 URLs whatever the slot (display only) |

**Dead config — inert, but a slot-1 literal that reads as live**

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1841, 1876, 1910–1912` set `VITE_API_URL` / `VITE_ORIGINATE_URL` / `VITE_ANALYTICS_URL` to `http://localhost:6882/…` in the issuer, verifier and admin frontends' **runtime** `environment:`. Those images are static Vite builds (`RUN npm run build`, then nginx — `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin}/Dockerfile`), `import.meta.env.VITE_*` is fixed at build time, and no build arg or `.env` supplies it, so the bundles use their relative `'/api'` fallback — correct on every slot. The values are never read; delete them so nobody takes them as the source of truth.

## Fix shape (Kamil's call)

Pass `GATEWAY_PORT` into compose for `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` and drop the three `:6882` fallbacks in m365 (fail if neither `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` nor `FRONTEND_URL` is set); have `bootstrap-env.sh` write `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` from `stack_env.sh` as it does `DATABASE_URL`; source `stack_env.sh` in the two smoke scripts; remove the dead `VITE_*` lines. [KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s proposed `check-stack-safety.sh` pin could take a "no literal slot port outside `stack_env.sh`" rule to hold all of it.

## Acceptance — comprehensive slot unit tests in the same PR

Slots are dynamic: a developer picks, drops and re-picks them at will, several sessions share one host, and slot numbers are never fixed. A value right for the slot it was checked on is wrong on every other — and the failure is silent (a request lands on someone else's stack, or an OAuth callback on the wrong gateway). That makes this a high-risk area, so the PR is not done without unit tests that prove every changed value **for every slot 1..4, not only slot 1 or the slot the author used**:

* `scripts/__tests__/bootstrap_env_slot_ports.test.sh` extended: for `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` = 1, 2, 3, 4, a fresh bootstrap writes `FRONTEND_URL`, `API_BASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS` (gateway + website origins) and `LLM_BASE_URL` on that slot's ports from `stack_env.sh` — and no other slot's port appears in the output.
* A render test (`docker compose config` per slot) asserting `ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI` resolves to that slot's gateway, and a unit test that `services/m365-integration` has no `:6882` fallback left (no-`ENTRA_REDIRECT_URI`, no-`FRONTEND_URL` case refuses rather than defaulting).
* The two smoke scripts target the named slot's gateway for 1..4 and refuse locally when no slot is named.
* A static guard (e.g. in `check-stack-safety.sh`) failing on any literal published port of ANY slot 1..4 outside `stack_env.sh` — bite-checked: plant one, see it red, remove it.
* Tests are hermetic: run unslotted AND under each slot's environment with identical results (the offline-suite rule), never spawned with the shell's slot variables leaking in.

## Not in this ticket

[KS-1355](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1355/stack-tooling-is-not-slot-derived-end-to-end-stack-guard-lists-a)'s four spots. `Blockchain/Testing/**` `TARGET_BASE` defaults → [KS-1382](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1382/blockchaintesting-five-auditdasttenant-isolation-entry-points-default) (the Internal Audit Harness, Kamil). The build break → [KS-1380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1380/develop-does-not-build-since-ks-1378-1339-analytics-billing-and). `docker-compose.production.yml` (deployed, not slotted).

## Correction history

First filed 29 Sep 08:29 UTC with the `VITE_*` values as the headline ("the frontends call slot 1's gateway"). Re-checked against the Dockerfiles the same morning: they are build-time variables never supplied at build, so that claim was wrong and is now listed as dead config; the template counts and canonical-template references were also corrected.

## Environment

Peter's Mac, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026. Found while pairing platform-k slot 2 for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) run.

## The slot-derivation group's shared static guard now EXISTS — created by KS-1355, and this ticket extends it

Facts only, from the KS-1355 build (Seat K 8th, 2026-10-13). KS-1355 is the first of the five to
land, so by this ticket's own acceptance point 1 — *"the first ticket to land creates it; the
others extend it; nobody adds a second guard"* — it created the guard.

**Where it is:** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-stack-safety.sh`, section **3c**. The file went
from 100 to 105 invariants.

**Its scope is deliberately NARROW, and stated in the guard itself:** scripts that run the
**platform** compose stack with `up` / `run` / `restart` / `down`. It does **not** yet cover the
env templates, the 20 service `.env.example` files or the two smoke scripts this ticket lists.
**That widening is KS-1381's**, and the guard's own comment says so by name. Do not add a second
guard.

**What it asserts today:**
- Every declared platform launcher sources `stack_env.sh` — `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh`,
  `Blockchain/Dev/stop-secuura.sh`, `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-local.sh`. It replaced a
  `for f in "$START" "$STOP"` loop that covered two of them, which is how `start-local.sh`
  brought the platform stack up slot-blind with the gate green.
- `LAUNCHER_EXCEPTIONS` — each entry `path|reason`, with a ticket. Current entries:
  `start-environment.sh` and `stop-environment.sh` (**KS-1550**), `observability.sh` (KS-200,
  standalone stack), and two Akto side-stack scripts.
- A **census**: a NEW tracked script that runs the platform compose and is in neither list fails
  the gate.
- Both directions of the list: an exception that is **no longer** a launcher is reported stale,
  and an exception with **no reason** is refused.

**Measurement worth having before you extend it:** a naive text match for a compose
`up|run|restart|down` hits **19** tracked `.sh`, of which **7 are false positives** — the only
mention is a comment or a line that *prints* a compose command to the operator
(`check-slot-credentials.sh`, `setup-dev-environment.sh`, `stack_guard.sh`,
`verify-slot-credential-isolation.sh`, `systemTest/__tests__/slot_target.test.sh`, and two Akto
scripts). Filtering comments and printer lines (`echo`/`printf`/`say`/`print_info`/…) gives the

KS-1380.desc:
## BLUF

A clean build of platform-k `develop` at `0aa9b52c6` fails: `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild` stops with *"Build FAILED for: analytics billing governance — not starting containers"*, so no stack comes up. The previous clean build on this Mac, at `d9ce1403d` (28 Sep), succeeded. Between the two, no `package.json` or Dockerfile of those three services changed; what changed is [KS-1378](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1378/five-new-advisories-block-every-push-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address) **(**[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1339](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1378-bump-morgan-nodemailer-ip-address-and-undici-off-five-815a0a16d4c7), `2cb858335`**)**, which refreshed `packages/shared/package-lock.json` and several services' locks — but not these three.

## Evidence

`packages/shared/package-lock.json` (top-level `node_modules/@types/*`):

|  | before `2cb858335` | after | `services/analytics` lock at `0aa9b52c6` |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `@types/express-serve-static-core` | 4.19.8 | **4.19.9** | 4.19.8 |
| `@types/pg` | 8.20.0 | **8.23.1** | 8.20.0 |
| `@types/express` | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 | 4.17.25 |

Each service image copies the built `/shared` (with its own `node_modules`) beside the service's `node_modules`, so `tsc` sees two copies of the same declarations:

```
analytics  src/index.ts(34,7): error TS2742: The inferred type of 'app' cannot be named without a reference to '@secuura/shared/node_modules/@types/express-serve-static-core'. This is likely not portable.
           (also routes/analytics.ts:20, routes/dashboard.ts:12, routes/health.ts:7)
billing    src/db.ts(45,32): error TS2345: Argument of type 'import("/app/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool' is not assignable to parameter of type 'import("/shared/node_modules/@types/pg/index").Pool'.
           (plus TS2742 on index.ts:33, routes/billing.ts:26, routes/webhooks.ts:29)
governance same TS2742 family
```

`#1339`'s file list refreshes the locks of queue, security, timestamping, prism and others; `services/analytics`, `services/billing` and `services/governance` are not in it.

**The mismatch is wider than the three that fail (re-checked from every lock at** `0aa9b52c6`**).** Eleven service locks still carry `@types/express-serve-static-core` 4.19.8 / `@types/pg` 8.20.0 against shared's 4.19.9 / 8.23.1: analytics, billing, governance (fail) and **kyc, nft-certificate, referral, staking, tenant-provisioning, tokenisation, transfer, wallet-connector** (built fine in the same run — none of their exported types is inferred across the boundary today, so they are latent, one annotation-less `const app = express()` away from the same error). `services/shared` locks 4.19.8 and `vc-issuer` a third `@types/pg` (8.21.0). At the last good commit `d9ce1403d`, `packages/shared` itself locked 4.19.8 / 8.20.0 — every lock agreed, which is why that build passed. All 35 images were attempted in this run; exactly these three failed.

## Likely fix (Kamil's call)

Refresh the failing three — and the eight latent ones — to the same `@types/express-serve-static-core` / `@types/pg` versions `packages/shared` now pins (or pin those `@types` in shared to what the services use). A check that every service lock agrees with `packages/shared` on the `@types` it re-exports would stop the next bump doing this — [KS-953](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-953/class-editing-api-gatewaysrcindexts-silently-reddens-packagesshared) is the same class (a change in one package silently reddening another).

## Reproduce

```bash
git worktree add --detach <path> origin/develop      # 0aa9b52c6
cd <path> && SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=<N> ./Start_Up/start-secuura.sh --rebuild
```

## Environment

Peter's Mac, Docker Desktop 8 CPU / 31.3 GiB, fresh K worktree at `0aa9b52c6`, slot 2, 29 Sep 2026 \~09:25–09:50 BST. Found while bringing up a paired K for the platform-s [PS-914](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-914/data-testid-coverage-audit-scan-every-page-and-ui-element-razor-views) gate run. Not caused by that work (no platform-k change on it).

KS-1375.desc:
**BLUF — the gate measured this at runtime on the merged code (gate38 finding N-1330-1, Major). A credential revoked through** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, resubmitted with any other** `id`**, answers** `verified: true` **with** `checks.status: true`**.** Measured at the PR head and at the merged END.

This is not a defect of #1330 against its ruling — an edited id *is* an unknown id, and pass-through for unknown ids is the open card's default. It is filed because the measured cost of that default is **wider than the card prices it**.

**The mechanism, as the gate read and drove it:**

* Both revocation resolvers key on the caller-supplied `credential.id`, and the stored-record arm abstains on `found: false` (`services/vc-issuer/src/services/revocationResolvers.ts`; `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts` :478-:484).
* **Neither verify route wires a** `didResolver`, so an Ed25519 proof gets a structural check only unless `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (`verifier.ts` :372-:396, read).
* The proof payload **does** cover `id`, so a wired didResolver would catch the edit.
* In production every Ed25519 credential already fails with `No DID resolver configured…` (pre-existing, read, not driven).

**Why it matters more than the card says.** The card `secuura-ks1352-unknown-credential-id-verify-policy` (open, `ruled_ts` null) prices its option a as "a revoked credential whose record was lost still verifies true" — an accident. The measured behaviour is deliberate and trivial: **any holder of a revoked credential can un-revoke it on a development-mode stack by editing one field.**

**Fix-shape (the gate's, quoted):** "wire the issuer's DID resolver on both verify routes so the proof binds `id` (then an edited id fails signature), or key revocation on a proof-bound value."

**Regression cell (the gate's, quoted):** "revoke R1, submit `{...doc, id: 'urn:x'}`, expect `verified: false`."

**Relation to the shipped work.** #1330 (squash `9caa42ad05f145251db820ba43eaf7941316668f`) is what makes revocation reachable at all; before it, verify consulted no authority. This finding is the remaining hole in the id-keyed approach. The unknown-id policy question itself is KS 1368; this ticket is the measured cost that should inform it.

**Board search before filing, with controls:** `didResolver`, `revocationResolvers`, `id-edit`, `edited id`, `No DID resolver` all returned **0**; the positive control `statusListResolver` on the same literal query shape returned **1** (KS-1352), and a nonsense control returned 0.

KS-1692.desc:
## BLUF

`revokeAllUserSessions` **answers** `0` **and does NOT throw when the Redis session store is unreachable** (`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318`: `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;`). Two callers treat that `0` as "there was nothing to revoke" and carry on reporting success. The sessions then validate again when Redis recovers.

**The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere:** `createSession` at `:156` raises `'Redis is not available — cannot create session'`. The inconsistency is the defect.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling after gate BO1 on PR #1655, which measured this failure mode on the password-reset route. **The two password routes are fixed in that PR** by a route-local guard; these two callers are deliberately out of KS-1407's scope and are why this ticket exists.

## Recommendation

Either make the shared function fail closed (a strict variant, or a throw plus an explicit opt-out for callers that genuinely tolerate a no-op), or give each caller its own availability check. It is a **wider ruling than one ticket's scope** because it changes behaviour for every caller at once, which is exactly why PR #1655 did not take it.

## The enumeration (every product caller, measured)

| caller | file:line | what it does with the `0` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **user-erasure subscriber** | `services/auth/src/services/userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` | `const sessionsRevoked = await revokeAllUserSessions(userId);` — an **erased** subject's sessions stay live while the store is down. This is the data-protection path and the reason this is High. |
| **admin status change** | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838` | inside `if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser))` — the KS 796 path whose whole point is "cut the sessions this status cannot hold". With the flag false it cuts none and the status change still answers success. |
| password change / reset | `routes/users.ts`, `routes/auth.ts` | **FIXED in #1655** — both confirm the revocation is possible before the write and re-assert after it. |

Control for the enumeration: the same search shape finds `revokeSession` in **17 files**, so it is not blind.

## Why High rather than Medium

The erasure path is a data-protection obligation: an erasure that reports success while the subject's sessions remain usable is a compliance failure, not only a bug. The admin path is the KS 796 thesis — "this status cannot hold a credential" and "cut the sessions it already has" must not be able to disagree — and under this condition they disagree silently.

## Exposure, stated precisely

While the flag is false the old sessions are refused anyway, because `getSession` returns null. **The exposure is the resurrection after recovery, not the outage itself.** That is the gate's own framing of the equivalent reset case and it applies unchanged here.

## Not measured

I did not drive these two callers against a downed store myself; the mechanism is a source reading of `session.ts:317-318` plus the gate's measurement of the identical path on reset (probe B1: 200, token burned, 0 revoked, and the old session ACTIVE again after recovery). The inference is that the same `return 0` reaches these two callers; the probe for each is not run.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `userErasedSubscriber`, "admin status change revoke sessions redis unavailable", "revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 silently", "erased subject sessions survive". No open ticket covers this. **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0** hits and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned a hit, so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407.

comments.body:
## Gate BS1 adds TWO more members to this family, and one wording fix

While gating PR #1655 (KS-1407, merged `86df4f5a52cc`), gate BS1 measured two further cases of the same root cause this ticket names — `revokeAllUserSessions` not failing closed when the session store is impaired. Verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-20_gate-BS1-pr1655-ks1407-r2/verdict.md` (`sed '1d;$d' | shasum -a 256` = `8480cd2c56ef` = its trailer). Both are **outside** KS-1407's diff and belong here.

### Member: a revocation that THROWS (gate note N1, MEDIUM)
The silent zero is now fail-closed on both password routes. A **throw** is not:
- **Reset (probe R3):** `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, 1 write, **0 burns**; the old session is ACTIVE after recovery, but the retry answers 200, burns once and kills it. Fail-closed.
- **Change-password (probe C3):** `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, the password **was** written, the old session is **ACTIVE** after recovery, and **the caller is told neither**. The natural retry with the old password gets `400 Current password is incorrect`.
- A `.catch(() => 0)` on either route reds **0 of the 23** KS-1407 cells, so no author cell pins this; the gate's R3 and C3 do.
- **Gate's recommended shape:** wrap the revoke in each route and map a throw onto the same post-write **503**, with the "WAS changed / WAS reset" wording, plus one cell per route.

### Member: the unguarded index delete (gate note N2, LOW-MEDIUM, `session.ts:323`)
`revokeAllUserSessions` checks the flag once at `:316`; each `revokeSession` re-checks at `:298` and returns false silently; **`redis.del(user_sessions:<id>)` at `:323` is not guarded.** Probe R4, with 3 sessions and the store flipping mid-loop: the first reset answered 503 with the token unburned, the index set was **deleted anyway**, and the retry then found an empty set, revoked 0 and answered **200 with session 3 still ACTIVE**. The gate's own realism caveat: with real ioredis the window is narrow (a command issued during an outage either resolves after `ready` or rejects, which is the N1 class). Same root as KS-1691's missing tombstone.

### Wording fix to carry in the same round (gate note N4, trivial, mine)
Two defects of my own in the merged KS-1407 code, which the gate directed here rather than to a new PR:
- change-password's post-write 503 says *"Sign in again with the new password"*, but the caller's **own** session survives that path — the gate's C2 made the advised retry on the same bearer and got 200.
- my comments cite `session.ts:317-318` and `:156`; at the merged head the silent zero is at **`:316`** and `createSession`'s throw at **`:155`**.

**This is a later tier-1 round, not now** — per Wednesday's post-merge instruction.

**Gate BS1's note N1 is closed. PR #1669 is up at head `4728c1d613038a8082625f79e564837953bd7453` — a revocation that THROWS after the password write now maps onto the same post-write 503 the check-then-act path already produces, on both password doors. This is PR 1 of two: the `session.ts` half (the unguarded `del`, and the silent zero as it reaches the admin status change and the erasure subscriber) is PR 2 and is ruled separately.**

**The gap, in the gate's words:** *"A revocation that THROWS after the write is fail-closed on reset and only half fail-closed on change-password. No author cell pins either."* KS-1407 installed a flag check either side of the write, but `revokeAllUserSessions` can **reject** as well as answer a silent 0, and a throw skipped the post-write re-assert entirely and landed in `next(error)` as a **500 INTERNAL_ERROR**. BS1's probe C3 measured the change-password case: the password *was* written, the attacker session was **still ACTIVE** after recovery, and the natural retry with the old current password answered **400 "Current password is incorrect"**.

**The fix** wraps only the revoke and re-throws as the existing post-write 503, so a store that is DOWN and a store that THROWS are indistinguishable to the caller. Not `.catch(() => 0)` — that is the author's own A5 arm, which the gate measured reding **0 of 23** cells and which would convert this into a 200 with nothing revoked.

**The number that earned the cells: A5 now reds three of them.** The red-proof judges **14 cells — my 5 plus the 9 pre-existing** — so collateral is a failure, and none appeared:

| arm | failing cells |
|---|---|
| no mutation (positive control) | none, **14/14** |
| `.catch(() => 0)` on both routes | **T1 T2 T3** |
| the catch removed (throw → 500) | T1 T2 T3 |
| a swallow that continues to 200 | T1 T2 T3 |
| the "sign in again" clause restored in both 503s | **T3 alone** |
| the post-write re-assert removed | **B1-R2, B1-R3** — not my cells, proving they do not piggyback on the KS-1407 flag guard |

**Two things deliberately not done, both recorded in the PR body.** N4's line-cite half is a **no-op**: at this develop the head has exactly `session.ts:317-318` and `:156`, so the comment is accurate and editing it would make it wrong — the earlier correction was measured against a different tree. And an arm I had planned (A9: "make the revoke resolve 0, T1/T2 must not red") was **false** — a resolving revoke with a healthy store answers 200 while T1 expects 503 — so I replaced it with the independence arm above rather than run an assertion that could not hold.

**A finding now recorded in the route itself:** `authenticate()` already refuses a change-password request when the store is down, verified at source (`validateSession` → `getSession` returns null when the client is unavailable). So that route's pre-check is **defence in depth only**; the post-write mapping is the reachable half, because the store can drop between authentication and the revoke. Both halves are labelled in the code.

**Suite:** `105 files / 1132 → 1137 tests`, **+5, 0 vanished**, reaching `1137 passed, 0 failed, rc 0`. Leg 16 reports auth at `42 errors: 42 in the baseline, 0 new`, so the added test lines introduce no type errors — the gate's figure, not mine.

⚠ **Known residue:** one run of three showed `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity` failing at **5004 ms**, the 5000 ms boundary class already in `BACKLOG.md` across six source-scanning files; my cells failed 0 times in every run. The cells inject the throw at the mock, so they pin the route's *handling* of a rejection and say nothing about which real ioredis conditions produce one. And the change-password route's two 503s now carry byte-identical messages on purpose — T3 pins the clause on both, but nothing pins that they stay equal.

KS-1683.desc:
## BLUF

**Any authenticated caller can read every stored credential through** `GET /api/credentials` **(list), and any credential by its document hash through** `GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash`**.** KS-1116 binds `GET /api/credentials/:id` and `GET /api/presentations/:id` to the principal that created the row. These two routes were deliberately left out of that change, because Platform S may call them and that could not be measured from Platform K. **KS-1116 does not close the credential exposure; this ticket holds the rest of it.**

## What was measured (develop `937c7d10b`, `services/vc-issuer/src`)

* `GET /api/credentials` (list): `routes/credentials.ts:233-262` → `credentialRepo.list` (`repositories/credentialRepo.ts:139-205`). The filters are caller-supplied query parameters (`issuer`, `documentType`, `limit`, `offset`). With none supplied the WHERE clause is empty and up to `limit` full credential bodies come back, newest first. There is no owner condition on the DB path or the memory path.
* `GET /api/credentials/by-hash/:hash`: `routes/credentials.ts:367` → `getByHash` (`credentialRepo.ts:114-131`), `WHERE credential->'credentialSubject'->>'documentHash' = $1 LIMIT 1`, with no ORDER BY and no owner condition.
* Both routes sit behind vc-issuer's `jwtAuthenticate` (`index.ts:86-92`), and neither is in its `publicOps`. So this is a cross-principal read by an authenticated caller, not anonymous access.
* **A connector can reach both today.** The gateway mounts `/api/credentials` with `authenticateToken(false)`. Its x-api-key branch mints a connector JWT from a validated key and attaches it (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:311`, `:355-375`, `:474`), and vc-issuer accepts that JWT.
* Rows today (read-only counts, 2026-10-20): `vc_credentials_store` holds 0 rows on demo and 0 on kintsugi.
* In-repo consumers: none. Nothing in `frontend/` calls `/api/credentials` (control: the same search finds `api/` in 3+ frontend files). Outside vc-issuer, `by-hash` for this route appears only in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:38665`; anchoring's `verify-by-hash` is a different route.

## Why it was not bound in KS-1116

The Platform S repository is not visible to the Platform K project's GitHub identity. `GET repos/Secuura/platform-s` answers 404 to that token, while `GET repos/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura` answers 200 on the same token, and the token can list exactly one repository. So whether Platform S calls either route is **unmeasured**, not "no".

Under the KS-1116 rule a connector would see only the rows its own connector principal created. If Platform S reads credentials that users created, binding these routes breaks it.

## Open question

Does Platform S call GET /api/credentials or GET /api/credentials/by-hash, and if so for credentials created by whom?

## When it is answered

* The KS-1116 rule (`services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts`, `mayRead`) applies to both routes.
* `list` needs the owner condition in its SQL **and** on every returned record, so that pagination and `total` stay correct and the memory fallback is bound too.
* `by-hash` should return the first credential the caller may read, not the first match. With `LIMIT 1` and no ORDER BY, a caller's own credential could otherwise be hidden behind someone else's.

## Provenance

KS-1682.desc:
## BLUF

`exchangeAuthCode` **hands each new Microsoft 365 connection the FIRST refresh token in a process-wide MSAL cache, not the one for the account that just signed in.** Once two organisations have connected within one process lifetime, the second organisation's connection stores the **first** organisation's refresh token. From its first token refresh onward, the second organisation reads the first organisation's Microsoft 365 as its own.

**No attacker and no leaked id is needed**: two organisations connecting normally is enough. That is KS-1673's harm (one organisation acting as another in Microsoft 365) reached by a different root cause. This is token **selection**, not organisation binding (KS-1673) and not callback state binding (KS-1677).

**Dormant today:** KS-1673's read-only measurement found 0 connections on kintsugi and demo.

## The mechanism, line by line

At develop `640bc7efdfd4` (develop is now `5ac66264b9ee`, which is #1645, docs only - m365 is unchanged). `token-manager.ts` blob `b72a62f4617d`, `index.ts` blob `ba99e5dd8cbf`.

| line | what it does |
| -- | -- |
| `token-manager.ts:26`, `:51` | ONE module-level `ConfidentialClientApplication` for the whole process, shared by every organisation. Its token cache is msal-node's default in-memory cache, living as long as the process. |
| `:85` | `acquireTokenByCode` - msal-node writes this account's tokens into that shared cache. |
| `:93` | `let refreshToken = (result as any).refreshToken \|\| ''` - always `''`; see Measured, item 1. |
| `:94`-`:101` | so the fallback runs on **every** exchange: serialise the shared cache and take `Object.values(RefreshToken)[0]` (`:99`). **Nothing filters by the account that just signed in.** |
| (whole file) | nothing ever clears the cache or removes an account. The only cache call in the file is `:96`. |
| `index.ts:628` (callback), `:746` (`/complete`) | store that refresh token on the connection being completed. |
| `index.ts:862`, `:866`-`:867` | the refresh path uses the stored token. It writes back only a non-empty one, so a wrong token, once stored, is **kept**, and every refresh mints an access token for the wrong account. |

The connection's **first** access token is its own (`:85`'s result). The swap only shows at the first refresh, about an hour later, which is why nobody would see it in a demo.

## Measured

1. **msal-node returns no refresh token.** msal-node is 3.8.10 in this tree. The msal-common it actually resolves (`require.resolve` from msal-node) is its **nested** 15.17.0, NOT the hoisted copy. Its `AuthenticationResult` (`dist/response/AuthenticationResult.d.ts:19-41`) declares **0** `refreshToken` fields, with `accessToken` read the same way at **1** as the control. My first attempt at this read was VOID (a wrong path found no file, and its control also read 0). I discarded it and redid it.
2. **The exact expression on a REAL msal-node cache.** Using msal-node 3.8.10's own `ConfidentialClientApplication`, I deserialised a cache holding org A's refresh token, then org B's. I ran `token-manager.ts:96-101`'s logic verbatim: it returns `RT-OF-ORG-A` for B's sign-in. **Control:** a cache holding only B's returns B's, so the expression is not returning a constant. `getTokenCache()` returns the **same** object on every call (`true`).

## Not measured, said plainly

Not driven end to end against Microsoft: no real sign-in, no real refresh. I relied on msal-node's documented behaviour on two points: that `acquireTokenByCode` writes the account's refresh token into the in-memory cache, and that its serialiser keeps insertion order. A restart clears the cache, so the bug needs two sign-ins inside one process lifetime.

## Board search

Exhaustive, over all **1670** issues (archived included), title + description, exact substring:

* `getTokenCache` 0
* `firstRT` 0
* `acquireTokenByCode` 0
* `object.values(refreshtokens` 0
* `token cache` 4 (KS-156, 191, 198, 1074) - all Schemathesis, performance or anchoring by title.
* `refreshtokens` 1 (KS-317, Akto)
* `token-manager` 2 (KS-37, KS-1641) - neither owns this by title.
* `msal` 6 (KS-130, 470, 493, 1379, 1670, 1671) - none about refresh-token selection.

**Positive control:** `exchangeAuthCode` returns exactly KS-1677, whose description I read and which contains it.

Linear `searchIssues` (fuzzy, indexes comments): `refresh token cache msal` 32, `exchangeAuthCode refresh token` 31, `getTokenCache` 2 (KS-1074, KS-214). Every title read; none owns this.

## How it was found

Seat R 57th, 2026-10-20, reading `exchangeAuthCode` while measuring KS-1677. Filed High on Wednesday's ruling (2026-10-20 \~06:44 AEDT). **No fix is proposed here.** The shape is a later decision.

KS-1673.desc:
**BLUF:** In m365-integration, **nothing ties a Microsoft 365 connection to the organisation that owns it.** Any authenticated user, from any tenant, can do three things:

* list every registered SharePoint site **together with its** `connectionId` (`GET /api/sites`);
* use that id to list the files in **another organisation's OneDrive**, with that organisation's own access token (`GET /api/onedrive/files`);
* **download** one of those files into the synced-document store (`POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync`).

`POST /api/connections/init` takes the organisation from the **request body**, not from the caller's token. **Measured statically. Not driven live.** It only works where `ENTRA_*` is configured and a real connection exists. That is unmeasured for any deployed environment, and KS-693 shows a normal dev machine answers 503.

Found from gate AP1's note N5 on #1627 (KS-1671). Read by Seat R 55th at develop `a66cd6a4d1726794c816fd4fefec58c728d410e5` (`services/m365-integration/src/index.ts`).

## The chain

| step | route | what it does | org check |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `GET /api/sites` (`:890-903`) | with no `connectionId` query, returns **every** entry of `memSites`; each `SharePointSite` carries `connectionId` (`:104-113`) | **none** |
| 2 | `GET /api/onedrive/files` (`:1082-1110`) | `memConnections.get(String(connectionId))` (`:1087`), then lists Graph `/me/drive/...` with `connection.accessToken` (`:1091-1093`) | **none** |
| 3 | `POST /api/onedrive/files/:id/sync` (`:1121`) | same lookup by id alone, then fetches the item's metadata **and** `/content` from Graph with that token | **none** |
| — | `GET /api/connections/:id` (`:722-743`) | returns `organizationId`, `tenantName`, `status` and `scopes` for any id | **none** |
| — | `POST /api/connections/init` (`:612-640`) | `organizationId` comes from `initConnectionSchema.parse(req.body)` (`z.string().uuid()`), not from the token | **none** |

`connectionId` is `conn_<randomUUID>` (`:616`), so it cannot be guessed. **Step 1 is what makes it enumerable**, as soon as any site has been registered on that connection.

## What I read to answer "does any middleware bind the connection to the caller's org?"

* **api-gateway** `routes/proxy.ts:949-957`: `/api/m365` and `/api/onedrive` are `authenticateToken(true)` followed by `proxy('m365', …)`. That checks identity only; nothing scopes by organisation.
* **m365**: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate({ publicOps: ['POST /outlook/verify-hash'] }))` (`:606`) authenticates. I did not read its internals, because m365 never compares anything it sets to a connection's org. `requireM365` (`:259`) is a configuration gate (503 when unconfigured).
* **Census across all 22** `app.<verb>('/api…')` **routes in the file:** **0** read the caller's organisation from `req.user` or headers, and **0** compare `organizationId`. The census is a regex. I then read the five routes above by hand.

## Also from AP1 N5 (same route)

`GET /api/onedrive/files` interpolates a raw `folderId` into the Graph path (`:1090`: `/me/drive/items/${folderId}/children`), with no type check and no encoding. The handler's `try` → `next` means this cannot crash the process. Path text is passed to [graph.microsoft.com](<http://graph.microsoft.com>) under the connection's token.

## Priority: High, and why

It is a **cross-organisation read of customer files**: list, then download, using another organisation's Microsoft token. It is open to any authenticated user, and the enumeration needs only one registered site. Wednesday's rule for this class is High.

**What would lower it, and is not measured:** whether any deployed environment has `ENTRA_*` configured with live connections. Where it is not configured, every one of these routes answers 503 (KS-693). **Checking that means reading a live box, which I have not done.** The connection store is also in-memory and reloaded from the database (`loadFromDb`), so whatever a deployment holds is reachable once it is configured.

## Fix direction (not built)

* Bind each connection to the **caller's** organisation, taken from the verified token, never from the body.
* Every lookup by `connectionId` (or site id) must refuse a caller from a different organisation, with a 404 rather than a 403 so it does not leak that the id exists.
* `GET /api/sites` must filter to the caller's organisation.

This needs a tier-1 gate, with cross-org cells that use two organisations.

## Searched before filing

Searched "onedrive files folderId", "m365 connectionId org tenant isolation", "m365 connection ownership", "onedrive connection cross tenant" and "memConnections". The negative control `zkqvplmxhwrt` returned 0.

* **KS-1670** mentions `memConnections` only for the unencoded success redirect.
* **KS-748** and **KS-619** are about API-key and gateway tenant resolution, not m365 connections.
* The PS-1075..1084 storage tickets are Platform S design.

No ticket owns this.

**BLUF: the last follow-up owed on this ticket is up for review, PR #1640. It is test-only, plus one corrected API description. Nothing is merged or deployed.**

https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1640 — head `c210733f6592`, on `develop` `a4187f0f6`.

**What it closes.** Part B's Teams tests used a stand-in for the database. The stand-in could not see a query whose filter had been **widened** — for example, "this organisation's rows, *or* rows with no organisation". The security review wrote two such breakages that passed all 16 tests but leaked on a real database. This PR runs the four Teams queries — list, notify, delete, register — on a **real in-memory Postgres**. The table definition is read from the repo's own schema file each time, and ownership is checked against the database itself.

**How it was checked.**
- The review's two breakages, plus a third of mine (delete widened the same way), are now each **caught by exactly one new test**. The old 16 tests still pass under all three, which is the gap this PR closes.
- The old tests are unchanged.
- The service's full suite passes: 147 of 147.

**The API description** for sending a Teams notification no longer says it posts "to all configured webhooks", nor that other services call it. It now says what the route does: it reaches the caller's own organisation's webhooks, and a login token with no organisation is refused.

**One thing to know.** The in-memory Postgres reaches this service through another package's development tooling; this service does not declare it. If that ever changes, these tests **fail loudly** — that was checked by removing the package. They never skip silently.

**BLUF: all of KS-1673's code is now merged. Part A, part B and the test follow-ups are on `develop`. Nothing is deployed yet, so the ticket stays open: it is done only when deployed and checked live.**

The last piece merged as `2b205beada00a2f0fb3144e38198e471848132b6` on `develop` (#1640, squashed, one parent `c9ab6b36ff92`). The landed tree is `fc0a930ac613667f1f1e4cc73106777b86c1693f`, exactly the tree required before the merge. The review (gate BC1, the second round) found nothing further.

**What is now on `develop` for this ticket**
- **#1633** — Microsoft 365 connections, SharePoint sites, OneDrive and synced documents are bound to the caller's own organisation.
- **#1637** — Teams webhooks are bound the same way.
- **#1640** — the Teams tests now also run on a real database engine, so a widened filter can no longer pass unnoticed. The notify API description is corrected.

**Before deploy, two things to know.** Both are recorded on this ticket and on KS-1678.
- Existing connections and Teams webhooks created by the admin setup wizard will be **owned by nobody**, because the wizard saved a tenant id where the organisation id belongs. Re-connecting or re-registering is the remedy. There were **0** of either on kintsugi and demo when last measured.
- API keys with no organisation will be **refused** on the Teams routes. That is intended under the no-admin-bypass ruling.

**Related, still open:** KS-1677 (the Microsoft sign-in callback can take over a connection given its id) and KS-1678 (the admin setup wizard).

**BLUF: a second route to this ticket's harm, filed separately as KS-1682 (High). Different root cause, not covered by the fix deployed here.**

This ticket binds each Microsoft 365 connection to its organisation. KS-1682 is about which refresh token a connection is handed in the first place. `exchangeAuthCode` takes the **first** refresh token in a process-wide MSAL cache, not the one for the account that just signed in. So once two organisations have connected within one process lifetime, the second organisation's connection stores the first organisation's refresh token. From its first token refresh it then reads the first organisation's Microsoft 365. No attacker is needed, and the organisation binding added here does not reach it.

Measured statically and on a real msal-node cache; not driven end to end. It is dormant today: 0 connections on kintsugi and demo. Details and the line table are on KS-1682.

KS-1671.desc:
**BLUF:** One unauthenticated `GET` can stop the m365-integration service. Express 4 parses query strings with `allowPrototypes: true`, so `?error[toString]=x` arrives as an **object whose** `toString` **is a string**. `String()` on that object throws `TypeError`. The throw happens inside an `async` handler, and m365 registers no `process.on` handler, so it becomes an unhandled rejection and **the process exits**. Develop has this today; it predates KS-1641 and #1622.

Found by gate AN1 (note N1), reviewing #1622. Filed by Seat R 55th, who reproduced the mechanism. Line numbers are at develop `bc3e2e2460fff5e961cd26b70da3ab0050fccbcc` (`m365-integration/src/index.ts` blob `829a72c9722b`).

## The three inputs

| request | value that arrives | where it throws |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/callback?error[toString]=x` | `error = { toString: 'x' }` | `:474` (`String(value)` inside `capCodePoints`), reached from the `:511` log |
| `GET /api/callback?error=a&error_description[toString]=x` | `error_description = { toString: 'x' }` | `:474`, reached from the `:512` log |
| `GET /api/callback?code=x&state[toString]=y` | `state = { toString: 'y' }` | `:521` `const connectionId = String(state)` |

Before #1622, the same three inputs threw at `:465` and `:472`. #1622 moved where the throw happens. It neither introduced the crash nor made it worse.

## Measured

* **On the real process (gate AN1):** `tsx src/index.ts`, Node v24.7.0, Express 4.22.3, qs 6.16.0. Each case ran on a fresh process, on develop AND on #1622's landing tree. Every time: the socket dropped, `/health` was refused, and the child exited with **code 1**.
* **Controls that did NOT crash (AN1):** `error_description[valueOf]=x`, `[a][b]=c`, `[]=p&[]=q`, `error=a&error=b` and `state[]=a&state[]=b` all answered 302 and the process lived.
* **Mechanism re-checked by me**, against the repo's own `node_modules`:
  * `express/lib/utils.js:290` sets `allowPrototypes: true`.
  * `qs.parse` with that option, then `String()`, **throws** `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` **on all three inputs**.
  * On the controls it returns `"[object Object]"` (`[valueOf]`) or `"a,b"` (arrays).

## Reachable without logging in

`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:936-939` mounts `/api/m365/callback` **with no** `authenticateToken` ("M365 callback must bypass auth"). It is proxied by path rewrite, which forwards the query string. **That is a static reading.** Neither AN1 nor I measured it through the gateway or against the deployed image.

## Beside it (gate AN1 N5)

`:564`, inside the callback's `catch`, calls `encodeURIComponent(err?.message || …)` with no guard. A lone surrogate in MSAL's error text would throw there unhandled, the same way. Reaching it needs a server-issued `state`, and the bug is older than #1622. The same field's reflection *decision* is tracked in KS-1641 / KS-1670.

## Census: does any other service do this? (read-only, static)

I looked for every `String(…)` or template-literal coercion of a `req.query` value inside a route handler, across `services/` and `packages/`, at develop `115797747cb6`. That snapshot is byte-identical to `bc3e2e2460ff` for everything except the two files #1622 changed.

* **9 sites. Only 2 escape as an unhandled rejection, and both are this route** (m365 `:465` and `:472` at that snapshot).
* **auth** `/social/:provider/callback` **(**`routes/auth.ts:1015-1016`**)** applies `String()` to `req.query.error` and `error_description`, also unauthenticated. **But it sits inside the handler's** `try` **(**`:968`**)**, so the throw goes to `next(error)` and the client gets an error response, not a dead process. Checked by hand.
* **api-gateway** `notifications.ts:126-127` runs in a **synchronous** handler behind a 401 check. Express 4 catches a sync throw. Checked by hand.
* **m365** `:482` **and** `:1016` are inside `try` blocks.
* **Services that register** `process.on('unhandledRejection')`**:** `packages/shared` (1 file), api-gateway (2), originate (1). **m365: 0.**
* **The census does NOT prove:**
  * It covers direct `String(x)` / `${x}` only. A method call on a query value (`.toLowerCase()` and the like, which throws on an array or object too) was searched **only in the direct** `req.query.x.method()` **form, and found 0**. That search's control matched a planted line. Calls made through a variable were not followed.
  * "Inside a try" is a brace-counting heuristic. I confirmed the two sites that mattered by hand.

## Fix (Wednesday's ruling)

Accept each query value this route reads **only when** `typeof === 'string'`. An array or object answers the same error redirect a missing value would. **Out of scope:** a process-wide `unhandledRejection` safety net. That is a design call, and KS-1427 owns the posture. For context, Express 5 (KS-775) forwards a rejected handler promise to the error middleware, which would turn this crash into a 500.

Every fix needs a cell per input that answers a bounded 302 **and** leaves the process alive (`/health` 200 afterwards), plus a plain-string control.

## Neighbours read before filing

The search's negative control (`zqwvxkplmhrt`) returned 0.

* **KS-1219:** an array-valued `scope` at OAuth `/authorize` answers **500**. Same input class, a different service, no crash.
* **KS-1427:** the shipped `unhandledRejection` posture. That is the safety net, not this route.
* **KS-1242:** an async middleware with no catch. Same escape mechanism, a different site.
* **KS-775:** the express 4 → 5 decision.
* **KS-763:** qs advisories.

None covers this site.

KS-1645.desc:
## BLUF

**KS-1506 switches** `GET /api/admin/audit/export` **back ON** — it answered **401 to every caller, a platform admin included**, and now serves. Gate V1 measured that directly: a `SUPER_ADMIN` token gets **401 on develop and 200 on the branch**. So this is not defence in depth; it is a dead endpoint becoming live.

**The now-live export has four faults, and they MUST be repaired before this export is deployed.** Three of them make the exported file quietly wrong rather than failing, which is the worst shape for an audit artefact: an operator who exports a year gets a short file with no indication that it is short. Nothing is deployed today — develop only — so there is no live exposure yet. Refs KS-1506.

## Recommendation

**Treat "the file is short or mis-scoped but looks complete" as the defect class, not four separate nits.** An audit export that silently omits rows is evidence that cannot be relied on.

1. **Page the upstream, or declare the cap in the response.** Send a `limit` and loop until `total` is reached, with a stated bound; or, if a cap is intended, put it in `meta` and in the spec so a caller can tell a truncated export from a complete one.
2. **Decide the** `to` **boundary and state it.** Either make `to` inclusive of its whole day (end-of-day, or `< to + 1 day`), or document that `to` is exclusive — and pin whichever with a cell.
3. **Validate** `type` **against** `AuditType` **and 400 an unknown value**, rather than forwarding an arbitrary string. Then pin that the filter actually filters, against a stub that honours it.
4. **Reconcile the spec with the route** (gate V1's Minor 2) — four disagreements, listed in Detail.
5. **Add a cell per repair.** The existing `ks1506` suite drives the real gateway app against a stub upstream and is the natural home; `ks745-audit-export-calls-the-list-route.test.ts` mounts the router directly and is the cheaper home for the query-string assertions.

## Detail

All source references are `services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts` at develop `b01dbdf8aa558de95e10e529f4abc2a914342fb3`, unless named otherwise.

### 1. At most the upstream's default page is returned — no `limit` is ever sent

The upstream request is built at `:139-143` and carries `from`**,** `to`**,** `type` **only**. A case-insensitive search for `limit` in the whole file returns **one** line, and it is a **comment** (`:160`). The response's `total`, `limit` and `offset` are parsed and then **discarded**: `:161` keeps `data.data.logs` alone. There is no paging loop.

So the export returns whatever single page the security service chooses to answer with. **Gate V1 measured that as 50 rows.** The route then reports `totalEntries: entries.length` (`:211`) — the length of the page it got, not the size of the range — so the response's own count agrees with the short file and nothing contradicts it.

### 2. The `to` day is dropped

`formatDate` (`:68-75`) ends in `date.toISOString().split('T')[0]`, so any time component is **truncated** and `to` becomes a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` forwarded as-is (`:141`). The truncated values are also what reach the filename (`:191`) and `meta` (`:208-209`), so the artefact names the range the caller asked for while holding a narrower one. **Gate V1 measured the** `to` **day excluded from the result.** *(The truncation is anchored above; that the upstream then treats the bound exclusively is the gate's live reading, not mine.)*

### 3. `type` is not validated and the gateway filters nothing

`:115` reads it as `(req.query.type as AuditType) || 'all'` — a **cast, not a check** — and `:142` forwards it verbatim. The gateway applies no filter of its own, so whether `type` does anything at all is entirely the security service's business. **Gate V1 measured it ignored.** An unknown value therefore yields a 200 with a filename and `meta.type` that both assert a filter nobody applied.

### 4. The published spec disagrees with the route in four places (gate V1's Minor 2)

`services/api-gateway/src/api-gateway.openapi.ts:610-647`:

| spec says | the route does |
| -- | -- |
| `from`/`to` are `.optional()` (`:622-623`) | **both are required** — 400 `"Both \"from\" and \"to\" date parameters are required"` (`:122-125`) |
| `from`/`to` are `z.string().datetime()`, an RFC-3339 **date-time** (`:622-623`) | the route's own 400 says `"Invalid date format. Use YYYY-MM-DD."` (`:134`) and truncates anything finer |
| **no** `type` **parameter is declared at all** — 0 occurrences in the whole block | `type` is read (`:115`), forwarded (`:142`), and appears in the filename (`:191`) and in `meta` (`:210`) |
| the 200 JSON body is `{ entries: [...] }` (`:635`) | the route answers `{ success, meta, data }` (`:205-215`) — there is **no** `entries` **key** |

The last row is mine, not the gate's. A spec-driven client that reads `entries` gets `undefined` from a successful export.

### What this ticket is not

* **Not** KS-745, which is about the export calling a route the security service does not serve (`/api/audit/logs` → `/api/audit`). That is repaired; this is the surface left behind it.
* **Not** KS-1512 / KS-1545 / KS-1544, which are all `GET /api/platform/audit-log` — a different route with its own paging.

**Deduped before filing:** six searches (`audit export 50 rows`, `audit export type filter ignored`, `audit-log export to date`, `audit export spec disagrees`, `platform audit export`, `audit export limit`), **18 distinct candidates** read. The nearest are KS-745 and KS-1506 itself; none covers these four. Controls on the same reader: `Mount the audit-export router behind authenticateToken` returns KS-1506 first, `Gate S1 residue` returns KS-1643 first — so the search was live.

### Attribution

Faults 1-3's **effects** (50 rows, the dropped day, the ignored filter) are **gate V1's live measurements against a real security service**, which I did not reproduce. What I added is the **source anchor** for each mechanism and the fourth spec disagreement. Named in #1608's body as the condition on deploying this export.

Filed by Seat R 52nd (lane Secuura/Blockchain-R), 2026-10-19.

@kamil.kreiser — read the NO GO at `767ab575818f`. Four S facts for the third-round decision, from S develop `7cb1a4e` (18 Oct):

1. **S no longer needs this residue fixed before 1549's rulings go live.** PS-1285 merged to S develop on 16 Oct (`6cabef6`): S's Verify page now sets the identity K echoes against the commitments of every sibling event on the same K anchor, and a chain identity that matches a sibling renders as "the anchor for this document carries the identity of its *share* event (platform-k keeps one anchor per document)", not as a Mismatch. So "latest event's identity wins" can reach originate's anchors whenever K is ready; the false-Mismatch exposure I described on KS-1385 is closed on S's side either way.

2. **MAJ-A's class includes every S flat anchor.** S's flat `POST /api/anchors` carries the S ledger row's own chain id as `documentId`, one new id per event, with no K document behind it — exactly the "anchor record with no document" the gate describes. Under #1568's external-id lookup, any organisation registering a document whose external id is one of those ids could rewrite the anchored identity, and S could not see or stop it from its side (it only ever reads the anchor back by its own `ExternalRef`). Holding #1568 is the right call for S.

3. **Census for option (ii), "050 refuses an external id that is already an anchor id": no legitimate S flow anchors before it registers under the same id.** S's originate `documentUuid` is the upload row's own chain id (`ToDocumentUuidV4(tx.ChainId)`, a v4 GUID); every flat anchor carries a *different* row's chain id. The one case where one id serves both is the upload row's labelled flat fallback after a refused originate — and S never re-originates a row that already holds an `ExternalRef`, so that id is retired with the row and is never registered afterwards. Option (i) (refuse when the stored anchor predates the claiming document) breaks no S flow for the same reason.

4. **S's preference is unchanged: (iii) KS-1384**, one anchor row per event with a tenant column, which also removes the overwrite S had to word around in PS-1285.

Nothing deployed on S either: dev-ps still waits for its develop deploy (PS-1284 carries the proofs for PS-1201, PS-1126 and PS-1285 together).

## What landed

## What the four gates measured
| round | gate | verdict | what it found |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Opus | NO GO | MAJ-1: tenant B's external id could equal tenant A's certification primary key (fixed by 050) |
| 2 | Opus | NO GO (cap) | MAJ-A: an `anchor_store` row with no `documents` row could be claimed by registering its id; MIN-A: on Prisma the refusal answered 500 |

Certification issue 201, revoke 200, recertify 201, expiry write 200. The census applies over 18 real anchored certifications and refuses a planted claim. MIN-A closed against real Prisma 7.8.0. Two minor follow-ups: **KS-1629** (gate evidence added) and **KS-1642** (new) |

Two round-2 cells pinned 050's constraint name, but the id is anchored first, so 051 fires first (same-timing row triggers run in name order). A test-only delta (`d74b7f951de8`, one file) makes them assert 051's name: 56/56, and reverting either assertion reds exactly that cell |

Round 3 also published a wrong claim, that the round-2 record had named the wrong route. Originate mounts the router at `/api/anchors` AND `/api/anchoring` (`originate/src/index.ts:278-279`), so the round-2 record was right. The correction is in 051's header and in the round-4 commit.
