KS-1603.desc:
## BLUF

`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `POST /api/anchors` (`:463-503`) upserts `anchor_store` on `(document_id, network)` **without checking who owns** `documentId` **or which tenant it belongs to.** This is **pre-existing on develop**. Facts only; **no fix shape is proposed here**. Found by the Opus gate on pull request 1549 (verdict `40bdc24d2e1f07dc`, its MAJ-1) and measured further by Seat J 9th.

## Facts

* **No ownership or tenant check.** The handler parses the body and upserts. `req.user` (role, userId, organizationId, tenantId — `index.ts:520-530`) is used **only** for the connector provenance row, never to authorise the write.
* **A human JWT skips the** `anchors:write` **scope** at the gateway: `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:873-878` with `middleware/scopes.ts:36-39` (read by the gate, not booted).
* `anchor_store` **carries no tenant and no row-level security.** Measured on a repo-built database: no tenant or owner column; `relrowsecurity = f`, `relforcerowsecurity = f`.
* `x-emitter-internal` **is trusted by mere presence** (`index.ts:524`). originate sets it on one call site only, and any peer on the compose network can send it (the F-04 class). Related: **KS-741** (that header is unstripped on the gateway's `/originate/` route) — a different defect, not linked.
* **What it does on develop today (the gate's develop control, measured on the real anchoring service):** a second POST from a **different tenant's user** for someone else's `documentId` is accepted (202, same row id) and makes the platform **re-mint the victim's own first payload** — a fresh transaction, fee and tx-hash churn, but **no falsification**, because the stored payload is write-once on develop.
* **Why it matters beyond cost:** pull request 1549 (KS-1385) as first written made `metadata_payload` overwritable, and **this gap turned that into falsification** — a tenant-B user rewrote tenant-A's attestation and public verify-by-hash answered `verified: true` with B's organisation and identity. That pull request is NO GO and its fix round narrows the overwrite; **this ticket exists because the underlying gap remains whatever that round does.**
* **Writers that reach this route** (the gate's sweep): originate's seven sites, each forwarding the **end user's or connector's own bearer** (not a service identity); Platform S's flat call through the gateway (`proxy.ts:873`) with a connector JWT; and the batch path `POST /api/anchors/batch` (`index.ts:735`), same authentication.

## Same class elsewhere

**KS-692** — `/api/status` revoke/unrevoke has no tenant ownership check. A sibling of the same class on a different route; not a duplicate.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title **and** description (not `searchIssues`, which is fuzzy): `who owns documentId` 0, `anchor_store has no tenant` 0, `ownership check` 1 (KS-692, read: a different route). Positive control `x-emitter-internal` → KS-741. Negative control: a freshly generated token written nowhere → 0. A FIRST negative control was **contaminated** — the term had been quoted inside KS-1599's own dedupe section, so it returned that ticket. Re-run with an uncontaminated token before relying on the zeros.

*Filed by Seat J 9th. Priority High, as Wednesday instructed. Not fixed here.*

comments.body:
**BLUF: a compound risk worth recording against this ticket, found while designing #1568 round 3. Not closed by round 3, and named as narrowing in its PR. Measured read-only at develop `83ed01af70fd5ed6cca9ac66f28ddcb8a1034105`.**

**There are TWO upserts on `anchor_store`, not one, and the second has no guard at all.**

* `anchoring/src/index.ts:1372` — the main upsert. `metadata_payload` is gated (the KS-1385 guard via `mayOverwriteStoredMetadata`, plus `content_hash` and `anchor_type` equality). The other **12** columns are unconditional. That is this ticket.
* `originate/src/routes/anchors.ts:109` (`saveAnchorToDb`) — `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET transaction_hash, block_number, content_hash, simulated, confirmed_at, updated_at`. **No guard, no identity logic, no tenant or organisation check**; it never calls `mayOverwriteStoredMetadata`. Three call sites: `anchors.ts:219` (inside a **GET** — see KS-1629), `:342` (`POST /api/anchors/`), `:442` (`POST /api/anchors/submit`).

**The compound risk.** `saveAnchorToDb` can rewrite `content_hash` on a row it does not own. `content_hash` is also one of the two equality conditions the main upsert uses to decide whether `metadata_payload` may be replaced (`anchor_store.content_hash = EXCLUDED.content_hash`). So a caller who can reach the unguarded writer can **change the value that the guarded writer's condition is tested against**, and thereby satisfy a condition that was meant to protect the stored identity — in two steps rather than one.

**What round 3 does and does not do about it.** Migration 051 closes the round-2 gate's MAJ-A upstream of both upserts, by refusing a `documents` row that claims an id an orphan `anchor_store` row already holds. It does not touch either upsert's column list, so **this ticket is untouched**, including the two-step above. Round 3 says so explicitly rather than implying coverage.

Worth noting for whoever picks this up: `anchor_store` rewrites of `transaction_hash` / `content_hash` / `simulated` on another tenant's row are not only an integrity problem — `content_hash` is the key public verify-by-hash resolves on, so rewriting it changes which bytes verify.

The structural answer remains KS-1384 (a tenant column on `anchor_store`), where I have recorded Stuart's preference and the sizing.

*Seat J 13th. Nothing deployed.*

**BLUF: the interim ownership check is built and at review in pull request 1615. It refuses exactly one thing — an anchor write whose `documentId` is held by a `documents` row in a tenant that is not the caller's — on both `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch`. Everything else behaves as develop does, Platform S's flat anchors and their retries included. The structural answer stays KS-1384 and is untouched.**

## What changed

The gate sits at the one site both routes persist through, so it covers the flat route, the batch loop, and any caller added later. The batch route additionally checks every id in one read **before** anything is written, so a batch holding one foreign document writes neither the batch row nor the items ahead of it.

`dbPersistAnchor`'s upsert gated `metadata_payload` alone (KS-1385). The other twelve columns moved unconditionally for any authenticated caller from any tenant — `transaction_hash`, `content_hash` and `simulated` among them, and `content_hash` is the key public verify-by-hash resolves on.

## What it deliberately still allows

* **An id that no `documents` row holds, in any tenant** — which is the whole of Platform S's flat-anchor traffic, and its retries. Stuart's answer of 15 October is what made this a requirement rather than a guess: S's flat `documentId` is its own ledger chain id, one fresh value per event, never a K document id. Refusing those would have refused the live integration, and refusing a repeat would have looped the registrar.
* **Any caller inside the document's own tenant.** The issuer / custodian test from KS-1385 is not the write gate: using it would have newly refused in-tenant callers who are neither, on the seven originate sites that forward the end user's own bearer. That was not this ticket's scope.
* **A caller with no usable tenant claim**, and **a write whose ownership probe faults** — both with a server-side warn. The worst case of this interim is therefore exactly develop's behaviour, which is the honest bound for an interim.

## What it does not close

The compound risk recorded here on 18 October is **narrowed, not removed**. An `anchor_store` row whose `document_id` names no document records no owner anywhere, so nothing short of the tenant column can say who may rewrite one — that is KS-1384. And originate's own unguarded upsert is a separate route that a guard inside anchoring cannot reach; its remaining exposure is measured and filed as its own ticket.

## Proof

Red first, at the current develop tip: three cells that the branch refuses are **accepted** there — the flat route, an existing row, and a batch — each reading `expected 202 to be 403`, with six control cells green at develop so the rig is shown to work before the reds are read. On the branch, 14 new cells pass and the service's existing 89 integration cells and 379 of 380 unit cells pass with it; the one failure is pre-existing and proved so against develop.

The residue is recorded where it belongs rather than left implied: **KS-1650** carries originate's own unguarded upsert and what is left of it, and **KS-1384** carries the structural answer.

*Seat J 14th. Nothing deployed.*

**BLUF: the interim ownership check is merged to `develop` as `ad784e702ca205230e39d329abefa8a85fb5946c` (pull request 1615), landed tree `8b67dde74820b61e746b2837f32f726b965755ca`. This ticket stays open deliberately: Done needs it deployed and checked live, and neither has happened. One accepted limitation is now tracked separately as KS-1652.**

## What landed

A caller is refused (403) when `documentId` names a `documents` row whose `tenant_id` is not the caller's — on both `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch`. The gate sits in `dbPersistAnchor`, the one site both routes persist through, so a route added later cannot go round it; the batch route additionally reads every id in one pass up front, which removes a partial write it previously had.

Everything else behaves as `develop` did, **Platform S's flat anchors and their retries included** — S sends its own ledger chain id, never a K document id, so no `documents` row holds it and the write is allowed. Exactly the 4 files, +711/−1. The landed tree equalled the review's prediction and an independent prediction made before the merge.

Verification at the merged head: anchoring integration **103/103** in 5 files; red-first **8 failed / 6 passed** with three behavioural reds (a cross-tenant write accepted at `develop` on the flat route, on an existing row, and in a batch); unit **379/380**, the one failure proved pre-existing at `develop` rather than asserted; tsc and ESLint clean. The four platform suites were **NOT run** — no Docker on the authoring machine; that is stated as not run, not as a pass.

## What this deliberately does NOT do

1. **The structural answer is still KS-1384** — a tenant column and one anchor per lifecycle event. An `anchor_store` row whose `document_id` names no document records no owner anywhere, so nothing here can say who may rewrite it; Platform S's own flat rows are in that class.
2. **The ownership probe allows on a fault, by design.** For the duration of a database fault the route is back to `develop`'s behaviour, with a warning naming this ticket on every such call. The interim's worst case is therefore exactly `develop`, which is the honest bound for an interim.
3. **A caller with no usable tenant claim is still allowed** — accepted when the change was planned, because the token's tenant claim is optional and a claim that cannot be compared would refuse rather than compare. That acceptance should not live only in a merged description, so it is now **KS-1652** (Medium), together with two review notes on the same two files: hardening one cell's connection-leak proof, and the batch route's N+1 probe count (speed only).
4. **originate's second, unguarded upsert** is **KS-1650** — a guard inside anchoring cannot reach it.

## Why this is not Done

It is merged, not deployed. The demo and kintsugi boxes were **read** during this work and never driven. Done needs the deploy plus a live check that a cross-tenant write is actually refused on a running box.

KS-1598.desc:
## BLUF

The pull request 1539 Opus delta gate left a follow-up set of seven items. **One of them is a reachable defect on an authorisation route**; the rest are a test gap, two cosmetics, a coverage gap and one documented acceptance. They are grouped here because they are one logical path through `services/security/src/index.ts` and its three suites.

**m1 is the defect: the admin-organisation-scope route's liveness guard does not fold the case of** `users.status`**, so a live ADMIN gets 404.**

## m1 — DEFECT (reachable)

`services/security/src/index.ts:1629` (measured at develop `026c2d1614065c79fc8d96007ac0d80f19fb9363`):

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE id = $1::uuid AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND upper(role) = $3 AND status = 'active' LIMIT 1
```

`$3` is bound to the literal `'ADMIN'` (`:1630`), so the **role** is folded with `upper(role)` and the **status** is compared raw.

The repo stores this column in either case **on purpose**. `migrations/046_users_status_vocabulary.sql` constrains it with `lower(status) NOT IN ('active','pending','suspended','deactivated','invited','inactive','deleted')` (`:34`, `:41`) and states the intent at `:47`:

> Case is folded rather than forbidden: mapDbStatus already accepts either case,

So a user row holding `ACTIVE` or `Active` satisfies the CHECK constraint and **fails this guard**. `PUT /api/security/admin-scopes/:userId` then answers **404 "No ADMIN with that id in that tenant"** for a user that is present, is an ADMIN, and is live. Only a platform role can call the route, so the impact is an operator being unable to grant a scope, not an escalation.

The gate's stated fix: compare `lower(status) = 'active'`.

**This is the second case-folding defect found in this route in one day**, so the whole route was swept rather than this one site patched. **The sweep returns a negative result: m1 is the only remaining unfolded comparison.** Per site:

| Site | Comparison | Folds? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `:1601` | `UUID_TEXT = z.string().uuid().transform(toLowerCase)`, applied to both `userId` and `tenantId` before any query | yes |
| `:1629` | `upper(role) = 'ADMIN'` | yes |
| `:1629` | `status = 'active'` | **NO — m1** |
| `:1638`, `:1690`, `:1693`, `:1741` | `::uuid` comparisons; uuid equality is case-insensitive by type, and the ids arrive lower-cased | yes |
| `:1641-1642` | the `known` Set compares `id::text` (Postgres renders uuid lower-case) against `UUID_TEXT` output | yes |
| `:1688` | `hashtext($1), hashtext($2)` — `hashtext` is case-sensitive, but both inputs arrive lower-cased via `UUID_TEXT`, so it folds end to end | yes, end to end |
| `:1766` | `k.keyHash === keyHash` — hex from one function | not a case question |
| `:1812` | `apiKey.isActive === false` | boolean |

## m2 — TEST GAP (no product defect)

`src/__tests__/ks1570b-concurrent-replace-is-not-a-union.integration.test.ts:100-102` and the 15 cells of `ks1570b-admin-scope-route` pin only the **final set**, not the audit chain. The gate reports that mutants **R2** (the advisory lock moved after the previous-set SELECT) and **R4** (the lock keyed on the raw un-lower-cased ids) **survive every author cell**, and are killed only by the gate's own F1 ×2, F5, F7 and F8.

The gate's stated addition: assert `aud.map(a => [a.before, a.after])` equals `[[[],[A1]],[[A1],[A2]],[[A2],[A3]]]`, plus optionally the F1 upper-versus-lower concurrent shape.

## n1 — COSMETIC

A doubled semicolon at both refactored sites: `const infra = isInfrastructureDbError(saveErr);;` at `:1398` and `:1568`. Exactly two occurrences in the file.

## n2 — COVERAGE GAP, not a behaviour change

The gate's note reads "add 53300 and 57P01 to KS-888's INFRA table (pre-existing, now visible)". Two measured corrections to how that should be read:

1. **The classifier already matches them.** `isInfrastructureDbError` (`:1134-1138`) tests `/^(08|53|57)|^(ECONNREFUSED|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|EHOSTUNREACH|ENETUNREACH|EPIPE)$/` against `String(err.code)` — a SQLSTATE **class-prefix** test. Measured directly, with controls: `53300` true, `57P01` true, `08006` true, `53100` true, `57014` true; controls `23505` false and `42501` false. So there is no behaviour to change and adding the codes as literals would be redundant.
2. **"KS-888's INFRA table" is a test fixture**, not the classifier: `src/__tests__/ks888-failed-mint-save-issues-no-key.test.ts:95`, three rows today (`08006`, `ECONNREFUSED`, a pool timeout with no code), driven through three `it.each` blocks (A2 mint, R1 revoke, V1 validate control).

So n2 is pure coverage: adding `53300` and `57P01` takes the fixture to five rows and yields six new cells, which are **green the moment they are written**. They are coverage, not a red-proof.

## n3 — DOCUMENTED, accepted

The status is read once at `:1628-1631`, before the lock at `:1688` and outside the transaction. The gate's F10 held a PUT inside its transaction and marked the target `deleted` meanwhile: the held PUT still committed **200 with its row written**, and the next PUT answered 404. The window is one transaction long and only a platform operator can act inside it. Accepted as documented; purging rows on demotion or deletion is KS-1592.

## n4 — COSMETIC

Rename the adopted cell's refusal message.

## n5 — BODY TEXT ONLY

Rephrase the "true for CONCURRENT calls only since…" line in the pull request 1539 body and correct its cell count.

## Not examined

The KS-1549 rotate lock at `:387` (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1), hashtext($2))` on a key row's tenant and a connector id) was **not** examined: no ticket, exposure unmeasured, and its inputs are database-canonical rather than caller-supplied.

## Dedupe

Literal `containsIgnoreCase` over title and description, because Linear's `searchIssues` is fuzzy and cannot be a membership test.

**The first negative control was VOID, and the reason is worth recording:** the token `zzqqxx-no-such-thing` returned **1** hit rather than 0, because that exact token had been written into **KS-1594's own description** as the documentation of an earlier dedupe. A control token written into the corpus it controls stops being a control.

Re-run with a fresh nonce: `qq262205d02f9fzz` → **0**, positive control `adminConfig` → **17**. Both fire.

Results with the working controls: `follow-up (pull request 1539` → 0 · `doubled semicolon` → 0 · `audit chain` → 0 · `INFRA table` → 0 · `lower(status)` → 0. The bare term `1539` returns KS-1592, KS-1591, KS-1545, KS-1543 and KS-1540 — none of which is this set. **Related:** KS-1570 (the route this follows up), KS-1591 and KS-1592 (filed from the same gate as separate findings).

Filed by Seat V 8th from the pull request 1539 delta gate's verdict.

comments.body:
**The four Info items from the round-2 gate (report `6a41c4bef88d1e55`, GO at 0 Major / 0 Minor / 4 Info), recorded on merge of `3c0a522216258040f32d400ede433e48e683f734`.** None is code; the gate ruled them text and coverage. Three of the four are corrections to this branch's own claims, and they are written here as corrections rather than paraphrased away.

### i1 — the vocabulary drift detector is blind to any status that is not pure `[a-z]`, and the prose overstated what the cells do

The cell that guards against the vocabulary drifting extracts with `/'([a-z]+)'/g`. The gate planted statuses in its own database and ran only that cell: `+archived`, `−invited` and a renamed constraint each go **red** with a real message, but **`+on_hold`, `+tier2` and `+re-invited` all go GREEN, 1 passed, rc 0.** So a vocabulary that grows by a status containing an underscore, a digit or a hyphen is not caught.

Second half, and this one is about wording rather than code: the comments in `index.ts` and in the test file say the cells "read the vocabulary off the live CHECK rather than carrying a typed copy". **They do not.** The cells iterate a typed `VOCAB` list, and *one* cell compares that list against the live CHECK. The accurate phrasing is "the typed list is checked against the live CHECK". The squash message for `3c0a5222` uses the accurate phrasing; the pull request body still carries the overstated one.

No status in the vocabulary today is anything but `[a-z]` — true of the live constraint definition and of auth's `DB_STATUS_TO_DOMAIN` — so nothing is missed now, and any future addition still has to pass the 18 dead and 4 live route cells. Minimal change when picked up: extract with `/'([^']+)'::/g`, or parse the `ARRAY[...]` form.

### i2 — the X0 mutant was NOT a load failure, and that label was mine

Checked against this branch's own artefacts before accepting it: `logs/mut_X0.log` reads `Tests 45 passed (45)` with `VITEST_RC=0`, and `logs/mut_X0_control.log` prints `DETECTOR: *** DETECTOR FAILED ***`. The gate reproduced it independently: a type error planted in the test file leaves vitest **green 45/45**, leaves the service's own `tsc` unchanged, and reds only under a program that includes the test tree.

So **X0 survived the cells.** It is a survivor that only a test-inclusive type-check catches — not a load failure. Nobody counted it as a kill, so no figure anywhere is inflated; the label was simply wrong, in the pull request body's mutant table and in two one-line summaries. **The squash message carries the corrected label**; the pull request body still carries "LOADFAIL". That discrepancy is recorded here deliberately rather than quietly edited, because the body is the artefact the gate read.

The underlying gap — that nothing type-checks `services/security`'s test files — is **KS-1554**, which already existed and now carries an independent reproduction from this round.

### i3 — `:34` is the `SELECT count(*)`, not the `UPDATE`

The round-1 correction said "`:34` and `:41` are the NORMALISING UPDATE's `NOT IN`". Read at the head of `migrations/046_users_status_vocabulary.sql`: lines **31–34** are the `SELECT count(*) INTO offending` that decides whether to normalise, and lines **38–41** are the `UPDATE` itself, both inside one `DO` block. So `:41` was right and `:34` was not. The accurate phrasing is "the normalising block's `NOT IN`", and the squash message uses it.

The rest of the round-1 i1 correction stands and was verified twice over: the constraint is `CHECK (lower(status) IN (...))` at **`:60`** under the name `users_status_vocabulary`, confirmed against both the migration file and a live `pg_get_constraintdef`.

### i4 — the role fold is one codepoint wider than recorded, and it goes to KS-1601

Under the database's default collation the non-ASCII codepoints whose `upper()` lands in ASCII are **U+0131 → `I`** *and* **U+017F (long s) → `S`**, by the gate's enumeration over every codepoint. Neither can spell `ADMIN` except through U+0131, so the conclusion on **KS-1601** is unchanged, and under `COLLATE "C"` the count is **0** — the same one-token change shuts both. Added to KS-1601.

---

**For the record on what this merge did and did not do.** The guard is `lower(status COLLATE "C") = 'active'`, one behaviour line. The gate measured it by enumeration rather than sampling: over every codepoint `1..0x10FFFF` excluding surrogates, `COLLATE "C"` leaves **zero** non-ASCII codepoints whose `lower()` differs from the input, against **1,404** under the default collation. At the route, all **64** ASCII spellings of `active` give 200 with one row and one audit row, all **32** U+0130 spellings give 404 with nothing written, and six fold-class strings are refused `23514` by the CHECK. On the previous head the same 32 gave **200 with a row**.

**Nothing is deployed.** KS-1598 stays open; the merge contributes to it.

KS-1594.desc:
## BLUF

`services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:924-983` **mints API keys with a raw** `INSERT` **and applies NO provisioning rule at all.** It is a second hop 1 for the KS-1584 two-hop escape, on a different service, and KS-1584's fix does not reach it.

**Measured by the pull request 1541 Opus gate** (verdict sha256/16 `3df0f1ae2c007542`, finding **M1**, rated Major, **pre-existing on develop and outside KS-1584's diff**): an `ORG_ADMIN` can mint a key carrying `organizations:register` with **no** organisation, a **whitespace** organisation, or a **FOREIGN** organisation — and on KS-1584's head that key then mints into organisation A2 with A2's connector id, **201, measured 3 of 3**.

## Why KS-1584 does not cover it

KS-1584 put the hop-1 default deny in the **security** service's mint route and the bound in shared `decideTenantAccess`. This route reaches neither:

* it writes `svc_api_keys` **directly** with `$queryRaw`, so `decideMint` and `decideTenantAccess` never run;
* `const scopes = Array.isArray(d.permissions) && d.permissions.length > 0 ? d.permissions : ['read']` — the requested permissions are stored verbatim, with **no provisioning-capability check**;
* `const orgId = (d.organizationId as string) || req.user?.organizationId || null` — the **body wins**, unvalidated and **unnormalised**, so `'   '` is truthy and is stored as `'   '` rather than as absent.

**Reachable:** the router is guarded by `adminConfigRouter.use(authenticate(), requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'))` (`adminConfig.ts:38`), mounted at `/api/admin` (`services/originate/src/index.ts:300`), and `/api/admin` is in the api-gateway's proxied prefix list (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:392`). So an `ORG_ADMIN` token reaches it through the gateway.

## The gate's minimal fix — a PROPOSAL, not a ruling

1. **Refuse any** `permissions` **set where** `isProvisioningCapable` **holds unless the caller is a platform role.** That is the same default deny KS-1584 applied at the security route, through the one shared predicate.
2. **Store** `normaliseOrgId(orgId)`, so `''` and `'   '` are stored as **absent** rather than as a distinct organisation.
3. **Bound** `body.organizationId` **to the** `ORG_ADMIN`**'s own organisation.**

**(3) IS OPEN and needs its own ruling.** The gate's words: it is the same class as the KS-1533 arm. Today this route lets an `ORG_ADMIN` name any organisation in its tenant, and bounding it is a behaviour change for any caller that relies on that — the admin frontend and e2e paths have **not** been surveyed here. Do not build (3) without a ruling.

(1) and (2) are fail-closed and narrow. (3) is a scope decision.

## Not measured

* Whether any current caller — the admin frontend, e2e, or a seeded script — passes a foreign `organizationId` to this route today. **That survey belongs in the plan, before any build.**
* Whether a key already minted this way exists in any environment. A census belongs with the deploy seat; originate already writes one for keys.

## Round

**This is the FIFTH piece of the KS-1570 round and the round does not deploy until it merges** (Wednesday's ruling with the pull request 1541 GO; recorded in `DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md`). Pull request 1541 is merged as gated; this is its sibling.

## Dedupe

Linear's `searchIssues` is **fuzzy** — it returns hits for a nonsensical control term — so it was not used. Deduped with a literal `containsIgnoreCase` filter over title and description, controlled both ways (`zzqqxx-no-such-thing` → 0; `adminConfig` → 15). `second hop` → 0. The nearest prior art is **KS-1206** (Done): the same route, but about a missing `connector_id` and an unclamped rate limit — not the provisioning scope. `organizations:register` matches only KS-1584 and KS-568 (systemTest coverage).

Filed by Seat V 7th from the pull request 1541 gate.

KS-1584.desc:
## BLUF

**Any tenant-level** `ADMIN` **(scoped or not), and any** `ISSUER_ADMIN`**, can still obtain an API key that names ANY organisation of its tenant AND is bound to that organisation's connector, in two calls, through a provisioning key it is allowed to mint.** KS-1570 does not close the deploy blocker it was written for until this is fixed.

* **Pre-existing:** not in pull request 1535's diff, and identical on develop.
* **Deploy-blocking for KS-1570's purpose:** the KS-695 erasure trusts that key row's organisation and connector, and the erasure is irreversible.
* Facts only, from the pull request 1535 Opus gate (verdict sha256/16 `908a786016f5c2f2`, finding **M1**). **The fix needs Kam's ruling** (see the end). Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## The two hops (measured by the gate on 1535's head `335dfd78`, and the same on develop)

1. **Hop 1:** an `ADMIN` mints a key with `scopes: ['organizations:register']`.
   * `decideMint` takes the KEY_ADMIN early return for every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member, whatever the requested scopes (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:97`).
   * An unscoped ADMIN can do this as an **unqualified** key, which is the path Kam's KS-1570 ruling deliberately keeps open.
2. **Hop 2:** that key's connector principal is a **provisioner**: role `connector` plus `organizations:register` (`services/security/src/index.ts:1218`). It mints `{ organizationId: A2, connectorId: <A2's connector> }`.
   * **Measured: 201.** The row stores `organization_id = A2`, `connector_id = conn_of_A2`.
   * Role `connector` meets neither the org-bounded arm nor the new ADMIN-scope arm (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:170-275`).

The gate measured this for an **unscoped ADMIN**, an **ADMIN scoped to** `{A1}`, and an `ISSUER_ADMIN` **with claim A1**. So KS-1533 arm 1's organisation bound is open by the same route.

**Why it matters:** the KS-695 connector erasure trusts a key row's organisation and connector (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:125, 144, 333-345`).

## The gate's minimal fix (NOT chosen here)

Apply KS-480's limit 1 to non-platform key admins: only a platform role may mint `organizations:register` (and wildcards).

* That needs **Kam's ruling** if a tenant admin legitimately provisions. Wednesday is taking it to Kam on a card.
* No build until it is ruled.
* The gate's regression cell is `evidence/gatetests/gate1535-d-twohop.integration.test.ts` in its evidence folder. It is red on 1535's head and on develop today, and should go green.

## Not tested by the gate

* The gateway hop end to end. It built the connector bearer from auth's `generateConnectorToken` claims and this service's own `/api/keys/validate` output; the gateway proxies `/api/security/*` → security `/api/*` behind `authenticateToken`.
* The erasure actually running against a hop-2 key (a code read only).

**Context:** KS-486 (Review A) recorded that `decideMint` allows on role alone. This two-hop route to a foreign organisation's connector is not on any ticket. The board was searched for "two-hop", "escape from the scope", "provisioning key", and `organizations:register` together with admin and mint.

KS-1570.desc:
## BLUF

**The tenant-level** `ADMIN` **role can mint API keys for ANY organisation inside its own tenant**, because the KS-764 organisation arm never engages for it. Kam ruled to **leave it unbounded for now**, with the note that **it must be changed before deployment**. That makes this a deploy blocker.

**⚠ The blast radius was widened by a second ruling.** Kam ruled the erasure merge-timing card **b** — *"Merge now and accept that every later develop deploy carries the live erasure"*. So **once PR #1497 (KS-695 part ii) is on develop, this ADMIN bound blocks EVERY later deploy**, not only an erasure deploy. Kam was told this on the panel and offered to keep the merge back.

Facts only; no build. The SHAPE of the bound is Kam's to rule (candidates below, unranked).

## Kam's rulings, verbatim

Times as the board stamped them (13 Oct 2026, board time, `view=wednesday`), relayed by Wednesday:

* **09:53:40** — *"Decision secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013: a — Leave ADMIN unbounded for now | note: keep a note that this needs to be changed before deployment"*
* **09:56:23** — the erasure merge-timing card, option **b**: *"Merge now and accept that every later develop deploy carries the live erasure"*

## Measured behaviour (develop `7c6b3d88`)

I ran `services/security/src/__tests__/ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts` on develop's tree myself: **20 / 20 pass**. Three cells carry the point:

| cell | what it shows |
| -- | -- |
| `:162` **RED (R1)** | an `ISSUER_ADMIN` of org A1 naming org A2 (same tenant) is **REFUSED** — the arm works for an org-bounded role |
| `:195` **UNDECIDED POLICY (KS-1535)** | an `ADMIN` naming another organisation **STILL MINTS (201)** — the arm never engages for it |
| `:204` **MEASURED** | `platform_admin` cannot mint at all: `decideMint` refuses it before the arm, so it is **not** a vector |

## Why: which roles are bounded today, read at `7c6b3d88`

| set | where | members |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` | `services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49` | `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ADMIN` |
| `PLATFORM_ROLES` | `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59` | `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` |
| `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` | `keyRevokePolicy.ts:76` | `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` |

* `decideMint` (`provisioningPolicy.ts:95`) returns `{allow: true, via: 'admin'}` at `:98` for every `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` member.
* `decideTenantAccess` (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:141`) engages the organisation arm only at `:173`, `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))`. `ADMIN` is in neither `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, so the arm is skipped and it returns `same-tenant` (`:208`, `:225`).
* **Revoke, by reading only (NOT measured):** `decideKeyRevoke` (`:239`) builds its organisation scope from the key and routes through the same `decideTenantAccess`, so `ADMIN` is equally unbounded on **revoke** inside its tenant.

## Why it matters

The **KS-695 part (ii)** connector erasure trusts the key row it is called with, and the erasure is **irreversible**: it destroys another organisation's titles, descriptions and organisation name. A key minted by a tenant `ADMIN` carrying another organisation's id is exactly the shape the round-4 Opus gate named as **M-1** on PR #1497. KS-1533 arm 1 closed that path for `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`; `ADMIN` is the remaining role.

## Candidate shapes (UNRANKED — Kam's to rule)

* **A role change:** add `ADMIN` to `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, so the existing arm engages for it.
* **A per-organisation scope on the admin:** an `ADMIN` carries the organisation(s) it may act for, and the arm checks against that.
* **An allow-list:** a per-admin list of organisations it may mint or revoke for.
* **Remove** `ADMIN` **from** `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`**:** it may not mint or revoke keys at all.

Each changes what an existing `ADMIN` account can do on the day it ships; the KS-779 ruling on org-less accounts (*"record all ten as intentionally org-less"*) is the precedent for how an org-less admin is treated.

## Related

* **KS-1533** — the parent; arm 1 merged as PR #1521.
* **KS-695** — the erasure this must precede.
* **KS-1535** — the policy question, now ruled; it records the decision, and this ticket is the work it requires.
* **KS-1536** — the role vocabulary split.

KS-1561.desc:
**PRODUCT RULING PENDING - NO BUILD.** Which registrant should `POST /api/verification/verify` present as the certifier when two organisations have registered the SAME content hash? Today a later, hash-only registrant outranks the original, so one organisation can make another organisation's bytes verify as certified by itself without any forged field. This ticket carries the facts and the question; it is not an instruction to build.

## What was measured (Seat J 5th, 2026-10-12, scratch probe on the real routes, real Postgres, as `secuura_app`, single-tenant and pool mode identical)

1. Organisation B's user registers hash H (`POST /api/documents`, 201). `verify {contentHash: H}` answers `isCertified: false` and no `certification`.
2. Organisation A's user registers the SAME hash H as A's own document: **201**. Duplicate hashes across organisations are accepted; K never receives the bytes, so there is no proof of possession.
3. A calls `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `documentId` = A's own document (the legacy certify path; allowed, the caller is the owner, and PR #1525 / KS-1538 keeps it allowed) and `data.issuedBy: "Org A"`: **201**.
4. `verify {contentHash: H}` now answers `isCertified: true` and `certification.certifiedBy: "Org A"`. The two rows: B's stays `anchored` (owner B); A's is `certified` (owner A). `selectVerifiableRow` (`verification.ts`) prefers a `certified` row, so the later registrant outranks the original.
5. Also seen there: `certification.certifierOrganizationId` carries A's **user** id (`certMeta.issuerId = issuer.id`), not an organisation id.

No lineage path and no forged field is involved, so none of the KS-1557 fixes (parent access check, hash bound to the parent, reserved keys stripped, `siblingCertification` resolving the certification) closes this.

## The product question

Which registrant does verify present as the certifier for bytes registered more than once? Candidate shapes (not ranked, not ruled): present a certification only when the certifying organisation holds the ORIGINAL (earliest, or earliest anchored) registration of those bytes; or present every registrant's certification as a list and say which registrant is which (the KS-584 P3 lookup contract); or keep today's behaviour and say so in the contract.

## Relation to other tickets (read, not duplicates)

* **KS-584** (Deployed to UAT, P1) decides what correct resolution means for verify-by-hash and shipped `selectVerifiableRow` as an interim; **KS-590** (Backlog) is its parked regression. This ticket is the trust facet of the same selection: it does not ask for a different interim, it asks which registrant may be presented as certifier.
* **KS-1557** (High): the lineage-path forgery. **KS-1538** (PR #1525): the legacy certify path now needs access to the document.

## Evidence

`5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatJ-5th/evidence/ks1557/`: `probe.integration.test.ts.txt` (cell PB), `probe1557_false.json` and `probe1557_true.json` (the two runs), and the two jest logs.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for five terms on two organisations registering the same hash, `selectVerifiableRow`, duplicate hash across organisations, which registrant is the certifier, and hash-only registration without proof of possession. 200 distinct issues read. Literal matches: `selectverifiablerow` 0, `duplicate hash` 0, `multi-registrant` 0. The only issue matching two or more of eight distinctive tokens was KS-1557; I read KS-584, KS-590, KS-598 and KS-735, and none states this question. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked: "none in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

Source: Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:28Z) that it is filed now as its own High ticket with the label "product ruling pending", no build; she takes the registrant question to Kam.

KS-1557.desc:
**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane; decide the fix, then build it test-first):** any write-role caller in a tenant can make another organisation's bytes verify as CERTIFIED, under an issuer name the caller chooses, through the LINEAGE path of `POST /api/certifications/issue` (`parentDocumentId` set). **No build is started by this ticket; the gate's measurement and fix-thinking are quoted below.**

## What the gate measured (Opus tier-1 gate of PR #1525, KS-1538; real routes, real Postgres, as `secuura_app`, single-tenant and pool mode, identical on base and head)

1. Org B's user registers bytes with hash H. `POST /api/verification/verify {contentHash: H}` returns `checks.isCertified: false` and no `certification`.
2. Org A's user calls `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `{type: 'verification_certificate', parentDocumentId: <B's doc OR A's OWN doc>, data: {title, contentHash: H, issuedBy: 'Org B Official Registrar'}}` and gets 201.
3. Verify of H (anonymous, and as B) now returns `checks.isCertified: true` and `certification.certifiedBy: "Org B Official Registrar"` with `certifierOrganizationId: null`. With B's document as the parent, B's document also gains a `newerVersions` entry owned by A. B's own row is untouched.

## Two independent causes

* **(a) No access check on** `parentDocumentId`**.** `certifications.ts:412-431` checks only for cycles, and `saveDocument` resolves the parent by `external_id` within the tenant (`documentRepo.ts:419-450`).
* **(b) The derived row's** `content_hash` **is taken from the caller's** `data.contentHash` (`certifications.ts:564-567`). `siblingCertification` (`verification.ts:220-236`) then treats any same-hash `signed` row carrying a `certificationId` as certification evidence for those bytes.
* **A parent access check alone would NOT close it.** The gate's ITEM5c control uses the CALLER'S OWN document as the parent and the other organisation's hash H: (b) alone is enough.

## Fix-shape the gate offers (the owner decides)

Require the same access predicate on the parent (the rule `GET /api/documents/:id` enforces, as KS-1538 now applies on the legacy path), AND bind the derived row's hash to the parent's stored hash instead of the caller's `data`. Regression test for the owner: the ITEM5c shape (A's own parent, B's hash), asserting that verify of H stays `isCertified: false`.

## Scope and status

* **Pre-existing, and PR #1525 (KS-1538) does not make it worse**: base and head behave identically on this path, and the KS-1538 guard is skipped by design when `parentDocumentId` is set. **KS-1538 does NOT close cross-organisation certification; this ticket is the open half.** Before KS-1538 the legacy path reached the same outcome more directly.
* Not measured: cross-tenant verify (the verify calls carried the tenant of the certifier); the real gateway, real JWT and real anchoring service (the principal was header-injected, anchoring was a local stub).
* Line numbers are the gate's, at the head of PR #1525. Gate evidence: the probe cells ITEM5 and ITEM5c and `matrix_table.md` in the gate's evidence folder for PR #1525 (verdict sha256/16 `0273b5bb14d3f036`).
* Related, read and distinguished: KS-563 (verify said `isCertified` for merely-anchored documents; its narrowing is why `siblingCertification` exists) and KS-549 (issuer name not persisted). Neither covers a caller choosing the certifier name or the hash.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "siblingCertification", "lineage path parentDocumentId certification access check", "certifications.ts contentHash derived row verify certified", "isCertified another organisation's bytes certifiedBy issuedBy", "verification.ts siblingCertification content_hash certificationId" and "parentDocumentId no access check cross-organisation". 282 distinct issues read. Literal matches in title or description: `siblingcertification` 0, `data.contenthash` 0. Three issues matched two or more of the seven distinctive tokens (KS-549, PS-544, PS-549); I read KS-549 and KS-563 and none covers this. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked, so this is "none in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), verdict GO WITH NOTE, finding S-1; Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:01Z) that it is filed as its own High ticket now.

KS-1556.desc:
**BLUF:** The #1527 (KS-1549) Opus gate returned GO WITH NOTE: 0 Major, 2 Minor (verdict sha256/16 `2c90295b5fb0e300`, head `a430061c`). This is the one P2 follow-up Wednesday's GO requires. #1527 turns a measured 9-in-10 outage into exactly one active key under every shape the gate tried. Both Minors are narrower than the defect it fixed. Until (a) lands, **KS-888's contract ("a failed save leaves memory unchanged") has one known gap**.

**Context:** Lines are on #1527's head `a430061c`, `services/security/src/index.ts`.

- [ ] **(a) m1: a failed COMMIT can leave this process refusing a key the database still holds active.**
  * Where: `saveKeyAndRetirePriors`, `index.ts:318-326`, with the undo at `:330`; and validate's refresh at `index.ts:1447-1450`.
  * Mechanism: the rotate changes the in-memory map BEFORE COMMIT and undoes it if COMMIT fails. The undo restores the OBJECT it captured, `m`. If the OLD key is validated while the COMMIT is in flight, validate reads the row, sees it "revoked in memory", and `memApiKeys.set()`s a NEW object marked revoked (the KS-888 R2 rule: revoked if either source says so). The undo then restores the old object, which is no longer the map's entry. After the rollback the database keeps the old key active, and this process refuses it on every call.
  * Measured by the gate: 3 of 3 at head with the window widened by `pg_sleep`, 0 of 3 on develop, control green. It needs a lost connection at COMMIT.
  * Fix shapes (choose and measure): the undo re-reads the CURRENT entry by id (`memApiKeys.get(id)`) and restores that entry's fields; or the in-memory changes move after COMMIT under an in-process per-connector mutex, so they stay in lock order. Cell: the gate's widened-window shape, with a forced COMMIT failure, asserting that the old key validates again afterwards.
- [ ] **(b) m2 (latent): the fix assumes READ COMMITTED.**
  * Under REPEATABLE READ, 5 of the 8 KS-1549 cells fail with serialization errors. Today's setting is READ COMMITTED, so this is latent: a change to `default_transaction_isolation`, or to the pool's connection options, would surface it.
  * Fix shape: `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED` as the first statement of this transaction, plus a cell that runs the integration file under a REPEATABLE READ default.

**Not exercised by the gate or by me:** pgbouncer (not installed). The lock is transaction-scoped, the form `pool_mode = transaction` supports.

**Related:** KS-1549 (the fix), KS-888 (the contract with this gap), KS-1370 (validate reads the in-memory map).

**Dedupe (2026-10-13):** title and description searched for saveKeyAndRetirePriors, REPEATABLE READ, isolation level, serialization, COMMIT fail, undo, memApiKeys, revoked entry and validate writes.

* Hits: KS-605, KS-603, KS-1284, KS-1439, KS-1353, KS-1408, KS-627, KS-528, KS-888, KS-1174, KS-869, KS-889, KS-1370, plus 44 unrelated "undo" hits (mostly PS-\* UI).
* None covers either item. KS-888 and KS-1370 are the contracts this touches.

KS-1538.desc:
## BLUF

**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane): measure, then fix.** `POST /api/certifications/issue` with a `documentId` and NO `parentDocumentId` (the legacy certify path, `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:557-575` at the gate's head) runs `UPDATE documents SET status = 'certified', certification_metadata = ...` with `WHERE external_id = <the caller's documentId> AND tenant_id = <the tenant>`. **There is no organisation or owner predicate**, so a caller of one organisation in a tenant can certify, and rewrite the `certification_metadata` of, a document that belongs to another organisation of the same tenant, by naming its `documentId`.

**Pre-existing and unrelated to PR #1516**, which did not touch this path. It was found by the gate while it enumerated writers of the `documents` table. It writes `certification_metadata`, which the KS-695 erasure does not read, so it does not affect KS-1508 or #1497.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure first (red-first cell on real Postgres, both tenancy modes, as** `secuura_app`**):** organisation A's connector or admin certifies organisation B's document by `documentId`; observe the status and the `certification_metadata` of B's row afterwards. Not run by anyone yet: this is the gate's reading of the code.
2. **Fix:** bound the `UPDATE` by the caller's organisation (the document's `issuer_organization_id`, or its owner, as the neighbouring read paths do), and refuse with a 403 that is identical for an unknown document and another organisation's, the way KS-764 bounded revoke. Look at who else calls this branch (`documentId` without `parentDocumentId`) before choosing the predicate, and check Platform S's use of it first.
3. **Consider the same predicate on the other** `documents` **writers** in `certifications.ts` once the shape is decided.

## Detail

* Why P2: it is an authorisation gap inside one tenant, on a write that changes a document's certification state, found at read-only level and not yet measured at runtime. It is not a deploy blocker for KS-695.
* Dedupe done before filing: no existing ticket on the board names this file and symbol (searched title, description and comments, archived included, for "legacy certify", "certify path", "organisation predicate", "owner predicate" and "SET status='certified'"). KS-486 (the AuthN/AuthZ/tenancy/IDOR review, Deployed to UAT) matched the phrase "owner predicate" and I did NOT read it for this path.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1516 (KS-1508), verdict sha256/16 `020f335956fb7b09` (GO WITH NOTE at head `770d0f3de074`, merged by squash `b2085e99ff1c` on Wednesday's GO of 2026-10-12 16:40Z), note N-6. Gate files: `WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1516/` (`verdict.md`, `gate1516-attack.integration.test.ts.txt`, `evidence_*.txt`). Line numbers are the gate's, at head `770d0f3de074`. These are the gate's readings and runs; I have not re-run them.

## BLUF
@stuart.jamieson

**One question for Platform S. It does not block you.** Does S ever send `documentId` WITHOUT `parentDocumentId` on `POST /api/certifications/issue`, and if it does, for documents its connector did not create?

## Why we are asking
- That is the legacy certify path (`certifications.ts:557`). It sets the named document to `certified` and rewrites its `certification_metadata`. The only bound today is the tenant.
- The fix we are building makes it enforce the same rule `GET /api/documents/:id` already enforces: the owner, a system admin, the designated recipient, or the connector that created the document. Anyone else gets the same answer as for an unknown document.
- If S certifies documents its connector did not create through this path, it would be refused after the fix. We want to know that before it merges.

## What we know and do not know
- Read at develop `b08ee6299e86`. Not run; no cell has exercised this path yet.
- We cannot read S's code, so we do not know S's use. The lineage path (`parentDocumentId` set) is not affected by this change.

A one-line reply here is enough. If the answer is "never", nothing else is needed.

## BLUF
Facts about the code around the legacy certify path, recorded here for the next reader. No proposal in this comment. The fix for the path itself is being built under this ticket.

## Measured (unfixed develop `b08ee6299e86`, real Postgres, as `secuura_app`, single-tenant and pool mode)
- Organisation A's user, and separately organisation A's connector, certified organisation B's document through `POST /api/certifications/issue` with B's `documentId`: HTTP 201 both times. B's row went from `anchored` to `certified`, `certified_at` was set, and `certification_metadata.certificationId` held A's certification id. The owner column was unchanged.
- A `documentId` that exists nowhere also answered 201, with a certification that certified nothing.

## What the code does (read at the same commit)
- `certifications.ts:570-578`: the legacy `UPDATE documents ...` sits inside `try { ... } catch { /* best-effort */ }` (the catch is at `:579`). Every error from that UPDATE is swallowed.
- A `documentId` that is unknown, belongs to another tenant, or is in a status outside draft, pending_signature, anchored and signed matches no row. The handler still reaches its `res.status(201)` (about `:633`). A certification is issued; the document is not certified.
- `saveCertification` (`:482`) runs before that UPDATE, so the certification row exists whether or not the document was updated. The anchoring submission runs before that.
- Document reads by id are bounded by tenant only, with no owner or organisation check in the lines that follow: `getDocument(id, tenantId)` at `documents.ts:2060` (the `/version` route), and the same call at `:2707` and `:2977`. Which routes those last two belong to is not yet mapped, and their access paths are not read in full.
- `GET /api/documents/:id` lets any caller in the tenant read a document whose owner id is empty: the refusal condition at `documents.ts:1062` starts `userId && document.owner?.id && ...`, so an empty owner id short-circuits it. A connector that creates a document without `onBehalfOf` leaves `owner_user_id` NULL.

## Not measured
The two reads of `documents.ts` above (`/version`, and `:2707` / `:2977`) have not been run. Line numbers are at the commit above.

@kamil.kreiser — **never.** S's certify always sets `parentDocumentId` (the K document it was given at originate); when a document has no K parent id, S falls back to the flat anchor and does not call `POST /api/certifications/issue` at all (`CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs`, `CertifyAsync`). So the legacy `documentId`-only path is not used by S, and the access rule you are adding there does not touch it.

KS-1929.desc:
**BLUF:** `batchLoadRelatedData` in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/db/optimization.ts` runs `SELECT * FROM ${model} WHERE ${relatedField} = ANY($1)` through `$queryRawUnsafe`. `model` and `relatedField` are the function's own string parameters, interpolated with no validation; only `parentIds` is bound. It has 0 callers in this repository, but the shared package is publishable (GitHub Packages, access restricted), so callers outside the repository are unmeasured.

## Where (develop `ca36945e9740`)

* `optimization.ts:99` the function; `:105-107` the call and its template.
* Reachable from outside the file through `export * from './db/optimization'` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts:18`) and the package subpath export `./db/optimization` (`package.json:141`).
* Found when the SQL-injection guard (`scripts/check-no-sql-injection.sh`) was made to read multi-line templates (KS 1867 and KS 1865). The other two sites it finds, `originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:310` and `signatories.ts:346`, were traced and interpolate fixed text only; this one is not like them.

## Caller census (read 2026-11-02, develop `ca36945e9740`)

* In this repository: `git grep -w batchLoadRelatedData` finds 1 hit, the definition (`optimization.ts:99`). Positive control: that hit is the definition. A random token finds 0. Nothing in the tree passes anything to `model` or `relatedField`.
* All 22 open pull requests: 0 hits in their diffs (every diff non-empty; the control token `package_format_gate` is found 15 times, word-matched, in PR 1898's diff).
* The local Extranet project: 0 hits, and it does not import the shared package.
* GitHub code search over the Secuura organisation finds 1 hit, the definition. It proves nothing beyond this repository: the token used sees one repository in the organisation (Distributed_Secuura), and the control that excludes that repository returned nothing for that reason.
* THE GAP: the package is publishable. `package.json` has `publishConfig` with registry `https://npm.pkg.github.com` and access `restricted`; `scripts/publish-shared.sh` runs `npm publish` (nothing in the repository calls that script); `.npmrc` points the npm scope `secuura` at GitHub Packages. The GitHub packages API answered 403 ("Resource not accessible by personal access token") on the organisation's package listing and 404 ("Package not found") on `/orgs/Secuura/packages/npm/shared/versions`. A 404 here cannot be told apart from "never published", so it is not known whether any version exists or whether another repository installs it. An installed copy could call the helper with any `model` and `relatedField`.

## Its sibling in the same file

`getOptimizedCount` (`optimization.ts:119`) is `return prisma[model].count({ where });`. It has a different shape: no SQL text is built. `model` indexes the client object, so a name that is not a model delegate throws a TypeError and a name that is one runs a Prisma `count` on that delegate. It also has 0 callers (`git grep -w getOptimizedCount` finds 1 hit, its definition). It is not part of this ticket.

## Proposed fix (not built by this ticket's filing)

* Validate `model` and `relatedField` as plain SQL identifiers before any query: anchored `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`, length-capped (Postgres limits an identifier to 63 bytes), and throw a constant error otherwise.
* Keep `parentIds` bound. Keep the signature and the result for valid input.
* Deleting the export is not proposed: consumers that cannot be seen could break.
* Until it is fixed, the SQL-injection guard lists this site as `ALLOWED-OPEN`, separately from the sites that were traced safe.

KS-1888.desc:
**BLUF:** In the billing service, 12 routes take a Stripe customer id, a payment-method id or an invoice id from the caller and pass it to Stripe. None of them checks that the id belongs to the caller, and none checks a role. So any authenticated user who has another customer's id can read and change that customer, spend its certification credits, list or detach its payment methods, and read its invoices. `GET /billing/customers/by-email` returns a customer, id included, for any email address, so an email is enough to start. This is **read from code, not exercised**. It is pre-existing; QA gate 47 found it on KS-1850 (pull request 1855), which changes only `POST /billing/admin/credits`.

## The routes (develop cb2320368ae4, `services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts`)

The gate cited these at the pull request's head, 2 lines further down.

| Route | Line | What the caller supplies, and what Stripe is asked to do with it |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /billing/credits/use` | 653 | `customerId` and `credits` in the body; `useCertificationCredits` spends that customer's credits |
| `GET /billing/customers/:id` | 263 | reads that customer |
| `GET /billing/customers/:id/credits` | 284 | reads that customer's credit balance |
| `PUT /billing/customers/:id` | 307 | changes that customer |
| `GET /billing/customers/by-email` | 333 | `?email=`; `findCustomerByEmail`, the whole customer returned |
| `GET /billing/customers/:customerId/purchases` | 462 | lists that customer's purchases |
| `GET /billing/customers/:customerId/invoices` | 486 | lists that customer's invoices |
| `GET /billing/invoices/:id` | 590 | reads that invoice |
| `POST /billing/customers/:customerId/setup-intent` | 513 | creates a setup intent for that customer |
| `GET /billing/customers/:customerId/payment-methods` | 529 | lists that customer's payment methods |
| `POST /billing/customers/:customerId/default-payment-method` | 546 | sets that customer's default payment method |
| `DELETE /billing/payment-methods/:id` | 570 | `detachPaymentMethod` on that payment method |

## What was read

* Each handler's body, up to its closing line, was scanned for a read of the caller (`req.user`, a userId, a tenant), a role reference, an owner compare, or a 403. All 12 handlers had 0 hits. KS-1871.desc:
**Read from code at** `3974f364cbc8` **(the head of pull request 1836), not run against a stack.** Found by QA gate 39 on KS-1807 PR-2 and re-read by me.

**What the code does.** `POST /api/documents` is handled in the api-gateway (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, the `router.post('/api/documents', authenticateToken(true), ...)` handler) before the proxy to originate. For a document type that requires approval (`requiresApproval` with an `approvalWorkflowId`), the handler calls `createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`) and, when that returns `gated`, answers **201** with `status: "pending_approval"` and a `workflowInstance` and returns. It never calls originate on that path. The only checks before it are: `authenticateToken(true)` (any valid token), the connector `documents:write` scope check (applies to API-key callers only), the connector document-type allow-list, `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (type enabled, MFA, verification level, auth provider), and the control-byte guard. None of them is a role check.

**What the gateway does not check.** Originate's create handler (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, around line 387) refuses with 403 `FORBIDDEN` unless the caller has a `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` role (`ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`; `services/originate/src/middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts`) or the `documents:write` scope. On the approval-gated path that check never runs. So an authenticated caller with no document-write role (for example `OWNER`, the self-registration default, a holder or a verifier) gets a 201 where the same call on a non-gated type gets a 403.

**What that call writes.** `createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` stores a workflow instance (`setWorkflowInstance`) and the submitted body as a pending document (`setPendingDocument`, with `createdBy` set to the caller) in the platform store, so an approver is shown a document the creator could not have created.

**Searched for a gateway role gate and found none.** Searching the gateway source for a role gate on `/api/documents` finds only the proxy-path list and the upload body parser in `index.ts`; the `requireAdmin` helpers in `routes/admin.ts` are on admin routes. Positive control: the same file's `authenticateToken(true)` mounts are found (12 in `routes/verification.ts`).

**Not established.** Which document types a deployment has gated (it is configuration). What happens at the final approval step: the gateway forwards the stored document to originate with `x-user-id` set to the creator and the gateway vouch header but no `Authorization` header (`routes/verification.ts`, the workflow-instance approve handler), and I did not trace whether originate then applies its role check to that forward. A refused forward answers 502 `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED` after the instance is already persisted as approved (see KS-1184). Whether pending documents accumulate without a cap or expiry was not checked.

**Related, not duplicates.** KS-1814 (anchor route has no role, owner or revoked-document check), KS-1688 (version route has no per-document access check on its source), KS-1847 (docs claim rules the code does not apply), KS-1850 (OWNER admitted on two admin routes), KS-1184 (approve persists before the forward).

**Docs.** The wording on the pull request is being corrected under KS-1807 (the docs now say the role check is originate's and that the approval-gated 201 is returned before it runs); the behaviour itself is not fixed by the docs series.

KS-1861.desc:
**BLUF:** `DELETE /api/tenants/:id` (and `DELETE /api/platform/tenants/:id`, which proxies to it) does not delete a tenant's data. It clears the tenant's rows from the wrong database, drops a database that does not exist on the shared path, touches none of the tenant's rows in the shared application database, swallows every error, and answers `{ success: true, deleted: true }`. The tenant's tokenisation vault entries and wrapped encryption keys are left in the main database. `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` says deletion "Removes all vault entries for the tenant" and "Drops the tenant's PostgreSQL database". Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Related: KS-1336 (the dormant per-tenant database path), KS-1789 (tenant-provisioning key row written after the caller gives up), KS-239 (erasure decision for subjects, a different path).

## What the code does

`Blockchain/Dev/services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`, `app.delete('/api/tenants/:id')` (`:523`):

* **Wrong database for the vault (**`:551`**):** `for (const table of ['vault_entries', 'tenant_contacts', 'tenant_config', 'platform_document_registry']) { try { await platformQuery(`DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE tenant_id = $1`, ...) } catch {} }`. `platformQuery` is the platform database (`secuura_platform`). The tokenisation service connects to the main database instead (`services/tokenisation/src/db.ts:9`, `DATABASE_URL`; its own KS-288 comment says `tenant_keys` and `vault_entries` live in the main `secuura` DB) and writes `vault_entries` there (`vault.ts`, `INSERT INTO vault_entries`). A tenant's live vault entries are therefore not deleted.
* **Keys never touched:** `tenant_keys` (the wrapped per-tenant key, `tokenisation/src/index.ts`) does not appear in `tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` (0 hits; control: 12 hits in `tokenisation/src/index.ts`).
* **No data rows deleted:** the tenant's rows in the shared application database (`users`, `documents`, and the rest) are not touched; every tenant shares that database.
* `DROP DATABASE` **is a no-op (**`:561`**):** `DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "secuura_tenant_<slug>"`, a database that is never created unless `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is set (it is set in no configuration file; KS-1336 measured this).
* **Errors swallowed:** the table loop uses an empty `catch {}`; the drop only warns. The answer is `res.json({ success: true, deleted: true })` (`:573`) whatever happened.
* **Audit row:** `tenant_deleted` is written to `platform_audit_log` either way.

## Effect

After "deleting" a tenant, the registry row, contacts and config are gone, but its PII vault entries, wrapped key, users and documents remain in the shared database, and the caller is told the deletion succeeded. Whether any tenant has been deleted on a live environment was not checked.

KS-1860.desc:
**BLUF:** Suspending or archiving a tenant (`PATCH /api/platform/tenants/:id/status`, `PATCH /api/tenants/:id/status`) changes a label and enforces nothing. The one place that is meant to refuse a suspended tenant, `extractTenantContext`, asks a map that does not contain suspended tenants, so its 403 can never fire; auth, the gateway, originate and security have no suspension check of their own. `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` says `suspended` means "Access revoked, data preserved" and `archived` means "Read-only, pending deletion". Read from code, not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying `docs/MULTI-TENANCY.md` for KS-1807 (PR-3). Related: KS-1336 (the dormant per-tenant database path; it does not cover this), KS-1406 (tenantless tokens).

## What the code does

All paths under `Blockchain/Dev/`.

* **The check:** `packages/shared/src/db/tenant-context.ts:80`, in `extractTenantContext`: `const status = manager.getTenantStatus(tenantId); if (status === 'suspended' || status === 'archived') { ... 403 }`, only when `manager.isEnabled()` and the tenant is not the default tenant.
* **Why it cannot fire:** `getTenantStatus` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-pool-manager.ts:283`) returns `this.tenantConfigs.get(tenantId)?.status`. That map is filled by `refreshConfigs`, whose query is `... FROM tenants t ... WHERE t.status IN ('active', 'provisioning')` (`:305`), and it is cleared and reloaded on each refresh. A suspended or archived tenant is therefore absent from the map, `getTenantStatus` returns `undefined`, and the 403 branch is never taken.
* **What happens instead:** `getPool` (`:217`) logs "Unknown tenant ..., falling back to default" and returns the default pool, so the request proceeds.
* **Where the check is mounted:** originate only (`services/originate/src/index.ts:230`, inside the multi-tenancy block). Searching the non-test source of `services/auth`, `services/api-gateway`, `services/originate` and `services/security` for a tenant-status or `'suspended'` check on a tenant found 0 hits; control: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts` contains `suspended`. Login and token issue do not look at the tenant's status.
* **No read-only mode for** `archived`**:** searching services and packages for `archived` outside tests finds only `tenant-context.ts:81`. No deletion scheduler exists either.
* **No transition order:** `PATCH /api/tenants/:id/status` (`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`, around `:432-456`) only checks that the value is one of `active`, `suspended`, `archived` and then updates, so `archived` to `active` is accepted. (The doc draws `provisioning -> active -> suspended -> archived`, reactivation from `suspended` only.)

## Effect

An operator who suspends a client to cut off access sees the registry row change to `suspended`, but the client's users can still sign in and their requests are served (auth, the gateway and security check nothing; originate's check cannot fire). Whether any environment relies on suspension today was not checked.

## How to confirm

On a stack with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`: suspend a seeded non-default tenant through `PATCH /api/platform/tenants/:id/status`, wait for the next config refresh, then call an originate route as that tenant's user. Expected by the doc: 403 "Tenant is suspended". By this reading: 200. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Make `refreshConfigs` load suspended and archived tenants (or read status separately from the pool config), enforce the status where tokens are issued and at the gateway, and decide what `archived` means before documenting it. The docs would then lead and the code align.

Searched the board before filing: `suspend`, `tenant delete`, `KS1336`; nothing covers tenant suspension being unenforced. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

KS-1851.desc:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/credentials/{id}/revoke` in vc-issuer checks neither the caller's role nor who created the credential. Any signed-in caller who knows a credential id can revoke it. KS-1116 bound the credential and presentation READS to the creating principal; the revoke write was left out. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Filed on the coordinator's word (2026-10-30 ANSWER, 01:40Z). Related: KS-1116 (the creator binding, reads only) and KS-1845 (admin or owner checks missing on routes that need them).

## Evidence

* **Route:** `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts`, `router.post('/:id/revoke', ...)`: takes `id` from the path and an optional `reason` from the body, calls `credentialRepo.revoke(id, reason)`, answers 404 "Credential not found" when it returns nothing, otherwise 200 with `credentialId` and `revokedAt`. There is no role check and no comparison with the credential's creator.
* **Repository:** `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`, `revoke()`: looks the credential up with `getById(id)` (the exact-id lookup that KS-1116 deliberately left unbound for the public verify path), rewrites its `credentialStatus` (`revoked: true`, `revokedAt`, `revocationReason`) in the in-memory store, and runs `UPDATE vc_credentials_store SET credential = $1 WHERE id = $2`. The SQL has no owner or tenant condition. Not checked: whether row-level security on that table limits the update to the caller's tenant.
* **What sits in front:** the gateway mount `/api/credentials` is `authenticateToken(false)`; the service's own `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` requires a valid token for everything except its three public operations (verify credential, verify presentation, the identity-credential types), so an anonymous caller is refused. Any valid token passes, whatever its role or tenant.
* **The binding that exists:** `services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts` (`mayRead`) binds `GET /api/credentials/{id}`, the credential list and the by-hash read (KS-1683) to the creating principal; its header names only the public verify path's revocation lookup as deliberately unbound and does not mention revoke. `ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts` exercises revoke only by the creator.
* **Why it matters:** the public verify path's revocation lookup reads the stored revoked status (`credentialStatus.revoked`), so this is a write that changes another principal's credential into a revoked one. Not assessed: how guessable a credential id is, and whether the verify routes act on the flag (KS-1352 and KS-1375 are about exactly that).

## How to confirm

Create a credential as user A, revoke it by id with a token for user B in the same tenant (and one in another tenant). Expected by the KS-1116 ruling's intent: 404 or 403. By this reading: 200. Not run.

## What the docs say

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` (KS-1807 PR-1) records the gap as a fact with an `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)` line, because the KS-1116 ruling covers reads and no ruling says who may revoke.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. The shape of the existing binding would extend naturally: read the owner with `getRecordById`, apply `mayRead` (or a revoke variant that also admits the tenant administrators), and answer a refused caller exactly like an unknown id.

Searched the board before filing: `credentials/{id}/revoke`, `credential revoke`, `credentialRepo.revoke` and `revoke a credential` returned KS-188, KS-1352, KS-1375, KS-1684 and KS-692 and none is about the missing owner or role check on this route (KS-1352 and KS-1375: a revoked credential still verifies; KS-1684: the creator refused a read after a revoke on the memory path; KS-692: the status revoke route's tenant check; KS-1116 and KS-1683 are about reads). Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

**BLUF:** Two routes that answer 403 "Admin access required" let `OWNER` through. `OWNER` is the role every self-registered user gets (registration always assigns it), so any registered user passes both: `POST /admin/credits` in `services/billing/src/routes/billing.ts`, which adds certification credits to a customer (credits are money), and `PUT /admin/platform-fee` in `services/nft-certificate/src/routes/nft.routes.ts`, which sets the NFT platform fee. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Filed on the coordinator's word (2026-10-30 ANSWER, 01:40Z). Related: KS-1845 (the same class: admin-labelled routes with no or too wide a role gate).

## The routes

1. **billing** `POST /admin/credits` — comment "Add certification credits to a customer (admin only)". The handler reads `req.user?.role` and answers 403 `FORBIDDEN` "Admin access required" unless the role is in `['SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN', 'OWNER']`. It then parses `{ customerId: string, credits: positive integer }` and calls `getStripeService().addCertificationCredits(customerId, credits)`, answering `{ customerId, creditsAdded, newBalance }`. Nothing ties `customerId` to the caller's own account or organisation. The gateway mount `/api/billing` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(false)` plus the proxy.
2. **nft-certificate** `PUT /api/nft/admin/platform-fee` — comment "Update platform fee configuration (admin only)". Same role list and the same 403 body. It then parses `{ percentage: 0-100, fixed: >= 0 }` and calls `costEstimatorService.updatePlatformFee(percentage, fixed)`, answering the new values. The gateway mount `/api/nft` is `authenticateToken(false)` plus a proxy guard.

`OWNER` is assigned on every registration path (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts` sets `role: 'OWNER'`; an explicit `role` in the request is refused 422), so for these two routes "Admin access required" admits every registered user. A search of `services` and `packages` source (tests and docs excluded) for a bracketed list containing the string `'OWNER'` returns exactly these two lines; the control, the same pattern on the billing file alone, hits it.

## How to confirm

One request to each route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (a freshly registered user). Expected by the route's own message: 403. By this reading: 200 with the new balance, and 200 with the new fee. Not run.

## What the docs say

`docs/security/ROLES-AND-AUTHORIZATION-INVENTORY.md` (KS-1807 PR-1) records the two inline lists as a fact with an `UNDECIDED (KS-1807, 2026-10-30)` line, because no ruling says whether `OWNER` is meant to pass; this ticket is where that is decided.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. If "admin only" is the intent, drop `OWNER` from both lists (or use the shared `requireRole`) and, for credits, bind `customerId` to the caller's own customer unless the caller is a platform admin.

Verdict file (the coordinator's reference, local to her): `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-30_gate30-1826/verdict.md`; the probe `g30-probe-race.test.ts` (P1 and P2) sits beside it. Related: KS-1804, where it was found, and the neighbours the gate named, KS-809, KS-1052 and KS-1081, none of which is about concurrency. KS-1327 is the same whole-row read-modify-write class on KYC writes, not on backup codes. Filed on Wednesday's word.

**The verdict text, quoted (F1, lines 46 to 50 of the verdict, unedited):**

* **F1 (Major, PRE-EXISTING product, out of this PR's scope; recommend filing).** The single-use burn is not atomic.
  * **Where:** `passwordLoginGate.ts:273-285` + `userRepo.ts:891-894`. The code reads, then splices in memory, then writes the whole array by `WHERE id` only.
  * **Effect:** two concurrent logins with one backup code both get a credential, and two concurrent logins with different codes can leave a spent code valid (a lost update). Measured against a stateful stub (probe P1 and P2), NOT against Postgres.
  * **Board search (Linear** `searchIssues`**, includeArchived):** no ticket matched literally on "backup code concurrent", "backup code race", "mfa_backup_codes race" or "backup code twice"; the fuzzy hits were KS-809, KS-1052 and KS-1081, none about concurrency. Control: a nonsense term gave 0. KS-1052 and KS-533 contain no race or concurrency text (grep).
  * **Possible remedies (not built):** `UPDATE … SET mfa_backup_codes = array_remove(mfa_backup_codes, $hash) WHERE id = $id AND $hash = ANY(mfa_backup_codes)`, requiring rowCount 1; or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` in a transaction.

**Fix shape (the gate's, not built here):** a conditional update that removes exactly the presented code and requires it to be present, or a row lock, as quoted above. It touches the credential path, so the fix would get a tier-1 gate.

**Board search before filing** (issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, 2026-10-30): random-token control 0 hits; positive control `passwordLoginGate` 13 hits including KS-1804. `mfa_backup_codes` 5 hits (KS-1052, KS-938, KS-809, KS-795, KS-783), `mfaBackupCodes` 6 (KS-938, KS-809, KS-783, KS-732, KS-622, KS-256), `array_remove` 0, `backup code race` 0, `backup code twice` 0, `burn is not atomic` 0, `lost update` 4 (KS-1377, KS-1370, KS-772, KS-485: none about backup codes), `FOR UPDATE` 2 (KS-1327, KS-757: neither about backup codes). KS-809, KS-1052, KS-1081, KS-533 and KS-1804 read whole for race or concurrency text: no statement about concurrent burns.

**Not measured by this filing:** anything against Postgres; both effects were shown against a stateful stub by the gate's probe, and this ticket does not repeat it.
