KS-1845.desc:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/kyc/:id/review` approves or rejects a KYC verification and sets its `currentLevel` (up to `GOVERNMENT`), but it checks no role and no ownership. The only authentication in front of it is `jwtAuthenticate` on `/api` inside the kyc service and `authenticateToken(true)` on the `/api/kyc` gateway mount, so any signed-in caller who knows the id of a verification in state `under_review` can decide it. The published spec declares `403 Reviewer role required` on this operation. Four more routes that their own comments or the spec call admin-only have the same shape. Read from code at `develop` `530f09112`; nothing was probed against a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-1, authentication, roles and scopes). Doc-versus-code difference: the spec (and the inventory's "they rely on gateway auth + ownership/tenant checks") says a gate exists; the code has none.

## The routes

1. **kyc review** — `services/kyc/src/index.ts`, handler for `POST /api/kyc/:id/review`. It parses `reviewVerificationSchema` (`status` approved or rejected, optional `reviewNotes`, optional `newLevel` NONE to GOVERNMENT), takes `reviewerId` from `req.user?.userId` (falling back to the string `admin`), then writes `verification.status` and, on approval, `verification.currentLevel = data.newLevel || verification.requestedLevel` and saves it. There is no `requireRole`, and nothing compares the verification's owner with the caller. Spec: `services/kyc/src/kyc.openapi.ts` declares the 403 with the description "Reviewer role required". Gateway: the `/api/kyc` mount in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` is `authenticateToken(true)` plus the proxy. Not checked: whether the verification's `currentLevel` is read back into a user's token level elsewhere.
2. **governance** — `POST /api/governance/process-expired` in `services/governance/src/routes/governance.ts` (comment: "admin/cron endpoint"); spec `governance.openapi.ts` declares 403 "Admin role required". The gateway mount `/api/governance` uses `authenticateToken(false)` (the shape KS-736 tracks).
3. **transfer** — `POST /api/delegations/admin/process-expired` in `services/transfer/src/routes/delegations.ts` (comment: "admin trigger"). Mount is authentication only.
4. **staking** — `GET /api/stake/all` in `services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts` (comment: "List all stakes (admin)"); the handler pages `SELECT * FROM svc_stake_positions`. Mount is authentication only. Not checked: whether that table is tenant-scoped.
5. **wallet-connector** — `GET /api/wallets/sessions` in `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts` (comment: "List active sessions (admin)"). Mount is authentication only.

For all five the service mounts no role gate (a census of `services/*/src` for `requireRole`, role comparisons and `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` finds none in kyc, governance, transfer, staking or wallet-connector; the same census finds originate's 73 hits, so the instrument fires).

## Evidence and how to confirm

Read at `develop` `530f09112`. A live check is one request per route with a token whose role is `OWNER` (the self-registration default); the expected answer by the spec is 403, and by this reading it is 2xx (or 404 for an unknown id). Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Peter's ruling recorded on KS-1668: the docs lead and the code aligns to them; Kam decides which side moves. The aligned fix is a role gate on each route (the shared `requireRole` in `packages/shared/src/middleware/index.ts` is already mounted in billing, tokenisation and vc-issuer), and for the kyc review an owner-not-reviewer check as well. KS-1807's PR-1 documents the difference rather than the intended gate, and marks the passage so a test is not written against current behaviour.

Searched the board before filing: `Reviewer role required` 0 hits, `process-expired` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1762), `kyc/:id/review` 1 unrelated hit (KS-1327, a read-modify-write race). Control in the same session: `subjects:erase` returned KS-843.

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/app.ts:45-47`: `/api` requires a JWT except the two verify operations. The caller is therefore authenticated, but nothing compares the caller to a record's owner or tenant.

**BLUF:** Pull request 1813 (head `77a807d188ab`) builds this ticket's fix: GET /api/anchors/:id and GET /api/anchors/document/:documentId now answer another tenant's anchor with exactly the 404 an absent row gets. It is waiting for the QA gate; not merged, not deployed. **What changed.** A new `anchoring/src/anchorReadGate.ts` applies the write side's ruled decision table (KS 1603) to the two reads. It refuses only a row whose document belongs to another tenant, and allows the caller's own tenant, flat anchors (no document holds the id), a caller with no usable tenant claim, and a probe fault (fail-open, one warn line). The refusal is byte-identical to the absent-row 404, never a 403, so it does not reveal that the anchor exists; the server log names the document and both tenants. `index.ts` gains one import and one gated line per handler (+6 -0); on the by-id route the document-id fallback is gated too.

**What proves it.**
* 12 unit cells driving the real app: 7 red on develop's handlers, 12 of 12 with the change.
* 17 of 17 mutants killed (each parsed first, each file restored and sha256-checked).
* 1 integration cell on a migrated Postgres (15.19, 57 migrations) with the app as `secuura_app`: red on develop's handlers (tenant A read tenant B's anchor), green with the change. The schema read directly: `anchor_store` has row-level security off, no policy and no `tenant_id`, so nothing below the handler scoped these reads before.
* Anchoring unit suite 35 files / 497 cells on develop's code, 36 / 509 with the change, 0 new reds (the one pre-existing `threadTokenMint` failure is in both). Integration lane 6 files / 104 cells, all pass.
* Pre-push hook: 13 of 16 legs ran, 3 skipped (3, 4 and 8 need a local stack), nothing failed; shell suites 98 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (ks949: no PostgreSQL binaries on this host). That is not a pass of the skipped legs.

**Known gaps (deliberate).**
1. A flat anchor stays readable by any authenticated caller: the row records no owner (needs KS 1384's tenant column).
2. A caller with no usable tenant claim is allowed (the KS 1652 hole): platform admins, and connector keys whose metadata has no tenant.

KS-1814.desc:
**BLUF:** Surface: originate `POST /api/documents/:id/anchor`, the retry route. I read the route and every layer in front of and behind it at develop `6d41673e0f79`. The only gates are authentication (a Bearer token and an active session), tenant scoping, and the refusal "Document is already anchored". There is no role gate, no owner check and no terminal-status guard. So any authenticated user in the tenant, including the public-signup `OWNER` role, which the share and transfer-custody gates exclude by design (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:24-27`), can make originate call the anchoring service for a document whose blob is missing or `anchor_failed`; on success the route writes `status: 'anchored'` over the document, revoked or deleted ones included. This is a source reading. I ran no request against any box and did not execute the route.

**Route** (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, `:1437-1571`):

* `:1442` `getUserFromRequest` and a 401 when absent; `:1449` `getDocument(id, tenantId, req.db)` and a 404 when the document is not found in the caller's tenant.
* `:1458` the only state check: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored". A document with no blob at all passes it.
* `:1474-1478` it calls `${ANCHORING_SERVICE_URL}/api/anchors` with the caller's own `Authorization` header; `:1489` the body carries `...anchorIdentityFields(req.body)`, so the caller's request body supplies the identity fields (the comment above it, `:1488`, is "the re-anchor path carries S's identity too").
* `:1534-1537` `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { blockchain, status: 'anchored' })` with no options; `:1545` starts the confirmation poll; `:1560` answers 202.
* Within `:1437-1571` there is none of `ALLOWED_*_ROLES`, `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES`, `hasAnyRole`, `requireRole`, `requireSelfOrRole` or `requireScope` (census of the file below).

**Siblings in the same file:** `POST /` (`:373`, `ALLOWED_CREATION_ROLES`), `transfer-custody` (`:1789`, `ALLOWED_TRANSFER_CUSTODY_ROLES`, declared `:1782`), `version` (`:2263`, `:2258`), `share` (`:2464`, `:2458`), `sign-cert` (`:2936`) and `sign-wallet` (`:3204`) each check a constant built from `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` (`middleware/documentWriteRoles.ts:37`: `ISSUER_ADMIN`, `ORG_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`; the file says at `:24` that `OWNER` is deliberately absent). `revoke` (`:2650`) is owner-only: `if (document.owner?.id !== user.id)` then 403 "Only the owner can revoke this document" (`:2677-2679`). The token census finds no gate in `sign`, `sign/request` or the lifecycle-events routes; I did not read whether they have another kind of check, so this ticket does not claim the retry route is the only route without one. W 7th's comparison, `GET /:id` (`:1078-1217`), is not a role gate either: its matches are the admin cross-tenant fallback terms.

**Layers in front** (read):

* originate `index.ts`: gateway provenance (`:219`), emitter-marker strip (`:223`), the multi-tenancy block (`:226-244`), request tenant resolution (`:259-262`) and `tenantGucContext()` (`:263`). They establish where a request came from and which tenant it is in; none checks a role or an owner.
* `documentsRouter.use(authenticate())` (`documents.ts:175`). `authenticate()` (`middleware/auth.ts:82-137`) verifies the RS256 token and the session; it sets the user and checks no role.
* api-gateway `routes/proxy.ts:657`: `requireScope('documents:read', 'documents:write')` on the whole `/api/documents` mount. `middleware/scopes.ts:34-36` lets JWT and email users straight through ("controlled by RBAC, not scopes"), and `:51` passes an OAuth or API-key caller on ANY ONE of the listed scopes or `*`, with no distinction by method. A search of the gateway's non-test source for `documents:write` and for a method-aware scope check found none for this path. Whether an OAuth or API-key principal reaches originate in a form originate accepts, I did not read (`utils/originateForward.ts`).

**Layer behind** (read): anchoring `index.ts:469` is `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, authentication only. `POST /api/anchors` (`:475`) has no role gate; the only role reference near it is the connector branch (`:554`). [KS-1603](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1603/security-pre-existing-anchoring-post-apianchors-never-checks-who-owns) already tracks that anchoring does not check who owns `documentId`.

**Terminal status** (read): `documentRepo.ts:598` and `:621-622` make the status write `WHEN preserveTerminal AND status IN ('revoked','deleted') THEN status ELSE <new>`, and `preserveTerminalStatuses` defaults to false (documented at `:520-534`, KS-521: the async anchor pipeline "stomped a revoked set by the owner ... so a revoked document verified again"). The create path passes it (`documents.ts:1015`, `:1038`); the retry route does not. `revoke` writes the status only (`documents.ts:2705`), so a revoked document whose blob is absent or `anchor_failed` satisfies the route's entry condition.

**Cost, as logged:** each accepted anchor logs a submission with a fee. Seat D 42nd's demo log shows `"Anchor submitted to Cardano"` with `"fee":179449` (lovelace) in `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatD-42nd/evidence/demo/moved_logs.txt`. Whose wallet pays on each box, I did not verify here.

**Real callers:** Platform S uses this route in its normal flow; KS-1688's comment of 2026-10-19 describes "the anchor kick that follows it (`POST /{newId}/anchor`)" signed with the owning organisation's connector key. Any gate has to keep that principal working; `transfer-custody` shows one shape (a write role OR a scope, documented at `documents.ts:1589-1591`). I am not proposing the fix.

**Not run, not read:** no request to any box; the route was not executed; cross-tenant behaviour beyond the tenant-scoped `getDocument` and the RLS context was not exercised; the gateway's API-key and OAuth path into originate; `sign`, `sign/request` and the lifecycle-events routes, which show no role token.

**Evidence:**

* Source: develop `6d41673e0f79c0f02c2ec7b893cc960b6fa3ec10`, the files named above.
* Seat W 7th's section 16, item 9 (and item 10, the revival): `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-7th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev2.md`, lines 496 and 497. Its claim was a lexical count "not verified against upstream middleware"; this ticket is that verification.
* My route census and reads: `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatR-61st/filings/board_search_i.txt` for the board search.

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 17 hits, a random token 0 hits): `documents.ts:1437` 0 hits; "/:id/anchor" 6 hits and "POST /api/documents/:id/anchor" 4 hits, read: [KS-1557](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1557/security-a-write-role-caller-can-make-another-organisations-bytes) (quotes the route name inside an error message), [KS-1385](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1385/ks-1175-follow-on-the-anchors-k-emits-for-share-transfer-custody) (lists the route among six sites that forward identity), [KS-520](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-520/anchoring-fabricates-a-tx-sim-hash-and-marks-the-document-anchored), KS-319, KS-535, KS-566 (archived, other defects); `anchorIdentityFields` 1 hit ([KS-1709](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1709/originate-the-certification-issue-route-swallows-a-non-ok-response), other defect); `DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES` 10 hits, read by title: [KS-1688](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1688/security-post-apidocumentsidversion-has-no-per-document-access-check) is the same class on `POST /:id/version` (a missing per-document check on the source document), KS-547 (archived) is a decision about `/certifications/issue`; `preserveTerminalStatuses` 5 hits: KS-1424's table of unguarded `updateDocument` callers lists `documents.ts:1408` and the sync writers, not this route's call at `:1534`. No ticket names this route's missing gate or its missing terminal-status guard.

**Related:** [KS-1688](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1688/security-post-apidocumentsidversion-has-no-per-document-access-check) (same class, the version route), [KS-1603](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1603/security-pre-existing-anchoring-post-apianchors-never-checks-who-owns) (the anchoring side), [KS-485](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-k) (the security review plan).

KS-1717.desc:
**Ask:** give the anchoring service a guard against a caller setting `x-emitter-internal` itself, and correct the comment above it in the same change.

**What the gate found (note N1 of the #995 verdict):** the marker means "this is K's own originate-to-anchoring hop for an operation that already wrote its own provenance row", and anchoring skips `recordFlatAnchorProvenance` when it is present (`Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts`, `const isInternalEmit = typeof req.headers['x-emitter-internal'] === 'string'`, line 531 on develop `a9ce2cff1594`). #995 (merged, KS-741) strips the marker at originate's own inbound. **Anchoring has no inbound strip of its own.** The gate, verbatim: *"Anchoring has no inbound strip; its middleware is helmet, cors, json, rejectNulBytes, requestLogger, then jwtAuthenticate.* `docker-compose.yml` *treats anchoring exactly as it treats originate: both are on the flat network with host ports unpublished (*`:1286` *vs* `:557`*). That is the same exposure the PR uses to justify the originate strip. So a direct compose-network caller holding a connector JWT can set the marker and suppress its own flat-anchor provenance row. This is pre-existing and not introduced by this PR."*

**The comment over-claims.** Lines 519-530 (the KS-566 block) say the header "is not spoofable, by two strips" and that *"the only value that can arrive here is one originate itself set on its outbound hop"*. That holds only for paths through the gateway or originate. #995 left that wording in place (it edited the comment to name the originate strip). The gate: *"Reword the comment, or open a ticket for an anchoring-side guard."* This is that ticket; fix the comment in the same change as the guard.

**Design caution, my reading and not the gate's:** a plain strip at anchoring's inbound would also delete the legitimate marker originate sets on its own hop, so the guard has to tell the two apart (honour the marker only on a request that carries something only originate can present), not just drop the header. Whoever picks this up should settle that first.

**Also from the same gate (note N3, minor):** #995's cell C6 checks the strip's mount order only against `/api/anchors`. A move to between `/api/documents` (`originate/src/index.ts` lines 275-276, which also builds a marked hop) and `/api/anchors` would still pass C6. Today the order is correct. Worth one more cell when the order is next touched.

**Related, read and not a duplicate:** KS-1603 (In Progress, anchoring `POST /api/anchors` never checks who owns `documentId`) records in one bullet that `x-emitter-internal` "is trusted by mere presence" and that "any peer on the compose network can send it". That is the same exposure seen from the ownership ticket; it proposes no fix for the marker and does not touch the over-claiming comment. This ticket owns the marker guard and the comment. (KS-1603's bullet says originate sets the marker at one call site; the gate found two setters, `originate/src/routes/documents.ts` lines 878 and 1375.)

**Impact, as the gate framed it:** a caller on the compose network with a connector JWT can suppress its own flat-anchor provenance row; it needs network position and a valid credential.

Source: QA gate DA5, tier 1, round 1 (verdict `2026-10-23_gate-DA5-pr989-995-tier1/verdict.md`, sha256/16 of the body `be2f26d014ae8997`). Quoted from the verdict; **not re-measured by the seat that filed this.**

KS-1695.desc:
## BLUF

**Two pre-existing read gaps in** `services/originate`**, both measured on real Postgres 15 as** `secuura_app` **(NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS) by gate BX1 while gating PR #1659.** Facts only — **no fix is proposed here**, because the remedy is a design on an auth read path and is ruled before it is built.

1. `GET /api/certifications/:id` **has no owner, holder or org check at all.** A **human-issued** certification that the documents GET *does* cloak is served **200 to every same-tenant user of any organisation**.
2. **An empty owner skips the documents cloak.** `documentRepo.ts:176` derives `''` from `owner_user_id` NULL + `issuer_user_id` NULL, and `documents.ts:1124`'s conjunction is false on `''`, so the 404 cloak never runs. Affects **bare-connector documents** (on `develop` today) and, since `3cc46ae41fed`, **holder-less connector certifications**.

Neither was introduced by PR #1659. KS-1659's fold added a new **row type** to gap 2's existing class, not a new audience, and the gate's control proves it.

## ⚠ This falsifies KS-621's central premise for one row class

KS-621 is the tracking ticket for "document reads are scoped by tenant and owner, never by organization", and it states: *"**Nothing is leaking.** Cross-org document reads are denied today, and that was proved with a control... What actually denies the read is a **per-owner 404-cloak**."* **That cloak does not run when the owner is empty.** For owner-less rows the emergent cross-org protection KS-621 describes is therefore **absent, not merely unenforced**. A comment has been left on KS-621 pointing here.

## Measured audiences (gate BX1)

**a** = same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN`, same organisation · **a2** = same-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN`, **another** organisation · **b** = another tenant · **c** = the issuing connector.

| row | tree | endpoint | a | a2 | b | c |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| connector certification, no holder | landing | `GET /api/documents/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |
| **bare-connector** `POST /api/documents` (owner NULL, issuer NULL) | **develop AND landing** | `GET /api/documents/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |
| human-issued certification, no holder (owner = issuer = a UUID) | both | `GET /api/documents/:id` | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 |
| **human-issued certification** | **develop AND landing** | `GET /api/certifications/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | — |
| connector certification, no holder | landing | `GET /api/certifications/:id` | **200** | **200** | 404 | **200** |

The owner-less 200 body carries `"owner":{"id":""}` plus title, data and contentHash. The human-certification row being 404 on the documents path is the **positive control**: the cloak works when the owner is non-empty, so these 200s are not "everything is readable".

**Audience for the owner-less class: the whole tenant, every organisation, all roles.** ⚠ **Kam's KS-1116 ruling — owner-less rows readable by the row tenant's administrators (**`ORG_ADMIN` **/** `SYSTEM_ADMIN` **with a tenant on the token) — is NARROWER than what ships today for both row types.**

**List endpoints are not affected:** `documents.ts:321` filters on `d.owner?.id === userId` and the certifications list filters on holder or issuer id. Only **c** saw the new id in a list.

## Where

* **Gap 1:** `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:956-1010` — calls `getCertification(id, tenantId)` and returns issuer, holder, data and blockchain with no access predicate.
* **Gap 2:** `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:176` → `id: row.owner_user_id || row.issuer_user_id || ''`; `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1124` → `if (userId && document.owner?.id && document.owner.id !== userId && !isAdmin && !isRecipient)`.

## The remedy shapes BX1 costed — options, NOT a decision

1. **Fail the cloak closed at** `documents.ts:1124` (drop the `document.owner?.id &&` conjunct). One line, covers both row types. **Cost, measured: it strands the issuing connector.** A bare connector create writes **no** `create` **row in** `action_provenance` (0 rows against 12 documents), so `wasCreatedByConnector` never admits it, and per the KS-480 §6 comment at `:1126` Platform S drives the whole lifecycle through that id. Needs a companion — record a create row, or admit a connector whose organisation matches the row's. **Does nothing for gap 1.**
2. **Cloak an empty owner to admins plus the creating connector** — the KS-1116 ruling shape. Same edit plus a tenant-admin admit; same provenance dependency; does not cover gap 1.
3. **Set the owner at write time** from the connector's organisation or a tenant administrator. Reads unchanged, but it changes custody semantics (`anchorOverwriteGuard`), needs a write-path lookup, and does nothing for existing bare-connector rows.
4. **Refuse a holder-less connector certification** (400 `HOLDER_REQUIRED`). Smallest blast radius; returns to develop's "no row" with an honest error instead of 22P02-as-payload. A **client-visible contract change for Platform S**, and the bare-document class stays as it is.
5. **For gap 1: give** `GET /api/certifications/:id` **the same predicate** as `documents.ts:1124`. **Without it, options 1 and 2 do not close certification reads.**

**Plan against Kam's KS-1116 ruling**, which is the nearest precedent: a remedy matching that audience inherits his authority; a different audience is a new decision for him.

## Not measured

No gateway and no real JWT layer — BX1 mounted the routers directly with the repo's probe-user auth mock, so **any scope gating at api-gateway is unmeasured** and could narrow these audiences in production. Also not run: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, a `system_admin` or recipient reader, an `onBehalfOf` connector certification, the derived lineage row. The remedies were not built.

## Board search before filing

`owner_user_id` (control: 9 hits), "GET /api/certifications/:id ownership check", "certifications read no ownership check same tenant", "documents.ts cloak empty owner", "owner-less document readable by same tenant", "bare connector document no owner". **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0**; `owner_user_id` returned 9. Nearest neighbours: **KS-621** (the tracking ticket whose premise this corrects), **KS-1688** (the same class on `POST /api/documents/:id/version`, a different endpoint), KS-1603/KS-1652 (anchoring ownership), KS-1683/KS-1684 (vc-issuer reads). **None owns these two endpoints.**

Related KS-1659, KS-1116, KS-621.

## Round 2 pushed — PR #1667 at `c502c6434cf299d09b47b7b0ca354338f5892410`

Gate CF1 returned **GO WITH NOTE** on round 1 (0 blockers, 5 notes) and round 2 was ruled. The two notes that were code are closed; the rest are recorded as residue on the PR.

**N2 was a regression I introduced, and the measurement is the point.** Round 1 hand-wrote the admit set by copying the certification list route's literal `isAdmin` (`certifications.ts:906`), which **omits `SUPER_ADMIN`** — so a real platform administrator went from 200 to **404**. It now calls **`isPlatformRole`** (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:140`), the repo's single definition of a platform role, which upper-cases the claim so both casings of `SYSTEM_ADMIN` and `SUPER_ADMIN` pass.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| develop, no check at all | **21 failed / 15 passed** — every refusal cell red, and all four admin spellings **200** |
| round 1, hand-written set | **2 failed / 34 passed** — exactly the `SUPER_ADMIN` cells, nothing else |
| round 2, `isPlatformRole` | **37 / 37** |

Two consequences stated rather than hidden: for `SUPER_ADMIN` this by-id read is now **more permissive than the list route**, which keeps its narrower literal set — recorded, not resolved; and **`platform_admin` stays refused**, pinned by a cell named as a known accepted difference. That spelling was 200 on develop (no check existed). It is a gateway-only spelling — 6 non-test sites, all under `services/api-gateway`, **zero** in originate and **zero** in `packages/shared` (control: `super_admin` matches 20 files) — so admitting it here would make this route originate's first and only site for it. Recorded on KS 1536, which already is that ticket.

**N3** adds the cells the gate's own mutants found: no share lookup for a refused reader on **both** sibling reads, and an **exact** issuer compare, so upper-cased, prefix, suffix and whitespace variants of the issuer id are all refused — with a control proving the exact id is 200 so the cell can fail.

**Evidence.** Whole `services/originate` suite **136 files / 1,613 tests / 0 failed**; baseline **135 / 1,575 / 0**, so +37 is exactly this PR's cells with 0 vanished. **9 mutants, 9 killed**, each type-checked clean first and each killing a named cell by assertion — including the gate's own two. Predicted landing tree `8d61d5a1595680848790aa6337fa0e4cd4531721` against develop `c3ea4dc79af72f62ad7f211d1dbf8b9920ea094d`, two independent derivations agreeing.

**Not a pass, and not quoted as one:** the pre-push preflight reported `PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.` on both pushes — legs 3, 4 and 8 skipped for want of a local stack. The four platform suites were not run (no Docker on the build host), and nothing was exercised through a real gateway or real Postgres.

**Residue carried on the PR, not closed here:** the three ungated certification **write** routes (KS 1699); the stale E2E transfer spec (KS 1697); Stuart's Platform S statement, which is reported and not measured; and the fact that adopting `isPlatformRole` also adopts **KS 1591** — its `toUpperCase` admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as `SUPER_ADMIN`, which round 1's literal set would not have. I did not pin those three as admitted, deliberately: a green cell asserting a spoofable spelling is accepted would turn a KS 1591 fix into a test failure.

This ticket stays open: gap 2 (owner-less documents) is unbuilt and waits on Kam's card.

## Gap 1 is MERGED — `88933d5c7ebbb0af6ba1a1d4504998d581ba66c0`, tree `58849ee421ba16a6c7f8d2fb8e363d143653eced`, one parent `f418cddac51498adda34cfed0bf5486a2d8cca77`

**This ticket stays open.** The PR says `Refs`, never `Closes`: gap 2 (owner-less documents) is unbuilt.

**What shipped.** All three by-id certification reads — `GET /api/certifications/:id`, `GET /:id/lineage`, `GET /:id/evidence-bundle` — are now bound on the record by one shared helper: a **platform administrator** (via `isPlatformRole`, the repo's single definition), the **issuer**, or the **holder**. An empty principal never matches, so a bare-connector row whose issuer and holder both map to `''` is not open to everyone. The refusal is emitted by the same function as the unknown-id 404, so the two bodies cannot drift and a refused reader cannot tell "not yours" from "no such certification". The check precedes **every** side effect that used to run for a refused reader: the expiry write (and the `certification_events` row it writes), the `evidence_export` **charge event**, and the **share lookup** on both sibling reads.

**The gap this closes, in gate BX1's measured words:** **every same-tenant user of ANY organisation** read 200 — **a** (same tenant, same organisation) and **a2** (same tenant, another organisation) both 200; **b** (another tenant) 404; **c** (the issuing connector) 200 on a connector certification. Measured readers were **`ISSUER_ADMIN` only**; "all roles" was an inference from source, not a measurement.

**Kept working, deliberately:** the issuing connector still reads its own holder-less certification, the issuer keeps both sibling reads (the issuer UI calls them), another tenant is still 404, an allowed reader of an expired certification still gets the expiry write, and an allowed bundle reader is still billed.

**Evidence.** Whole `services/originate` suite **136 files / 1,613 tests / 0 failed** (baseline 135 / 1,575 / 0, so +37 is exactly this PR's cells, 0 vanished). Red-proof against develop's route blob: **22 failed / 15 passed / 37**. Against the first round's own helper: **3 failed / 34 passed** — that round had introduced a regression, refusing a platform administrator whose token says `SUPER_ADMIN`, and the 3 reds are what proved it. **9 mutants, 9 killed**, each type-checked clean first and each killing a named cell by assertion, including both mutants the review gate wrote itself.

**Two differences from develop we accept knowingly, both recorded rather than smoothed over:**
- For `SUPER_ADMIN` this by-id read is **more permissive than the certification list route**, which keeps its narrower literal set. Recorded, not resolved.
- A token whose role is **`platform_admin` now reads 404** where develop answered 200 (develop had no check at all). Ruled deliberately: originate recognises that spelling in no predicate of its own. An earlier draft of mine called it "gateway-only" — **that was wrong**: auth mints it verbatim from the `platform_admins` row and the column permits it. The narrower truth is that the table is created empty on purpose and the column defaults to `super_admin`. Recorded on [KS-1536](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1536).

**Residue, carried openly:**
- An exact **holder** compare is **unpinned** — a case-insensitive holder mutant survives all 37 cells. `R17` pins the issuer compare only.
- Adopting `isPlatformRole` also adopts [KS-1591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1591): its `toUpperCase` admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as `SUPER_ADMIN`. Reachability rests on reading code; no live token was decoded.
- The same class on the **write** verbs of this router is [KS-1699](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1699) (High): `POST /:id/verify`, `/:id/share` and `/:id/recertify` have no per-record access check, while `/:id/revoke` checks the issuer.
- A transferee reading by id is [KS-1697](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1697).
- Platform S reading with a non-issuer key remains **reported, not measured** — Stuart's statement from S's code, which this project's token cannot read.
- The four platform suites were not run (no Docker on the build host) and the pre-push preflight reported `13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED` on every push; nothing was exercised through a real gateway or real Postgres.

## Correction to my own earlier comment on this ticket

**I claimed, in this thread and three other places, that *"originate recognises `platform_admin` in no predicate of its own"*. It does.**

```
services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:60
  const SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES = ['super_admin', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'platform_admin'];
services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:78      (inside resolveTenantId)
  if (u?.role && SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES.includes(u.role)) {
```

**Used, not dead.** `resolveTenantId` gives a caller in that set cross-tenant tenant resolution (`req.tenantId`, then `?organizationId`, then the user's own org), where a tenant-bound admin gets only its own organisation.

**The instrument that produced the false claim, named.** My original census was `grep -rn "platform_admin" services packages | head -20`. The run had **41** non-test lines; `head` cut it at 20 and originate's fell below the cut. *A count that passes through `head` is a count of what fitted, not of what matched* — and I repeated it four times without re-running it. This is one hop further out than the lesson I cited in my previous correction here: that one was a census keyed on a string literal missing a value from a DB column; this one is a census whose **output was truncated**.

**Untruncated, per service** (non-test lines, `git grep` at develop `88933d5c7ebb`) — **41 total**: auth 21, api-gateway 7, **originate 4**, packages/shared 3, anchoring 3, tokenisation 1, security 1, m365-integration 1. Excluding references to the `platform_admins` **table**, which are not a role value: api-gateway 7, **originate 4**, auth 3, anchoring 3, packages/shared 2, tokenisation 1, security 1. Three of originate's four are the RLS bypass sentinel `app.tenant_scope_bypass = 'platform_admin'` (`db.ts:167`, `db.ts:191`, a comment at `documents.ts:1916`) and are **not** role claims; the fourth is `adminConfig.ts:60`.

**What changes and what does not.** The **outcome** — `platform_admin` refused on the three by-id certification reads — is unchanged; it stays Wednesday's ruling (a), and Kam now holds a card carrying the corrected facts. What is corrected is the **basis**, which was a fact I supplied. And the real inconsistency is sharper than the gateway-versus-originate one I described: **inside originate**, the same token is a super-admin for tenant resolution and a stranger to its own certification reads.

**Not measured:** no live token was decoded, and I have not shown that any real principal carries this role.

Also filed from this census: **KS 1701** — four originate sites hand-write the platform-admin role set and all four omit `SUPER_ADMIN` (`documents.ts:1076` and `:299`, `certifications.ts:959` and `:123`), which is the same omission that caused the measured regression caught in this ticket's round 2.

KS-762.desc:
## BLUF

`APP_DB_PASSWORD` **is committed as a literal** `:-` **default in** `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` **— 51 times.** A fresh volume bakes it in, and it is the password behind ~20 service connection strings. Split out of [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) (Review E, row E-1) so it can be fixed without dragging the whole review stream.

## Measured, not relayed

Against `develop` `541acae81` (2026-09-03):

```
literal  APP_DB_PASSWORD:-YuBz…  defaults : 51
control  any APP_DB_PASSWORD reference  : 53
```

So **51 of 53** references carry the committed literal. The value begins `YuBzECVdrAU9…` and is 32 characters.

**The Review E register understates this: it says "~20 connection strings".** The true figure is 51 sites. Recording that because a fixer sizing the change off the register would plan for a third of the work.

## Why it matters, stated precisely

It is a **local-dev** compose file, not production — that is the honest framing and it is why this is High and not Urgent. But:

* It is a real credential in a public-ish repo's history. Removing the default does not un-commit it; the value is in git history from whenever it landed, so the fix is **remove the default AND rotate**, not just remove.
* `:-` means the literal is the *fallback*, so any environment that has not set `APP_DB_PASSWORD` silently runs on the committed value. That includes a fresh clone, which is the common case for a new team member.
* The same file binds Postgres to `127.0.0.1` (E-4, now fixed), so the exposure is loopback — but a container on the same host is not on loopback-only terms with it.

## Done when

1. No literal `:-<secret>` default remains in `docker-compose.yml` — the variable is required, and the stack fails loudly if it is unset rather than falling back.
2. The value is rotated, and `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` documents the new variable.
3. **Stuart and Peter are told before it merges** — this is the one change here with a team cost: their local stacks will need `APP_DB_PASSWORD` set, and a stack that "fails loudly" will fail loudly for them first. That is a batched-notify item, not a surprise.

## Not done here, and why

I have not made this change tonight. It is a one-file edit, but requirement 3 makes it a coordination item rather than a quiet fix, and requirement 2 (rotation) touches a credential — @kam's call on both the timing and whether rotation is in scope for a local-dev password.

Filed from session 111 during the KS-490 ACTION-row pass. Searched first: no existing open ticket (`title contains "APP_DB_PASSWORD"` → 1, KS-8, **Done** and about a different defect in `01-create-app-role.sh`; `"committed credential"` → 0; `"compose password"` → 0; control `"password"` → 8, so the query discriminates).

## RULED — Kam, 2026-09-03 16:23 (via Wednesday's card `secuura-ks762-required-switch-2026-09-03`): KEEP THE DEFAULTS

No `:?required` switch. The `${APP_DB_PASSWORD:-<literal>}` fallbacks stay, so no local stack and no fresh clone breaks. **The rotation on 2026-09-05 09:00 is Kam's deploy step and is the half that actually retires the credential** — the switch is re-raised *after* that rotation, with a notice to Peter and Stuart.

This matches what was built: **commit `d82994b05`, local, unpushed** (develop's push gate is red for every author until #797 lands). It contains only the half that is safe either way:

- `env.example` **and** `.env.example` now document `APP_DB_PASSWORD` — it appeared in neither, which is how it came to be relied on as a committed literal rather than set. **Both files are tracked and are NOT the same file, and `.env.example` is the one `scripts/bootstrap-env.sh` reads and copies**, so a developer on the supported path would never have seen documentation added only to the other. (That the two tracked example files disagree is its own latent problem; not fixed here.)
- One trap nobody had written down: **on an existing stack, setting a new value breaks auth**, because `01-create-app-role.sh` bakes the role password into the volume at first init and never re-reads it. Recreate the volume or `ALTER` the role; on a fresh clone, just set it.
- `scripts/check-app-db-password-default.sh` — the red-proof, written now so the day the switch is re-raised it is a one-line change with a gate already waiting. It reports **which state** the tree is in and fails on an incoherent one: both forms present → FAIL (a half-applied switch has services starting on two different passwords); only `:-` → the state today, reported as an exposure and explicitly **not** a pass; only `:?` → the real gate (config must fail without the variable and resolve with it); neither → FAIL.

**Current output:** `52 committed-literal fallback(s), 0 required-form(s)` → HELD, exit 0.

Two bugs of mine, both caught by that checker failing — which is the only reason its FAIL arms can be claimed to work. The first predicate was "any `:-` form", which counted two safe sites (`01-create-app-role.sh` defaults to EMPTY then FATALs — the KS-8 guardrail; `pgbouncer/entrypoint.sh` falls back to another variable) plus my own prose, and reported a half-applied switch that did not exist. The exclusion then anchored `$` inside an alternation against `git grep -c` output, where every path is followed by `:<count>`, so it could never fire. Both fixed; the predicate is now the *shape* of a literal fallback, expressed without the secret so the checker never carries the credential it looks for.

Written by s137 (2026-09-06) on Wednesday's item-0(b) sweep of rulings made 2026-09-03/04 that carry no delivered mark. **Nothing here is executed** — both entries are records, and the second is a deliberate non-action.

**Kam's option, verbatim: `agent-rotates` = "Authorise the Secuura agent to run down --volumes on slot 1 + the regeneration (a one-off Docker grant, scoped to slot 1 only)".**

So the execution is evidenced, but it is evidenced **as a side remark inside a different ticket's measurement note**. Anyone auditing this grant from KS-762 alone would find nothing. That is what this comment fixes.

**Provenance:** Wednesday's s137 successor brief, 2026-09-05T21:53:00Z (SPF + DKIM `header.i=@agentmail.to` + DMARC pass), item 0(b), cards 2 and 8. Option text copied from the card store, not paraphrased.

## I did not make this change, and I think that is correct — all three conditions are @kam's

Picked this up as the next bounded P2 and stopped before editing, because the fix is **explicitly
held by a standing in-code instruction**, not merely undecided.

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:129-132` (KS-165):

> *"The defaults are intentionally kept so `docker compose up` works out-of-the-box — **do NOT switch
> to `:?required`** (it would break the team's existing local stacks, and a fresh volume bakes the DB
> password at first init)."*

And `scripts/check-app-db-password-default.sh` already says the same in its header: the required-form

So condition 1 is not "not yet done", it is **ruled not-to-be-done pending a decision**. Making it
would have overridden an instruction written into the file I was editing. Conditions 2 (rotation, a
credential) and 3 (tell Stuart and Peter, external comms) were already @kam's. **That is the whole
ticket.**

## What I did instead — three corrections, all measured at `306d0db92`

**1. The site count in this ticket is slightly wrong, and my own first count was worse.**

| source | figure | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Review E register | "~20 connection strings" | understates badly |
| this ticket | **51**, in `docker-compose.yml` | misses one file |
| my first sweep | 60 across 6 files | **wrong — I over-counted** |
| **actual** | **52** — `docker-compose.yml` 51 + `scripts/rls/verify-fail-closed.sh` 1 | matches the guard |

My 60 came from grepping `APP_DB_PASSWORD:-`, which also matches `${APP_DB_PASSWORD:-}` (the bare
"is it unset?" idiom at `docker/init/01-create-app-role.sh:32`), `${APP_DB_PASSWORD:-${DB_PASS}}`
(`docker/pgbouncer/entrypoint.sh:24`, falling back to a *variable*), and a comment in `env.example`.
**None of those carries the secret.** I found this by reading the lines instead of trusting the count
— and the existing guard's narrower pattern was right all along.

**2. The rotation date has LAPSED.** The guard prints *"Rotation is scheduled 2026-09-05 09:00."*
Today is **2026-09-07** — **two days past**, and the literal is unchanged. Whatever the ruling on the
`:?` switch, the scheduled rotation appears to have slipped silently and nothing is failing because of
it. That is the actionable item on this ticket right now.

**3. This surface is not unguarded, which lowers the urgency.**
`check-app-db-password-default.sh` is **one of only three `check-*.sh` guards reachable from a live
entry point** ([KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926)'s census) — invoked at
`start-local.sh:90` and `start-environment.sh:118`, so it runs on every local stack start. It passes
today (rc 0) while reporting the HELD state explicitly rather than calling it clean.

Its coherence rule also matters for how the fix must land: **both forms present → FAIL**, because a
half-applied switch means some services demand the variable and others silently fall back, so the
stack half-starts on two different passwords. **This cannot be done incrementally** — it is one atomic
change on the day it is ruled.

## What @kam needs to decide

1. **The `:?` switch** — it breaks every existing local stack and every fresh clone until each person
   sets `APP_DB_PASSWORD`. That is the team cost KS-165 protects against, and it is a batched-notify
   item for Stuart and Peter, not a surprise.
2. **The rotation** — scheduled for 2026-09-05, now 2 days lapsed.
3. **Whether rotation is even in scope** for a local-dev password whose exposure is loopback, given
   the value is already in git history from `1305bbda9` so removing the default does not un-commit it.

The day 1 is ruled, the guard becomes the gate with no edit beyond removing the fallbacks themselves —
which is what it was built for.

**Moving to Blocked** rather than leaving it In Progress: nothing here is waiting on engineering.

KS-753.desc:
## BLUF

`POST /api/timestamps` and `POST /api/timestamps/batch` return **201 with** `verified: true` when the RFC-3161 call fails and the code falls back to a locally-generated mock token. On an evidentiary write path that is the wrong default: **extend KS-523's fail-closed treatment so a mock fallback cannot be reported as a verified timestamp.**

Found by @PeterObeden while re-measuring [KS-740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-740) against a working TSA — **6 of 360 requests (~1.7%)** fell back (5 × `TSA rejected the request (status=2)`, 1 × `fetch failed`), each returning 201 / `verified: true`. **Pre-existing; not KS-740's doing and not PR #787's.**

## Recommendation

A batch or single entry whose TSA call fell back to a mock must not carry `verified: true`. Preferred shape: reuse the KS-523 path that already exists rather than invent a second one — the machinery is built and proven, it is simply opt-in today.

Open design question for the ruling: **refuse the write (503, as** `requireEidas` **does today) or persist it with** `verified: false`**?** The batch case argues for the second — refusing one entry of 100 because one TSA call was rejected is a worse outcome than recording it honestly as unverified. Recommend `verified: false` per entry for the batch path and keeping the 503 for `requireEidas: true`.

## Detail — reproduced on `develop`, not taken from the report

Measured on `develop` `348623b0d`, local stack. The running container's `dist/` carries **0** occurrences of `BATCH_TSA_CONCURRENCY` and **0** of `AbortSignal.timeout`, so **none of #787's code is in the path**. `TSA_URL` / `TSA_AUTH_KEY` / `TSA_NAME` are all length 0 in the container (controls: `PATH` 60, `ZZZ_NOT_SET` 0), so every request takes the fallback.

`POST /api/timestamps` **(**`timestampType: rfc3161`**) → HTTP 201:**

| field | value |
| -- | -- |
| `verified` | `true` |
| `eidasQualified` | `false` |
| `tsaName` | `"D-Trust GmbH (mock)"` |
| `proof[0]` | `0x7b` — `{`. An ASN.1 DER SEQUENCE is `0x30` |
| decoded proof | `{…, "provider":"D-Trust GmbH", "type":"rfc3161", "mock":true}` |

`POST /api/timestamps/batch`**, 2 entries** — both identical to the above.

**Control (same endpoint, same TSA state, one field added):**

```
{"…","requireEidas":true}  →  HTTP 503 QUALIFIED_TSA_UNAVAILABLE
"requireEidas: no eIDAS-qualified TSA is reachable — refusing to fall back to a mock token"
```

The control is the point: **the fail-closed path already exists on this exact code path and works.** The only thing separating a silent mock from a refusal is whether the caller opted in.

### Where it is

* `services/timestamping/src/tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:301-327` — the mock fallback. It is **honestly labelled**: `eidasQualified: false`, a `(mock)`-suffixed `tsaName`, `"mock": true` inside the token. Nothing lies.
* `services/timestamping/src/index.ts:466` — `verified: true, // Mock timestamps are pre-verified`. **Unconditional**, for every timestamp type. This is the field a relying party reads first, and it is the one that does not carry the signal.
* `services/timestamping/src/index.ts:445-452` — the KS-523 fail-closed block. Fires only on `data.requireEidas`.

### Why now, and the link to #787

#787's new 5 s per-request deadline is a **new trigger** for this pre-existing fallback: a TSA that is merely slow now aborts and lands in the mock path, which returns `success: true` and logs at `info`. The bound is correct and should ship — but it widens the mouth of a funnel that was already silent. That is an argument for this ticket, not against #787.

### Fix shape

1. Carry the fallback signal to the caller: `verified: false` when the token is a mock on an `rfc3161` request (the mock-only types `opentimestamps` / `blockchain` keep today's semantics — they are mock by design, not by failure).
2. Red-proof: force a fallback (dead `TSA_URL`, or a `status=2` rejection) and assert `verified === false` on both the single and batch routes.
3. Positive control that must stay green: a real DER token still returns `verified: true`. Without this the fix is indistinguishable from hard-coding `false`.
4. Persisted rows carry the same signal — `ts_timestamps.verified` is written from the same value (`index.ts:489`), so a GET must answer consistently.

## Related

* KS-523 — the fail-closed precedent this extends.
* KS-740 — where it was found; reproduction and the control are in [comment a3a94d04](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-740#comment-a3a94d04>).
* The sibling class, same service, **not** this ticket: `verifyTimestamp` (`qualified-tsa.ts:443`) returns `isQualified: true` as a **literal** for every real DER token with an extractable signer certificate — no policy-OID or QcStatements read exists anywhere in the service (`policyOid` is request-side only, `rfc3161-client.ts:119-125`). @PeterObeden offered to raise that one.

*Filed by the Platform K agent, 2026-09-02, session 109. Probe rows labelled* `KS-740-s109-*` *in local* `ts_timestamps` *— no demo write, no chain write.*

KS-734.desc:
## BLUF

**The e2e Playwright suite cannot run from a clean checkout**, and that is why "Playwright — not run" keeps appearing in Test Evidence blocks. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` is **not a workspace member**, has its own `package-lock.json`, and nothing installs it — so `npx playwright test` dies at collection with `Cannot find module 'otplib'` and **the entire run aborts, including the specs that would have passed**.

Once you clear that by hand, **20 of 82 tests fail** on a healthy local stack. Neither fact was recorded anywhere: `BACKLOG.md` mentions Playwright once, unrelated (control: "schemathesis" appears 6x, so the grep discriminates).

This now matters more than it used to. With GitHub Actions retired, `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` maps every retired CI job to a local command the PR author runs as the final check — and this one does not work.

## RECOMMENDATION

Two parts, in order:

1. **Make the suite installable.** Either add `tests/e2e` to the root `workspaces` array (currently `packages/*`, `services/*`, `frontend/*`), or have the documented run command do `npm ci --prefix tests/e2e` first. It works today only by accident: the root tree happens to hoist `@playwright/test`, `dotenv` and `@types/node`, but not `otplib`.
2. **Then triage the 20.** They need an owner and a baseline, the way the Schemathesis failing set has one — otherwise the suite is unusable as a gate even once it runs, because nobody can tell a new failure from the standing 20.

## Detail — how it fails

```
Error: Cannot find module 'otplib'
   at auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:13
```

* `otplib` IS declared — `tests/e2e/package.json` devDependencies, `^13.4.0`.
* It is **not** in the root `package-lock.json` (control: `@playwright/test` is, 1 match).
* `tests/e2e/node_modules` did not exist. `npm ci` there installs 16 packages, 0 vulnerabilities, and touches nothing tracked (`**/node_modules/` is ignored at `Blockchain/Dev/.gitignore:8`).
* Playwright aborts the whole run on a collection error, so the two recruitment specs never executed either — the failure is not confined to the spec with the bad import.

## Detail — the standing 20 (measured twice, same set both times)

Run: `npx playwright test tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts tests/recruitment/happy-path-wallet.spec.ts tests/recruitment/alternative-paths.spec.ts`

**9 x** `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **— basic login UI**
2.1.1 valid login (issuer) · 2.1.2 valid login (admin) · 2.1.3 session persists on reload · 2.1.4 logout redirects + cookie cleared · 2.1.5 login after logout · 2.2.1 wrong password shows error · 2.2.2 wrong email generic error · 2.2.3 empty email blocked · 2.2.4 empty password blocked

**1 x** `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **— assertion looks wrong, not the app**
2.4.6 "SQL injection in registration name is sanitized" asserts the response body does not contain `drop table`, but registration **succeeds** and echoes `displayName` back verbatim. The payload is stored and returned as data, which is the correct behaviour; the test is asserting against an echo, not against an injection.

**5 x** `happy-path-wallet.spec.ts` — CIP-8 wallet auth via API · wallet-signed document certification · Lace connection flow · wallet-not-installed handling · transaction signing

**5 x** `alternative-paths.spec.ts` — AP-2 revoked credential · AP-3 privacy-blocked field · AP-4 tampered-document hash mismatch · AP-5 invalid wallet address · AP-5 invalid signature

## Not caused by KS-712 / #760 — controlled

Same three specs run twice on the same commit, changing only the served spec (the gateway bind-mounts it, so a restart publishes it):

| served spec | result |
| -- | -- |
| #760's widened spec | 20 failed / 62 passed |
| the pre-change spec at `26100e24f` | **20 failed / 62 passed — identical set** |

The test code is byte-identical between the two (my commit touches 0 files under `tests/e2e`), and the yaml was restored byte-identical afterwards (md5 `c5174ac31273e51f63bb22c03c32c402`).

One run showed a 21st failure — 2.3.1 registration returning 503 — which did **not** reproduce: re-run on the same commit and served spec, 3/3 pass including the two dependents that had been skipped. Transient, proven rather than assumed.

## Related

* KS-712 / #760 — where this surfaced; Peter's review made "run Playwright" a blocking requirement, which is what exposed that it cannot run.
* `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` — Manual CI-gate equivalents.

## BLUF

**Two findings from the s107 post-merge SET on `develop` `81935f9a6`, one of which is yours and one of which needs its own ticket that the Linear cap will not let me create.** Homed here because KS-734 is the live sibling — `issueCreate` returned `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`activeIssueCount`) at 08:3xZ and I did not archive anything to make room.

## 1. Confirmation for KS-734 — the missing browser binary, measured

Running the suite on this machine:

```
cd Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e
npx playwright test tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts --project=prelaunch-auth --reporter=list
```

**43 passed / 10 failed.** **Nine of the ten are not results at all** — every one died in **1ms** with:

```
Error: browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at
  ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1200/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell
```

They ran nothing. That is exactly this ticket: the suite cannot run from a clean checkout. Worth adding to the ticket explicitly — **the failure presents as ten red tests, not as a setup error**, so a reader who counts reds attributes nine of them to the code under test. On a report that says "10 failed", nine are the missing binary.

Note also the project filter: these live under `--project=prelaunch-auth`, not `api`. `--project=api` returns `No tests found` — a silent zero.

## 2. NOT KS-734 — needs its own ticket when the cap lifts

**Test 2.4.6 "SQL injection in registration name is sanitized" (`auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`) fails on an ECHO, not an injection, and the assertion cannot tell them apart.**

`POST /api/auth/register` with `name = "Robert'); DROP TABLE users; --"` returns **201**, body carries `"displayname":"robert'); drop table users; --"` back verbatim. **The injection did not execute** — no SQL error, no `syntax error`, not a 5xx; the sibling assertions on `'sql'` and `'syntax error'` both passed. Parameterised SQL held. The only failing line is:

```js
expect(body.toLowerCase()).not.toContain('drop table');   // line 751
```

Any application that stores and returns a user-supplied display name fails that, whatever its SQL layer does — so it is a **permanent red carrying no signal**. Sibling 2.4.7 (XSS in name) **passes**, so the field is not simply unfiltered.

**UNMEASURED, deliberately:** whether `displayName` is escaped by its consumers on the way out. I measured the echo, not the renderers, and I am not going to imply I checked.

Suggested: re-aim 2.4.6 at no-SQL-error + `status < 500` (both already true), or assert the stored value equals the exact input — and decide the output-escaping question separately on frontend evidence.

## Attribution — this is not #745's

Measured, not assumed: #745's three hunks in this file all sit inside `2.8 MFA / TOTP` (lines 1207-1352); 2.4.6 is at line 734. Control on `git diff a9b63bbd7 81935f9a6 -- <file>`: `2.8.6` appears **2x**, `2.4.6` appears **0x**, so the grep discriminates. #745 touched no registration code. Both findings pre-date the merge.

## PR [#920](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/920) — BOTH parts done, READY FOR QA. Not merged.

**BLUF: `2112a99e3` is on origin, preflight PASSED 13/13.** The suite is installable from a clean checkout, an unready checkout now refuses with one legible message instead of N red tests, and the standing set is baselined — where the headline is that **the suite is not deterministic**, so this ticket's "20 standing failures" was never a number anyone could diff against.

- **PR:** #920 · **head:** `2112a99e31aec4b6e132dc6519c75d3afb6b2b02`, read from `git ls-remote origin` in the same action as the push
- **branch:** `kamilkreiser/ks-734-e2e-suite-installable` · **base:** `develop` @ `b6884888d`

## Part 1 — installable (the RECOMMENDATION's option 2, not option 1)

Took the `npm ci --prefix tests/e2e` route rather than adding `tests/e2e` to the root `workspaces` array. The workspace route would fold its lockfile into the root tree and change hoisting for all 24 services — a much larger blast radius than the defect warrants.

`npm run e2e:install` / `npm run e2e` from `Blockchain/Dev`. `check-e2e-ready.mjs` refuses an unready checkout, wired into **both** `pretest` **and** `globalSetup` — the latter because `npx playwright test` skips npm hooks — and placed **before** global-setup's side effects. Measured: the guarded run now emits `Acquiring tokens` **0** times and `Test document created` **0** times, where the unguarded run emitted each once **before** dying.

**Also fixed:** `test-helpers.ts:420` writes timestamped artefacts to `Blockchain/Dev/screenshots/evidence/`, an unignored path — so running the suite dirtied the tree. 0 files tracked there, 106 tracked elsewhere under `screenshots/` (control), so only the output subdirectory is ignored.

⚠ **A control caught a defect in my own first attempt.** I wrote the scripts with `npm --prefix … exec`, which resolves the package from that path but runs in the **caller's** cwd — Playwright then loaded a different config: **76 tests, no project labels**, against **82** the right way. Both look like a suite run. Proven empirically (`exec` cwd vs `run` cwd), fixed, and the trap written into DEV-PROCESS and BASELINE.

## Part 2 — the baseline, and it is not a single number

🔴 Same commit, same command, `lockout:*` cleared before **each** run: **23 failed**, then **11**; `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone gave **1**, then **11**. It brute-forces logins, `fullyParallel: true` is set, and every run leaves **4 `lockout:*` keys** — it races its own lockout. The flapping cells move as ONE block (both 23-runs carried the same 23), which rules out twelve independent flakes.

**Deterministic remainder, red in 5 of 5:** 10 recruitment/wallet cells + `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`, whose assertion is wrong rather than the app.

**This ticket's 20 = 9 + 11.** Nine were the missing chromium binary this PR now installs; control — the 2.1.x/2.2.x basic-login cells are absent from the 11-failure runs entirely.

## Filed, not fixed here — the ticket's "triage the 20" needs these first

- **KS-1038** — the self-lockout race. **Until this is fixed the suite cannot gate anything**, because a failure count carries no information. This is the real blocker on part 2's "give it an owner and a baseline".
- **KS-1039** — 2.4.6 asserts against an echo, not an injection (this ticket's own 2026-09-02 comment asked for it).
- **KS-1040** — preflight leg 4 reports "a published path is unroutable" when the cause is an exhausted login budget.

## NOT covered

- **The other ~37 spec files.** Only the three named specs (82 tests) are baselined; `tests/` holds ~40 across 10+ projects.
- **Whether `LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED=true` stabilises the flapping cells** — it must be set on the auth *container*, needing a restart of a shared local stack. Deliberately not done, so KS-1038's remedy is a suggestion, not a proven fix.
- **Schemathesis / Akto / k6** — no service, spec or config surface is touched.

## One friction this surfaced, and it bit this PR

Running the suite **blocks your own next push for up to 15 minutes.** The gateway limiter is `RateLimit-Policy: 100;w=900`, **IP-scoped not per-account** (control: `admin@secuura.com` 429'd in the same second; clearing `lockout:counter:demo@secuura.io` changed nothing), and preflight leg 4 logs in as `demo@secuura.io`. **This PR's first push was refused by exactly that.** Waited out `RateLimit-Reset` and re-pushed — no `--no-verify`. Documented in both `BASELINE.md` and `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` Known frictions.

*Posted from the Platform K session (s160). No merge attempted — no approval exists, and one cannot be self-supplied.*

KS-723.desc:
> **Origin.** Assembled from the measurement parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comments `ae3aab1a` (the 173-op survey) and `4b388b0b` ("the remaining ~157 operations are being sized as their own ticket"), on 2026-08-28 when `issueCreate` refused workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29 once creation worked again. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket** — every number below is the one already recorded on KS-712 and is dated to that run.

## BLUF

KS-712 established that **173 routed** `/api` **operations are absent from the OpenAPI spec**, which makes them invisible to both Schemathesis and Akto. Two slices of that gap have since been declared:

| slice | ops | where |
| -- | -- | -- |
| MFA · wallet-auth · social sign-in | 16 | [#760](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/760>) |
| the two settings PUTs (+ their GETs) | 4 | [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>) / [KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719) |
| **this ticket — the remainder** | **~157** | not started |

This is the mechanical bulk of the gap. It was deliberately not attempted in the KS-712 pass: *"That is a large mechanical change and wants its own PR and its own review; flagging the scope rather than half-landing it."*

## Shape of the remainder (from the KS-712 run, 2026-08-28)

Of the 173 routed-and-undocumented operations:

* **By method:** GET 83 · POST 64 · DELETE 12 · PUT 11 · PATCH 3. **90 of 173 are write methods** — the half that matters most for an untested surface.
* **By area: **`/api/admin` 58 · `/api/auth` 14 · `/api/users` 11 · `/api/workflows` 8 · `/api/anchors` 8 · `/api/platform` 7.
* **Unauthenticated response:** 401 ×149 · 400 ×8 · 200 ×15 · 204 ×1.

Subtracting the 20 already declared, the remainder is dominated by `/api/admin` (58 operations, none declared) — a single area worth about a third of the whole job.

## Suggested order

The dependency order recorded on KS-712 was MFA → wallet-auth → social callback → the rest; the first three are done. For the remainder, largest-coherent-area-first keeps each PR reviewable:

1. `/api/admin` (58)
2. `/api/users` (11) + `/api/platform` (7)
3. `/api/workflows` (8) + `/api/anchors` (8)
4. the long tail

## Constraints that apply to every slice

* **KS-424 guard:** every new operation needs an explicit `security:` block, or `check:openapi` fails.
* **The gateway BIND-MOUNTS** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — a spec change is published by *restarting* the gateway container, not by rebuilding an image. Verify the served spec, not the file on disk.
* Declaring an operation does **not** put it in Akto's scan collection — see the sibling ticket on `test:pr` never re-importing the spec. A slice of this work is only "covered" once both tools actually exercise it.
* Each slice will widen the Schemathesis failing set. Record the failing **set**, diff it against the previous run on the same instrument, and classify new entries rather than counting them.

## Two things this ticket is NOT

1. **Not a decision about behaviour.** Where declaring an operation would bless behaviour that has not been ruled on, split it out — that is exactly what happened with the two unauthenticated PUTs, which became KS-719 rather than being documented as-is.
2. **Not a total.** 173 is a floor, not a count: **60 of 105** `/api` **mount bindings did not resolve** to a defining file (dynamic mounts, re-exports, barrel files), so those services are counted only where they register absolute paths. The CI guard proposed on [KS-663](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-663) — assert every routed `/api` path appears in the spec — is the only thing that turns this from a survey into a number that stays true.

## Sizing

**Peter-sized, and deliberately routed to him** — this is mechanical spec authoring across ~157 operations in at least four PRs, on a surface he originally reported. Not a one-session job and not a job worth interleaving with security findings.

## Method (for the numbers above)

Recorded in full on KS-712 comment `ae3aab1a`: route registrations extracted from each service's **compiled** `/app/dist` **in the running container** (not parsed TypeScript — static parsing undercounts by 34% because a third of registrations are named exports), mount bindings resolved precisely rather than cross-producted, then **every candidate probed against the live gateway**, with the probe as the arbiter. `/api/docs/*` excluded as a Swagger catch-all that answers 200 on any nonsense path; the control that catches it is one nonsense path per prefix.

comments.body: Two of the undeclared `/api/anchors` operations are on Platform-S's hot path, so they belong early in slice 3: `GET /api/anchors/{id}` (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:827`) and `GET /api/anchors/tx/{txHash}` (`:1089`). S's refresher polls them for every in-flight anchor (`ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.cs:273-278`). The spec (2026-09-29) declares `/api/anchors`, `/thread-mint`, `/thread-state/{documentId}` and `/document/{documentId}` only. S's PS-614 gate reads the spec for verbs, so today a change to those two routes' response shape would be invisible offline.

KS-693.desc:
## BLUF

**Four M365 operations answer** `503 Service Unavailable` **when** `ENTRA_*` **is unconfigured, and a 503 is a server error — so every Schemathesis run on a normal dev machine records 9 failures that are configuration, not defects.** This is the KS-478 / KS-451 / KS-431 "raw 5xx instead of a clean refusal" family, and it now matters more than it did: since Kam retired GitHub Actions on 2026-08-27, the local Schemathesis run **is** the merge gate, so a permanent 9-failure floor makes that gate unreadable.

Found on the first run under the new final-check rule — develop `ca5b643e0`, full 32-service stack, auth re-seeded, run validity OK (0 of 307 operations errored).

## The failures

`9 failures, 3 warnings in 72.21s` — all `Server error`, all the same body:

```
[503] Service Unavailable
{"success":false,"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
 "message":"M365 integration not configured",
 "details":{"setup":"Add Microsoft 365 Business Basic license and configure ENTRA_* env vars"}}}
```

Operations:

| operation |
| -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/init` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/{id}/refresh` |
| `POST /api/m365/documents/sync` |

Reproduce (from the report):

```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"organizationId":"e3e70682-c209-1cac-a29f-6fbed82c07cd","tenantId":"84fe882e-d558-4800-892d-eb967ea4a232"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/m365/connections/init
```

## Why this is a defect and not just "configure your env"

**A missing integration credential is a known, permanent, expected state on every developer machine and in CI — it is not an unexpected server fault. **`503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` says "the server broke or is overloaded, retry later". Neither is true: the server is healthy and retrying will never help until someone buys an M365 licence.

The service already knows exactly what is wrong — it returns a precise, actionable `details.setup` string. It has all the information needed to answer honestly and chooses a 5xx anyway.

This is the same reasoning the team already accepted for KS-478 (`raw 5xx on POST /api/governance/delegate … instead of a clean business refusal`). The only difference is that this one is triggered by configuration rather than by input.

## Options

1. `501 Not Implemented` — the literal meaning: this server does not support this function. Declares in the spec, is not a server error, and Schemathesis will not flag it.
2. `400`**/**`422` **on the call** — treats "no connection configured" as a precondition failure like every other precondition in KS-478.
3. **Do not mount the routes at all when** `ENTRA_*` **is absent**, so they 404 like any unmounted feature. Cleanest, but changes the published surface conditionally, which the OpenAPI contract work (KS-663) would need to account for.

Whichever is chosen, **the response must be declared in the OpenAPI spec** or it will simply move from a `server_error` failure to a `status_code_conformance` failure.

## Interim, so the gate is usable today

Until this is fixed the four operations should be registered as by-design tolerated in `systemTest/schemathesis` (the KS-662 / KS-518 guard pattern) **scoped to these four operations by name and to the 503-when-unconfigured case only** — not a blanket 5xx tolerance. Without that, every author running the mandated final check sees 9 red and has to learn to ignore it, which is precisely how a gate stops working.

## Provenance

Schemathesis `pr` tier, develop `ca5b643e0`, 2026-08-27T08:50:44Z, seed 2899853179.
Report: `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/pr-2026-08-27T08-50-44Z/`.

KS-692.desc:
## Summary

`POST /api/status/:id/revoke` and `/unrevoke` enforce an **admin-class role** but **no tenant ownership check**. An `ISSUER_ADMIN` in one tenant can revoke or un-revoke a credential in **another tenant's** status list. Reproduced live on `develop 576ebef85`.

This is the **second half of KS-586**, which fixed the role gap and explicitly deferred the tenant gap — but **KS-586 is now** `Done`**, so nothing tracks the remainder.** That is why this ticket exists.

## ⚠️ What is already FIXED — read this before working the ticket

**KS-586 is done and its fix is live. **`/api/status` is no longer "no authorization at all". Anyone picking this up from a summary of [KS-570](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-570) will be looking for a defect that is not there.

| probe (local, `develop 576ebef85`) | result |
| -- | -- |
| `holder@secuura.com` (**OWNER**, non-admin) → revoke | **403 **`Role OWNER is not authorized for this action` |

The role gate at `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts:42-53` (`STATUS_WRITE_ROLES`, applied as a router-level gate ahead of the route table) works. Commit `bda40c91c` on `develop`, present in the running container.

## The defect that IS live — reproduced, controls both ways

Two `ISSUER_ADMIN`s in **different tenants**:

* `demo@secuura.io` — tenant `default`
* `registrar@oxford-test.invalid` — tenant `oxford`

| # | actor | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status` create list | **201** |
| 2 | demo (owner) | `POST /api/status/:id/allocate` `cred-xtenant-probe` | **200**, index 0 |
| 3 | **oxford registrar (foreign tenant)** | `POST /api/status/:id/revoke` that credential | 🔴 **200** — `{"revoked":true,"reason":"cross-tenant probe"}` |
| 4 | demo (owner) | `GET /api/status/:id/revoked` | **200** — `{"revokedIndexes":[0],"totalRevoked":1}` — the write really landed |
| 5 | **control** — oxford registrar | revoke against a **non-existent** list id | **404 **`Status list not found` |
| 6 | **control** — holder (OWNER) | revoke the same list | **403** (role gate) |

**Controls 5 and 6 are what make row 3 mean something.** Row 5 proves the 200 was a genuine authorisation pass and not a blanket accept — the same foreign caller is refused when the target does not exist. Row 6 proves role is still evaluated, so the only thing missing is the tenant comparison.

## Root cause

`services/vc-issuer/src/routes/status.ts`. The router-level gate checks **role only**:

```ts
return requireRole(...STATUS_WRITE_ROLES)(req, res, next);
```

There is no comparison of the caller's tenant to the status list's owner — **because the status list has no owner to compare to.** Status lists live in a process-local `Map` with no tenant linkage. The code says so itself (`status.ts:35-38`):

> *"Tenant scoping is NOT enforced here yet: status lists live in a process-local Map with no tenant linkage, and the ownership model is the KS-539/KS-547/KS-586 joint authorization decision — tracked on KS-586."*

**"tracked on KS-586" is no longer true.** KS-586 is `Done` (2026-08-12) and KS-547 is `Done`; KS-539 is open but scoped to *governing rules for document operations by agents*, not status-list tenancy. The deferral outlived its tracker — which is the actual reason this went untracked for two weeks.

## Why this is not a duplicate

* **KS-586** — `Done`. The **role** half. Fixed.
* **KS-570** — the **authentication** half: the gateway mount at `proxy.ts:702` has no `authenticateToken`, so revoked-session JWTs still pass. Different layer, still open.
* **KS-588** — `Backlog`. **Test coverage** for `/api/status` authorization. Would catch this once it exists; is not the fix.
* **This ticket** — the **tenant/ownership** half. No ticket held it after KS-586 closed.

## Severity

**High.** Revocation state is an integrity operation on a document-authenticity platform — an attacker with any admin-class role in any tenant can un-revoke a credential their victim revoked, or revoke a live one. Same family as [KS-643](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-643) (cross-tenant API-key revoke) and [KS-642](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-642), and it sits on the same **KS-621 tenancy boundary** that is currently held for @kamil.kreiser's design ruling.

Not raised to Urgent: exploitation needs a valid admin-class credential in *some* tenant, so it is privilege-escalation-across-tenants, not anonymous.

## Suggested fix — NOT implemented, deliberately

The ownership model is a **KS-621 boundary decision** and is @kamil.kreiser's call, exactly as with KS-643. Filing only, per the same hold.

The prerequisite is structural: **a status list must carry an owning tenant before any check can be written.** The process-local `Map` has nowhere to put one, so this is not a middleware one-liner — it needs the list persisted with a tenant column, which is likely the same decision as KS-539's ownership model.

Note the interlock, learned from KS-578/KS-643: adding a tenant check **without** giving lists an owner would refuse every caller, since no list has a tenant to match.

## Reproduction

Local stack, `develop 576ebef85`, both accounts seeded. Full curl sequence is rows 1–6 above. Probe artefacts were written to the **local** stack only (`ks661-tenantprobe-*`); status lists are process-local and clear on a `vc-issuer` restart. **Nothing was written to demo.**

Handed over by @peter on KS-570 (2026-08-26 08:10Z): *"The one still open is the /api/status authorisation gap … I will let you file that one too, as you hold the evidence for it."* — filed with the measurement rather than the paraphrase, which is how the KS-586 half turned out to be already fixed.
