KS-669.desc:
## BLUF

**The published OpenAPI spec points integrators at 18 URLs on two domains Secuura does not own — one of which is currently for sale.** The guard rule that fixtures.ts names as enforcing our domain policy (**E1**) only ever inspects **email addresses**; it does not look at URLs at all, so this has never been checkable.

The sharpest instance is one line:

```yaml
# components.schemas.AnalyticsExport.example
url: https://exports.secuura.com/exp_01HC9ZQ2ABCDEFGHIJKLMN/document...
```

`secuura.com` is **not ours**. The project `CLAUDE.md` records it as *"not owned (parked for sale on Afternic/GoDaddy; **do not link to it**)"* — and the customer-facing API documentation links to it, on the field a client reads to fetch a completed analytics export.

## Measured

Every URL appearing inside an `example:` block in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, by host:

| host | count | status |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `api.example.com` | 6 | fine — RFC 2606 reserved |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | `secuura.io` is not a domain we control |
| `exports.secuura.com` | **1** | **not owned; parked for sale** |

`fixtures.ts` already states the policy and the reason, for emails:

> *"*`secuura.io` *is not a domain we are known to control (we hold [secuura.ai](<http://secuura.ai>) and [secuura.net](<http://secuura.net>)), so publishing it in customer-facing docs points integrators at third-party infrastructure. Enforced by guard rule E1."*

The policy is right. The enforcement claim is not.

The 17 `example.secuura.io` occurrences span **12 schemas**: `OAuthAppCreateRequest` (redirect URIs), `WebhookCreateRequest`, `WebhookUpdateRequest`, `M365TeamsWebhookConfigRequest`, `M365CompleteConnectionRequest`, `M365AddSiteRequest`, `BillingCheckoutBundleRequest`, `BillingCheckoutCustomRequest`, `BillingCheckoutSessionResponse`, `DidService`, `DidCreateRequest`, `DidUpdateRequest`.

Note what those fields are: OAuth **redirect URIs**, **webhook delivery targets**, and **billing checkout** URLs. If a domain we do not own is documented as the canonical shape for a redirect target, the failure mode is not cosmetic.

## Why the guard never caught it — the mechanism

`scripts/spec-examples/check/rules-global.mjs:67-77`:

```js
/** E1 — an address outside the single reserved example domain. */
function checkEmailDomain(text, docPath, allow, findings) {
  for (const match of text.match(EMAIL_RE) ?? []) {
    const domain = match.split('@')[1].toLowerCase();
    ...
```

It iterates `EMAIL_RE` matches and splits on `@`. A bare URL produces no match, so it is never examined. E1 is an *email*-domain rule wearing a *domain*-rule name — which is exactly why fixtures.ts's "Enforced by guard rule E1" reads as covering more than it does.

The gate is green today (`check:openapi` PASS, 394 example blocks, *"every published example resolves to the fixture set"*) **with all 18 of these published**, so a passing run is not evidence here.

## Recommendation

1. **Add a URL-host rule to the global rules** (an E-rule sibling of E1) accepting only RFC 2606 reserved hosts plus an explicit allow-list of domains we actually own (`secuura.ai`, `secuura.net`). Anything else fails the gate. This is the piece that makes the rest stay fixed.
2. **Add** `FX.webhookUrl` **/** `FX.redirectUri` **/** `FX.exportUrl` on `example.com`, and repoint all 18. Needs the matching accept-list entry in `scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs` — the duplication trap recorded on KS-665.
3. **Fix** `exports.secuura.com` **first and separately** if 1–2 will not land quickly. It is one line, and it is the one pointing at a domain a third party can currently buy.

## Relationship to other tickets

* **KS-665** carries an open *"webhook example URL"* decision from the KS-256 §4 review — *"*`POST /api/webhooks` *publishes a URL the API refuses because the host cannot resolve, and fixing it collides with E1's reserved-domain rule."* This ticket supersedes the framing of that item: it is not one example needing a judgement call, it is **18 across 13 schemas with no guard coverage**, and there is no collision with E1 because E1 never sees URLs.
* **KS-256 / PR #568** is the branch these examples were generated on. **No change is requested there** — the branch is reviewed and waiting on sign-off, and this predates it in kind.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — measured by walking every `example:`/`examples:` block and extracting URLs by host.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/spec-examples/check/rules-global.mjs:60-77` — `applyGlobalRules` and `checkEmailDomain`; no URL inspection anywhere in E1–E4.
* `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/openapi/examples/fixtures.ts` — `EXAMPLE_DOMAIN`, and the comment claiming E1 enforcement.
* Project `CLAUDE.md` — `secuura.com` not owned, "do not link to it".

Found while working KS-665 item 2.

KS-665.desc:
The three items left open from @kksecura's 2026-08-19 review of PR #568. Split out per his own §8 reasoning — the parameter-example work is the bigger half of the same problem, and bundling it would expand a PR he has already reviewed twice.

**Every figure below was re-verified against the branch head** `92feea4a9`**, not carried over from the review.**

---

## 1. §4 — the five example-fixable 400s are still published

His triage stands unchallenged: **5 strictly example-fixable**, or **8 counting parameter examples**. My original "at most 4" was low. All five are still live in `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`:

| # | Defect | Count at head |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | `example-documentId` violates `SAFE_ID_PATTERN` | **17** |
| 2 | `example-code` exceeds the documented max of 8 | **3** |
| 3 | `example-challengeId` is not a uuid | **1** |
| 4 | `example-country` is not exactly 2 chars | **2** |
| 5 | `transfer-custody` pins two mutually exclusive fields | 1 |

Number 5 is the sharpest, because the spec contradicts itself **four lines apart** (`secuura-api.yaml:6318-6322`):

```yaml
description: Exactly ONE of `newHolderId` / `newHolderEmail` is required — neither is 400, both is 400.
example:
  newHolderId: example-newHolderId
  newHolderEmail: demo.issuer@example.com     # ← publishing exactly what the line above calls a 400
```

A reader copying that example gets a guaranteed 400, and the description already tells them why.

**Fix direction:** these land in the Zod sources (`services/*/src/*.openapi.ts`), then `npm run generate-openapi`. Numbers 1–4 need the placeholder to satisfy the constraint the schema already documents; number 5 needs the example to pin one field only.

## 2. The bigger half — parameter examples

Verified at head: **132 path parameters, 2 carrying an example.** That is the §7 gap on [KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own body, and it is why this is a follow-up rather than a patch. Together with `operationId`/`links` ([KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) — 0 of 613 links covered) it is the next real coverage step, and it dwarfs the five above.

## 3. §10 — the trap that produced the build failure, recorded nowhere

`npm run generate-openapi` runs the `*.openapi.ts` files through `tsx`**, which is transpile-only**. A type error in the very file the generator reads therefore **cannot** fail the spec gate.

That is exactly how the `documentUuid` breakage shipped: `check:openapi` was **green** — drift clean, E1–E9 0 findings across 354 blocks — while `originate` would not compile, and the failure only surfaced in the Docker build (30/34 images, `originate` + `migrations` red, no containers started).

`check:openapi` **green is not evidence the images build.** Nothing in `scripts/`, `CLAUDE.md` or `package.json` says so today. Options, in increasing order of strength:

1. Document it where the gate is defined and in `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Add a `tsc --noEmit` pass over the `*.openapi.ts` sources to `check:openapi`, so the gate covers the files it consumes.

Option 2 would have caught the original defect at the gate rather than in a 50-minute image build. @kksecura offered the wording or is happy for us to take it — his call.

## 4. A new instance of the §3 class his sweep did not reach

`secuura-api.yaml:7265` publishes:

```yaml
userAgent: Demo Issuer
```

Same mechanism as the 16 `address` fields fixed in `704c8c0f2`: a legitimate `FIXTURE_PERSON_VALUES` member landing on a **non-person** field, so **E5 passes it** — the guard is working to spec and the spec is wrong for the field. Not a leak; a documentation defect, since no client sends `Demo Issuer` as a user agent.

**Verified the rest are correct** — the other 21 `Demo Issuer` hits are all on genuine name fields and should stay:

```
17  displayName     2  channelName     1  fullName     1  name
 1  userAgent   ← the defect
```

**Fix direction:** same as §3 — either give `userAgent` its own fixture, or stop masking-category-3 claiming it. Worth deciding once for the class rather than per field, since `address` and `userAgent` are now two instances of it.

---

[KS-256](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256/add-openapi-inline-examples-to-all-329-operations-eliminate-coverage)'s own acceptance already carries the 26×400 triage as an open box, and its two remaining boxes are gated on [KS-660](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-660/ci-every-needs-build-suite-job-dies-in-3s-with-zero-steps-develop-is) (CI executes zero steps). Items 1 and 4 here are small, item 2 is large, and item 3 is a gate change — none of them belongs in a PR that has been reviewed twice and is waiting on sign-off.

| `develop` `29287565e` | 319 | 132 | **2** | 130 |
| `c114ceddd` (#568 head) | 319 | 132 | **42** | **90** |

The 90 break down exactly as the ticket recorded: 62 `id (string)` · 5 `customerId` · 5 `sessionId` · 3 `id (uuid)` · 2 each `cid`/`dsrId`/`did`/`address` · 1 each `chartName`/`widgetType`/`errorId`/`code`/`codeId`/`tier` · 1 `index (integer)`. Group spread also matches: billing 11 · kyc 9 · governance 7 · status 7 · m365 6 · transfers 6 · webhooks 5 · oauth 4 · long tail 1–3.

One number I read differently: **29** route groups counting by top-level resource (which is what reproduces your spread), **63** counting by resource + sub-path. Same data, and the 29 is the right unit for fixture design.

## 2. 🔴 The gate cannot see these examples — measured, not inferred

`leafName()` (`check/finding.mjs`) reports the last non-numeric segment of the dotted path. For a scalar `example:` on a parameter, that segment is the literal string **`example`** — never the parameter's `name`. E5 (`isPersonField`) and E8 (`IDENTIFIER_FIELD_RE`) both key off that field name, so neither can match.

I ran the gate four times against the `c114ceddd` spec, injecting `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000010` — `demo@secuura.io`'s user id, **E8's own founding defect**:

| # | where the leak was injected | example blocks | gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | untouched spec | 394 | **exit 0** — clean |
| B1 | as a **path-parameter** example on `/api/billing/customers/{customerId}/invoices` | 395 | **exit 0 — E8 silent** |
| B2 | as a scalar `properties.userId.example`, 32 sites | 426 | **exit 0 — E8 silent** |
| C | inside an **object-valued** example under key `userId` | 394 | **exit 1 — E8 fires** |

Run C is the control, and it fails independently: same value, same rule, same spec — it reports `components.schemas.OperationStatus.example.userId` correctly. So B1/B2 are a real structural blind spot, not a dud value or a broken harness. Note B1's block count rose to 395: the example **was** collected, it just was not inspected.

What *does* still reach a path-parameter example, tested the same way — all four fire and exit 1: **E1** (`someone@gmail.com`), **E3** (`issuer123`), **E4** (`doc-1777346021120-1e528170`), **E7** (a `sk_live_…` blob). Those run in the global sweep, which walks the whole document and needs no field name.

**Two consequences.** For this tranche, E5/E8 give no protection and review is the only control. And more usefully: the one-line fix is to sweep a parameter's example under the parameter's own `name` instead of `example`, which would put all 132 — and every scalar property example — back under E5/E8. Worth its own ticket; I have not written it, and it is not this ticket's scope.

## 3. 🔴 `secuura.io` — 17 published URLs, and the domain does not resolve

`c114ceddd` publishes `https://example.secuura.io/resource` **17 times**; `develop` publishes it **0 times**. They come from `scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`, which returns that literal for `format: uri`, and the codemod baked it into six `*.openapi.ts` files — including `successUrl`, `cancelUrl`, `redirectUri` and `webhookUrl`.

Measured, with a control set:

| domain | DNS status | NS |
|---|---|---|
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none, and no SOA |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns1/dns2.registrar-servers.com` |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1/dns2.registrar-servers.com` |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns3/ns4.afternic.com` (parked) |

`example.secuura.io` has no A record. I could not establish registration status — `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` line describes the TLD, not the domain. The DNS result is what I am relying on: the apex has no delegation.

This is not a new sin of yours — `fixtures.ts` already says it in its own words: *"`secuura.io` is not a domain we are known to control (we hold secuura.ai and secuura.net), so publishing it in customer-facing docs points integrators at third-party infrastructure."* That reasoning was applied to emails and E1 enforces it. **There is no equivalent rule for URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only inspects addresses — which is why KS-669 had to find `exports.secuura.com` by hand, and why this passes a clean gate.

Worth stating plainly in both directions: **#568 removes all 3 `demo@secuura.io` addresses** `develop` publishes (0 remain) — a real improvement, and exactly what E1 is for. The URL class is the part that travels the other way.

Suggested resolution, for agreement: point the synthesiser at `https://example.com/resource` (RFC 2606, already `EXAMPLE_DOMAIN`), regenerate, and add a URL-host rule alongside E1. That is a one-line change in `synthesize.ts` plus a regen — but it is your file and your branch, so I have proposed rather than touched it.

## 4. Where the accept-list actually lives

Flagging this because the next tranche adds ~22 entries and will hit it. `fixtures.ts` exports `FIXTURE_IDS` under the comment *"Every identifier the guard will accept in an `example:` block."* **Nothing consumes it** — a symbol sweep across every `.ts`/`.mjs` at `c114ceddd` returns one file, its own declaration. Control: the same sweep for `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` returns three consumers.

The live list is `scripts/spec-examples/check/contract.mjs`'s `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES`, and the duplication is deliberate and well argued in the test's own docstring. But the sync test asserts **set equality** for `FIXTURE_PERSON_VALUES` and only `toContain` over a **hardcoded five** (`tenant`, `issuer`, `holder`, `document`, `anchor`) for `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` — and it never reads `FIXTURE_IDS`. Today they already differ by six, five of which are documented as deliberate; the sixth, `FX.document.uuid`, is in `FX` and in the guard but not in `FIXTURE_IDS`.

So a maintainer who adds 22 fixtures to `FX` + `FIXTURE_IDS` and stops there changes nothing, and no test tells them. **Adding to `contract.mjs` is the step that matters.** Cheap fix worth folding into the tranche: derive the test's list from `FX`, or delete `FIXTURE_IDS` so it cannot mislead.

## 5. The proposed fixture set

Conventions kept exactly as established: all-zero UUID family, **resource range `…0030+`** so nothing reads as a principal (`…0001` tenant, `…0002` cert org, `…0010` issuer, `…0020` holder are taken; `…0030`/`…0031` in use). Prefixed ids keep the prefix the runtime actually mints and take a zero-family UUID as the body — format-true, unmistakably synthetic, resolvable to no account.

**A. Bare-UUID resources** — runtime evidence `uuidv4()` / `randomUUID()` at the service:

| fixture | value | serves | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FX.proposal.id` | `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000040` | `governance/proposals/{id}` ×6 | 6 |
| `FX.transfer.id` | `…0041` | `transfers/{id}` ×6 | 6 |
| `FX.kyc.verificationId` | `…0042` | `kyc/{id}` + complete/document/result/review/selfie | 6 |
| `FX.kyc.sessionId` | `…0043` | `kyc/microsoft/{sessionId}` ×3 | 3 |
| `FX.walletSession.id` | `…0044` | `wallets/session/{sessionId}` ×2 | 2 |
| `FX.notification.id` | `…0045` | `notifications/{id}`, `/read` | 2 |
| `FX.delegation.id` | `…0046` | `delegations/{id}`, `/revoke` — `delegationService.ts:234` `id: uuidv4()` | 2 |
| `FX.issuerCert.id` | `…0047` | `issuer-certs/{id}` ×3 — the only three the spec declares `format: uuid` | 3 |
| `FX.export.id` | `…0048` | `analytics/exports/{id}` — `exportId = uuidv4()` | 1 |
| `FX.userSession.id` | `…0049` | `sessions/{id}` — `user_sessions.id` is `UUID` | 1 |
| `FX.systemError.id` | `…004a` | `system-errors/{errorId}/resolve` — `system_errors.id` is `UUID` in `040_system-errors.sql` | 1 |

**B. Prefixed resources** — prefix taken from the minting code, not guessed:

| fixture | value | evidence | serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FX.m365.connectionId` | `conn_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000050` | `conn_${randomUUID()}` | `m365/connections/{id}` ×3 |
| `FX.m365.siteId` | `site_…0051` | `siteId = \`site_${randomUUID()}\`` (`m365-integration/src/index.ts:736`) | `m365/sites/{id}` ×2 |
| `FX.security.eventId` | `event_…0052` | `event_${randomUUID()}` | `security/events/{id}/resolve` |
| `FX.security.auditId` | `audit_…0053` | `audit_${randomUUID()}` | `security/audit/{id}` |
| `FX.security.keyId` | `key_…0054` | `key_${randomUUID()}` | `security/keys/{id}` |
| `FX.timestamp.id` | `ts_…0055` | `ts_${randomUUID()}` | `timestamps/{id}` |

🔴 **These six collide with E7, and I only found that by testing them.** `HIGH_ENTROPY_RE` is `/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{40,}$/`, and `prefix_` + a 36-char UUID lands on 40–42 characters — so five of the six (`conn_`, `site_`, `event_`, `audit_`, `key_`; `ts_…` is 39 and squeaks under) are rejected as key-shaped blobs. `BENIGN_SHAPES` exempts a **bare** uuid and a **ULID-ish** `prefix_`, but not `prefix_<uuid>`. E7 also runs *before* the fixture-list check and never consults it, so **adding them to `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` does not help** — and E7 is one of the rules that still applies in the path-parameter position (§2), so this would have bitten in the real tranche.

The tempting fix is to switch these to the existing ULID-ish style (`anc_01HC9ZN4ANCHORFIXTURE1`), which passes untouched. **I recommend against it**, because of what that style already costs us:

🔴 **`FX.anchor.id` is `anc_…`, and the anchoring service has never minted an `anc_` id.** It mints `` `anchor_${randomUUID()}` ``. The string `anc_` appears exactly **once** in the whole anchoring service — in `anchoring.openapi.ts`, i.e. the published example itself. So the fixture is format-**false**: an integrator copying it uses a prefix the platform does not produce. That is the fourth instance of this ticket's recurring class, after the 16 `address` fields, `userAgent`, and `channelName: Demo Issuer` — a value that is plausible, certified by a guard, and wrong.

**So: keep `prefix_<uuid>` and widen the rule, rather than bend the values to fit it.** Two changes, both tested:

1. `BENIGN_SHAPES` += `/^[a-z]+_[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i` — a prefixed uuid, when a bare uuid is already benign.
2. `FIXTURE_ID_VALUES` += the **19** of the 21 that are identifier-shaped (`FX.statusList.id` `'1'` is not identifier-shaped, and `FX.did` carries colons so `IDENTIFIER_VALUE_RE` skips it — neither needs an entry).

I applied both to a **copy** of `contract.mjs` in the scratch sandbox and re-ran: the full proposed set goes **exit 0, clean**. Control, same patched contract: the seeded-account leak from §2 run C still **exits 1**. So the widening admits the fixtures without blunting the rule.

**C. Shapes that are not UUIDs at all** — and this is where a shared `id` fixture would have been wrong:

| fixture | value | why |
|---|---|---|
| `FX.statusList.id` | `'1'` | 🔴 `/api/status/{id}` is vc-issuer's StatusList2021 (`routes/status.ts:95+`, binding `statusListId: id`), and the service **already publishes `statusListId: '1'`** in its own response examples (`vc-issuer.openapi.ts:839,890`). A UUID here would be wrong and would 404. Serves **6** of the 7 `status` params. |
| `FX.billing.customerId` | `cus_0000000000FIXTURE` | Stripe-shaped (`config/stripe.config.ts`; fixtures in-repo use `cus_123`). Serves `customerId` ×5 **and** `billing/customers/{id}` ×3 — same resource, two parameter names. |
| `FX.did` | `did:prism:00000000000000000000000000000000` | Satisfies the declared `^did:[a-z0-9]+:[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$`. Note the row id (`did_${randomUUID()}`) is **not** what the path takes. |
| `FX.credential.id` | `urn:uuid:00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000056` | vc-issuer mints `urn:uuid:${randomUUID()}` — a URN, not a bare UUID. Serves `credentials/{id}`, `/revoke`. |

That is **21 new fixtures**, covering **62 of the 90** — 11 in group A, 6 in B, 4 in C. The remaining **28** are in §6.

**D. Reuse, no new fixture:** `address` ×2 (`stake/position/{address}`, `tiers/{address}`) → **`FX.wallet.address`**, which already exists and is already the published Cardano address elsewhere. Adding a second address fixture would document two wallets where the spec deliberately documents one.

## 6. What should NOT get a shared fixture

- **`tier`** — a declared enum (`bronze|silver|gold|platinum`). The example must be an enum member; `gold` route-local. A fixture would add indirection to a one-word literal.
- **`index`** — `integer, minimum: 0`, the bitstring offset in the status list. Route-local `0`. It is a position, not an identity.
- **`chartName`, `widgetType`** — `z.string()` with no enum in the schema, so the permitted values live in the handler's branching, which I could not locate in `analytics/src/index.ts`. Route-local, and **the values need confirming before anything is published** — a wrong one is a guaranteed 404 with no schema to catch it.
- **`referrals/{code}`** — a human-chosen share code, not an identifier the platform mints, so it should read like one (`SECUURA-DEMO`) rather than like a UUID. Distinct from **`{codeId}`**, the row id: `referralService.ts` mints `id: uuidv4()`, so that one is a straightforward group-A addition once you confirm the path takes the row id and not the code — I left it out of the 21 rather than assume.
- **`nft/ipfs/{cid}`** ×2 — a CID is content-addressed, so any valid CID either names real content or nothing at all. "Account-false" is satisfiable but "resolvable to nothing" is not, in the way it is for a UUID. Needs a deliberate call: publish the canonical public example CID, or publish none.
- **`webhooks/{id}`** ×4 — the only `id` the spec constrains by pattern (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`), and I could not find its minting site (`whsec_…` is the *secret*, not the id). Not guessing a shape for a pattern-constrained parameter.
- **`oauth/apps/{id}`** ×4 — 🔴 possible conflict: `contract.mjs` already carries `app_01HC9ZP5FIXTUREID01` as `NEUTRAL_PREFIXED_ID`, but auth mints client ids as `sec_${randomBytes(16).toString('hex')}`. Whether the path `id` is the client id or a separate row id decides which is right. Your call — it is your constant.
- **`presentations/{id}`** — 🔴 **blocked by §3.** The runtime id is `${VC_BASE_URL || 'https://secuura.io'}/presentations/${uuid}` — a full URL whose default host is the domain that does not resolve. No honest example exists until that default is decided.
- **`gdpr/dsr/{dsrId}`** ×2 and **`nft/certificates/{id}`** — I had both in group A on the strength of their tables, then could not find either creation site: `dsrId` is only ever read from a payload (`z.string()`), and the NFT id is mapped from a row, never minted in `minting.service.ts`. Table type alone does not give a format. **Pulled rather than published on a guess.**
- **`billing/invoices/{id}`, `/bundles/{id}`, `/payment-methods/{id}`** — plausibly Stripe `in_` / `pm_` given `config/stripe.config.ts`, but I verified the `cus_` shape and not these. Same rule: three more one-line confirmations, not three guesses.
- **`m365/documents/{id}`, `onedrive/files/{id}/sync`, `teams/webhook-config/{id}`** — one occurrence each and no minting site found; cheapest to settle when the file is open.
- **`governance/participants/{id}`** — a *user*, so it should draw from `FX.holder.id`, not a new participant fixture. Flagging rather than assuming: if participants are their own entity, it moves to group A.

## 7. What I did not do

No branch, no code, no regeneration, nothing merged — the tranche hold stands until #568 lands. The gate runs in §2 were against a copy of the spec in a scratch directory outside the repo; the working tree was not touched. Values in §5 are proposals for agreement; none is written anywhere yet.

**Four things need your call before implementation:** the `secuura.io` host (§3), the E7 widening vs ULID-ish values (§5), the `oauth/apps` id shape, and whether `presentations` can have an example at all. The rest I would implement as specified, post-#568, cut fresh from `develop`.

Everything above was measured on `c114ceddd` today. If any of it disagrees with what you have, mine is the number to re-check first — you know this branch better than I do.

## Results 2026-09-14 — what today's 4.27.1 sweeps say about the three open items

Slot 3, from-scratch stack, `develop` @ `64c386e04` (PR #993 bump); `full-2026-09-14T15-04-07Z-slot3` 342 ops, 0 errored.

* **§4 — example-fixable 400s.** 4.27.1 now falls back to a generated valid body when an operation's `example`/`examples`/`default` are all invalid (changelog 4.27.1), so a bad inline example no longer costs an operation its positive coverage — it costs the *example* its purpose. The `positive_data_acceptance` bucket moved accordingly under the bump (KS-1169's before/after: 10 ops left it, 17 entered). Re-verify the five ops named here against the new run before spending effort on them; the fix is still the right one, the urgency may have changed.
* **§10 — the tsx transpile-only spec-gate trap.** Not exercised by today's runs (spec unchanged on `develop` today); no new evidence either way.
* **`userAgent: Demo Issuer` instance.** Not re-checked today.

One adjacent item worth folding in: the `LoginRequest` inline example `demo.issuer@example.com` / `<your-password>` locks itself out (F-06) on every sweep — details on KS-256. Refs as KS-NNN text.

KS-1285 (Schemathesis 4.27.2 → 4.27.5, 2026-09-21, slot 1, same head and seed): the examples-phase 400 set is **unchanged by the upgrade** — 17 operations answered 400 to their examples-phase case at 4.27.2 and 18 at 4.27.5 (all 17 still present; `POST /api/governance/proposals` added because 4.27.4 now fills missing values from schema `default`s). 4.27.5's "drop/skip examples that violate their own schema" removed none of them: these examples are schema-valid and fail runtime validation, which is this ticket's point. Numbers on KS-1285's evidence comment.

KS-663.desc:
Raised by Platform S, 2026-08-19, from a full S↔K audit against K develop `74a330fc0`. **Nothing is broken today** — the spec is in sync. This is about keeping it that way now that something depends on it.

## What changed on our side

[PS-614](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-614>) (merged, S develop `2403313`) makes Platform S read `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` at gate time and fail its build when S's lifecycle-verb vocabulary disagrees with K's published enum, in either direction.

We built it because of [KS-556](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556>): K added `protect`/`unprotect`/`restore` on 2026-08-03, S adopted them on 2026-08-18, and for 15 days those events anchored with **no** `documentType` **at all**. Nothing failed, because every guard S had compared one hand-maintained copy of K's list against another. Reading K's own spec is the fix.

**Your spec is a strong contract, and that is why we chose it.** Verified: it is *generated* (`scripts/generate-openapi.ts:28`) from the same `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` / `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` constants the runtime validates against, and the enums match exactly — 22 and 13, diffed programmatically, empty symmetric difference. That is a better guarantee than a hand-written spec could give.

## The gap

`check:openapi` **is not wired into any CI workflow.** It exists as an npm script (`Blockchain/Dev/package.json:43`), but grepping all 17 files in `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` returns **zero** hits. (`quality:static` in `pr-platform-suites.yml:238` runs in `systemTest/playwright`, a different workspace.)

So the spec is correct today by diligence, not by enforcement — and it is now load-bearing for a consumer outside this repo. A PR that changes a verb without regenerating would leave S's gate green while S sends something K rejects, which is the [KS-388](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388>) 400-the-whole-anchor case.

**Ask:** run `check:openapi` in the PR workflow.

## Two divergences worth closing while you are there

**1.** `/api/v2/verification/verify-file` **is in code but absent from the spec.** Handler at `services/originate/src/routes/verificationV2.ts:497`; `verify-file` does not appear in `secuura-api.yaml` at all. The v1 equivalent is missing too. It is the only verify variant where the **server** computes the hash — i.e. the one a client cannot lie to — so it is the one most worth publishing. Invisible to a spec-reading consumer today.

**2.** `documentUuid` **is stricter in code than in the spec.** Code requires UUID **v4** specifically (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:350` `UUID_V4_RE`, 400s v1/v5/v7); the spec publishes `format: uuid` (`secuura-api.yaml:4556-4557`), which any RFC 4122 version satisfies. A client generating a v7 UUID passes spec validation and is rejected at runtime. We happen to send v4 ([PS-570](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-570>) enforces the version nibble before sending), so this has not bitten us — but it would bite a new integrator. Either publish the v4 constraint or relax the code.

## One observation, no action implied

`emitLifecycleAnchor` (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1120-1128`) posts only `{documentId, contentHash, network}` to `/api/anchors` — no `metadata.documentType`, no `metadata.timestamp`. So lifecycle events recorded through **K's own** endpoints anchor unlabelled, while the same verbs sent by S on the flat path carry the verb on-chain. Consistent with [KS-319](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-319>)'s scope, but it means the [KS-556](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-556/add-protectunprotectrestore-to-the-ks-134-lifecycle-verb-vocabulary) / [KS-534](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-534>) / [KS-415](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-415>) vocabulary only ever reaches the ledger via the flat path. Flagging in case that is not intended.

## Verification

* A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating the spec **fails** CI.
* `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec.
* `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches what the code enforces.

*Everything above verified read-only against develop* `74a330fc0`*. Happy to review a draft against our gate before you merge — we are the consumer and can tell you quickly whether it reads correctly from our side.*

comments.body:
**PR [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) is open** — branch `feature/ks-663-wire-check-openapi-into-the-gate`, head `3d8b40a07`, rebased onto `develop` `d928a27f8`.

This branch had been committed and **unpushed since s123**. The reason was never the code: the pre-push preflight's advisory leg hung on an unreachable npm endpoint with no timeout, so the push could not complete. **KS-788 merged this morning (#807) and bounded it — this branch then pushed in 76 seconds, 11/11 legs, rc 0.**

Scope is **divergence 2 only**. Divergence 1 (the verify-file spec) stays out: a live probe found the route 415s at the gateway, so publishing its spec would create a divergence rather than close one. That is KS-791.

## PR #808 approved — divergence 2 verified live

Approved [#808](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/808) (divergence 2, the `documentUuid` v4 constraint). Full review posted on the PR; summarising here with the evidence, and flagging what remains open on this ticket.

Credit where due to the authoring session: divergence 1 was deliberately pulled from that PR after a live probe found `verify-file` 415ing at the gateway, so publishing its spec would have created a divergence rather than closing one. That is now KS-791 / [#813](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/813). Recorded as a finding rather than an omission, which is the right way round.

### What was verified

| Claim | How it held up |
|---|---|
| Runtime enforces v4 | `documents.ts:331` `UUID_V4_RE`, applied at `:438` |
| Published pattern matches it | `[0-9a-fA-F]` / `[89abAB]` is an exact expansion of the `/i` flag — no widening, no narrowing |
| Scoped correctly | `DocumentCreateRequest.documentUuid` only; response schemas deliberately untouched, since `ks584-p3-verify-list.test.ts:222` asserts a legacy non-v4 pkey is returned as `documentUuid` |
| `userUuid` / `organizationUuid` | Left as bare `format: uuid`, matching the KS-596 ruling that those accept any RFC 4122 version |
| Runtime blast radius | None — no spec-driven request validator anywhere in `services/` or `packages/` |

### Test evidence

Run against branch head `3d8b40a07` on a local Docker stack built from that commit (33 containers, 32 healthy), 2026-09-08.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_document_uuid_validation.py` | **9/9 passed** |
| `test_document_uuid_contract.py` | **7/7 passed** |
| Served spec carries the constraint | Confirmed at `/api/docs/openapi.yaml`, on `DocumentCreateRequest` only |

Offline property-based generation probe, 300 examples each, to rule out `format: uuid` and `pattern` starving generation:

| Spec | Populated `documentUuid` | Violating v4 | Health-check failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR head | 56 | **0** | none |
| `develop` | 93 | **93** | none |

The counterfactual is the useful half: on `develop` every generated value was unusable input the runtime was always going to 400. So this change does not only document the constraint — it stops the contract suite spending `POST /api/documents` draws on values the endpoint could never accept.

The four platform suites were not re-run, matching the PR author's own statement. For a spec-only change with no runtime consumer of the spec, the two modules above are the directly relevant coverage.

**One process note:** the first invocation returned `16 skipped`, not passes — no `API_TOKEN` for that stack. `scripts/setup.py` provisioned one and the re-run was green. Worth knowing, since a gate reading only the exit code would have read that first result as a pass.

### Suggest keeping this ticket open

Of the three verification criteria in the description, one is now met:

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| `documentUuid`'s published constraint matches the code | **Met** — #808 |
| `verify-file` (v1 and v2) appears in the published spec | Moved to KS-791 / #813 |
| A PR that edits a verb constant without regenerating **fails CI** | **Still open** |

On the third — and this is the original ask, so worth being precise rather than assuming it was covered: `check:openapi` runs from `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh:111`, a local pre-push hook. Grepping `.github/workflows/` for `openapi` still returns zero hits, on this branch and on `develop`. A local hook is bypassable and does not run server-side, so the criterion as written is not yet satisfied. It does not appear to have a ticket of its own.

One related suggestion while that is being picked up: nothing currently couples the published pattern to `UUID_V4_RE` — they are independent literals in two files, so relaxing one leaves the other silently wrong, which is the same drift class this ticket was raised about. A small assertion reading `UUID_V4_RE.source` against the generated spec would close it and would sit naturally alongside the CI wiring.

## Why a new ticket

The whole predecessor chain is **Done and archived**:

* [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) — Done 2026-07-10 · [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) — Done 2026-07-13 · [KS-449](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-449/write-path-residuals-from-ks-430-ks-431-remaining-raw-500s-request) — Done · [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) — Done 2026-07-29, archived

Each closed having fixed the raw-500 class down to its listed operations, and each time it has come back on different ones. Filed fresh per that precedent.

## Finding

**17** `not_a_server_error` **failures across 8 operations** — an unhandled value reaches a handler or the DB and throws, instead of being rejected with a mapped 4xx.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke` · `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` · `POST /api/m365/outlook/exchange-token` · `POST /api/security/rate-limit/check` · `POST /api/users/admin/create` · `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`

**Three of these are the** [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) **endpoints** — `/share`, `/lifecycle-events`, and the `documents/{id}` family. Kamil shipped the connector-actor fix on 2026-08-07 (`develop` `307483672`, PR #652) and verified all three return 201 on demo for a connector. These 5xx are on *fuzzed* input rather than the connector path, so they are likely a different trigger on the same handlers — but worth confirming they are not a regression from that change.

`GET /api/users/admin/list` and `POST /api/users/admin/create` are already documented on [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) **§2** with root causes traced (`parseInt(offset) || 0` lets `-1` through to Postgres; `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard). [KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) also notes **the negative-offset pattern is six sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reaches.

## Important — this count was inflated until today

`not_a_server_error` read **79 failures** on the previous sweep. It dropped to **17** once the governance active-proposal cap was cleared: the cap throws a bare `Error` that the route maps to `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and every fuzzed proposal-create was counting as a server error. That mis-mapping is filed separately. **62 of the previous 79 were that one defect** — worth knowing before sizing this.

## Where this was run

**Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** (kernel `7.0.0-28-generic`, **aarch64**) on Parallels, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, at `10.211.55.4`.

| Component | Version |  | Component | Version |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (aarch64) |  | Docker | 29.7.2 |
| Python (venv + host) | 3.14.6 |  | Node (services) | 24.19.0 (`node:24-alpine`) |
| Schemathesis | 4.24.3 |  | PostgreSQL | 15.18 (`postgres:15-alpine`) |
| pytest / Hypothesis | 9.1.1 / 6.165.2 |  | Redis | 8.10.0 (`redis:8-alpine`) |

Run of record: `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z`, seed `2794626967`, 24.1 min.

## Reproduce

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

# KS-565 §2 — negative offset reaches Postgres
curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'

# KS-565 §2 — non-string email hits .toLowerCase()
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' \
  http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

Full sweep: `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py full` — 94 replayable crash files with `code_sample` curls under `output/reports/full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z/schemathesis-crashes/`.

## Fix direction

Per [KS-421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-421/blocking-prs-billing-get-apibillingcustomerscustomeridpayment-methods) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) / [KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks): classify the error at the route boundary — map known provider/validation failures to 4xx/503, keep genuine unknowns as 500 with structured logging, and guard path params and body fields before they reach the DB. Add unit tests pinning each classifier. **Fix all six negative-offset sites, not the two the sweep found** ([KS-565](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-565/sweeps-2026-08-05-untracked-failures-across-10-ops-response-schema) §2 lists them).

## Note

The report had been attributing this class to [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) **with a bare ticket reference**, which reads as ownership. PR #656 now renders `KS-431 (closed — recurrence untracked)`; this ticket is the live owner.

Refs as KS-NNN text. Found by the [KS-589](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-589/systemtest-schemathesis-integration-mode-anchor-honesty-consistency-a) sweeps, 2026-08-07.

## Appended 2026-10-07 — raw 500 recurs on `POST /api/auth/wallet/verify`

**BLUF:** `not_a_server_error` fires on `POST /api/auth/wallet/verify`, a raw `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` on fuzzed input. The pair is **not** in `schemathesis-baseline.json` at `develop` b280b74ff. Its sibling `POST /api/auth/wallet/authenticate` is already baselined here (the "wallet-authenticate uuid-cast 500"); `wallet/verify` is a different operation in the same class.

**Evidence.** Run `pre-merge-ks-1445-2026-10-07T14-30-16Z-slot2`: Schemathesis 4.29.4, slot 2 on Peter's Mac, stack built from the KS-1445 branch (no service changes in that branch). Test case `xPmeIe`.
- Body: `{"nonce": " 4\u008dÝ…", "signature": "_", "walletAddress": "Þ򴫱\u008cÜ"}`, with no `challengeId`.
- Response: `500 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"An unexpected error occurred"}}`.
- Path (`services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts`): the body **passes** `verifySignatureSchema.parse` (about `:287`), then reaches `findChallenge(data.challengeId, data.nonce)` (about `:290`), a DB lookup, and later CIP-8 verification.

**Not established.** I did not identify the exact throw site. Slot 2's auth log around the run shows several error types on this route: `SyntaxError … is not valid JSON` from a `JSON.parse`, `CIP-8 parse/verify error`, `Challenge not found`. I could not tie one of them to `xPmeIe`. Replay with `st replay xPmeIe` against a stack to pin it.

**Counts are a floor.** It fired in that run and not in the run before it on the same commit.

**Fix direction:** as above. Classify at the route boundary, so a fuzzed nonce or address is a mapped 4xx, never a raw 500.

Re-verified from source at `develop` b280b74ff before posting. Found while running KS-1445's pre-merge gate.

**Cannot be closed from here; staying open and listed for a live sweep.** This is a recurring-class ticket across eight operations in several services, and its close condition is a Schemathesis `not_a_server_error` re-run on a live stack. Two of its three linked PRs are deployed; the third is not.

After Seat D's current kintsugi deploy lands #1428, ask the sweep owner (Peter's harness) for one `not_a_server_error` run against kintsugi and compare it with the 2026-08-28 baseline (3 operations: `/api/wallets/verify` by-design 501, `GET /api/users/admin/list`, `POST /api/users/admin/create`). I could not run it: the Schemathesis venv is machine-bound (BACKLOG), and the admin-gated operations need credentials this agent login does not have.

## Detail
- **Linked PRs:** #756 (`80880bb71`) and #757 (`0874b0ebe`) are in kintsugi's running revision `69f2045af2a4`. **#1428** (`1e7f90e26`, originate: refuses a negative offset, a null share...) merged 2026-10-08 and is **not** in it; it is in the deploy Seat D 17th is running.
- Known limits already on the ticket: `POST /api/wallets/verify` is a deliberate 501 owned by KS-686 and inflates the count; `GET /api/signatories?organizationId=<malformed>` is a ninth operation (2026-08-28).
- Unit-level verification of all eight operations was not attempted: it spans originate, auth, m365, security and webhooks.
- Seat V 3rd (Sonnet 5.5), 2026-10-12 (lot L06). Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatV-3rd/` (`planted_red_L06.log`, `kintsugi_probe_L06_2026-10-12.out`).

## BLUF
**DEPLOYED and live-proven for one of the three guards; the ticket stays open, as commit `1e7f90e` itself says (it covers 2 of the 6 negative-offset sites in KS-565 section 2, and the sweep recurrence needs a live Schemathesis run).** Not moved.

## Summary

This register tracks the biggest single class in the sweeps: the API politely refusing (4xx) request bodies the published spec says are valid. The steady fix is to bring each operation's spec and validator into line, in whichever direction is right for it. A small new member was added on 2026-09-28: `POST /api/gdpr/consent`, where the database declines a value the spec allows. Details are below for whenever it's picked up. Thank you, Kamil.

+++ The register (2026-08-07) and the 2026-09-28 addendum

### Why a new ticket

The predecessors are Done and archived: [KS-255](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255/fix-tighten-openapi-request-schemas-add-400-responses-for-12-endpoints) (Done 2026-06-15) and [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (Done 2026-07-29, itself the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked) recurrence). This is the same class recurring at a larger scale, filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

### Finding

**734** `positive_data_acceptance` **failures across 64 operations**, about 75% of all check failures in `full-2026-08-07T14-12-05Z` (seed `2794626967`, 22,744 cases, 317 operations; Ubuntu 24.04.4 aarch64 VM, Schemathesis 4.24.3, Postgres 15.18). Each failure card embeds a curl; the run also wrote 94 replayable crash files. Counts are a floor, not a total: generation samples rather than enumerates.

### Fix direction

Per [KS-423](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-423/blocking-pr-pre-merge-schemathesis-coverage-6-contract-drift-failures) / [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked): compare each route's validator with the spec, then tighten the spec to the runtime truth **or** loosen the runtime where the spec is right. Never narrow the generator. Cluster by service registration file.

### Addendum 2026-09-28 ([KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9)): `POST /api/gdpr/consent`

* **What:** a spec-valid body answered **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` *"One or more field values cannot be stored (too long or not an allowed value)"*. It's a draw: 2 of the 6 [KS-1353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1353/bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4275-4280-first-minor-since-427x-9) sweeps (sweeps 2 and 5, ×1 each).
* **The case:** `userId` (uuid), `purpose: "marketing"`, `source` = a 5-character string with a supplementary-plane character, `expiresInDays: 552`, plus 3 undeclared keys (allowed, since the schema doesn't set `additionalProperties: false`).
* **Where the 400 comes from:** `services/originate/src/routes/gdpr.ts:153` (`mapGdprWriteDbError`) maps Postgres **22001 / 23514 / 22007 / 22008 / 22021** to this 400. Its own comment says *"Value the spec permits but the schema can't store"*. So the refusal is deliberate; the gap is that the published contract doesn't declare the constraint.
* **Which constraint fired isn't recoverable:** the originate logs predate a slot rebuild. Candidates: `source`'s unusual character (22021 or a length limit), `expiresInDays` with no declared `maximum` (22008), or the extra keys if they reach a stored column. (An earlier note that said "extra keys → 400" was too specific.)
* **Direction:** a targeted probe per candidate names the Postgres code, then declare it in the spec (`maxLength`, `maximum`, a `pattern`, or `additionalProperties: false`).
* Listed in [KS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1361/schemathesis-baselinejson-lags-the-linear-registers-37-of-90-failing) for baselining against this ticket.

+++

## Addendum 2026-10-06 (KS-571): `/share` and `/transfer-custody` join the register — the exception that hid them is gone

**BLUF.** Two operations that had been hidden from this check now show it, Kamil. `systemTest/schemathesis/schemathesis.toml` used to let `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` and `/transfer-custody` answer 400 under `positive_data_acceptance`. That was meant for the connector-only `onBehalfOf` 400, but it hid every 400 on those operations. KS-571 replaced it with a narrower mechanism (the sweep no longer sends `onBehalfOf` from JWT personas). The real spec-vs-handler gaps underneath are now reported: **26 + 12 failing cases**. Thank you.

>>> Evidence (re-verified at source, `develop` `f556373b9`; sweep `full-ks-571-2026-10-06T10-09-50Z-slot4`, seed 571, slot 4, Schemathesis 4.29.3)

Spec-valid bodies the handler refuses with 400 (positive phase, no `onBehalfOf` in the body):

| Operation | Handler refusal (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`) | Cases | What the spec says |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` | `:1629` "One of newHolderId or newHolderEmail is required" | 26 | request schema has no `required` and no `oneOf`/`anyOf` |
| same | `:1635` "Supply either newHolderId or newHolderEmail, not both" | 3 | mutual exclusion not expressed |
| same | `:1653` "newHolderId must be a valid UUID" | 6 | `newHolderId` is `type: string`, no `format: uuid` |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` | `:2215` "Each recipient must have either an email or a userId" | 16 | `recipients[]` items have no `required` and no `anyOf` |

(Case counts are from the run's HAR, by reason. They overlap the 26 / 12 `positive_data_acceptance` failures reported for the two operations; the 3 `/share` 500s in the same run are KS-593's class, not this one.)

**Also worth knowing.** Before KS-571, `/version` (25) and `certifications/issue` (11) failures under this check were almost all the connector-only `onBehalfOf` 400, not this class (before→after 25→1, 11→1). Their entries in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` cite this ticket. That baseline correction is Peter's (KS-1361), not yours.

**Suggested direction (same as the register):** express the rules in the published contract. For transfer-custody, `oneOf` [newHolderId] / [newHolderEmail] plus `format: uuid`; for share, recipient items with `anyOf` [email] / [userId]. Or relax the handler where the spec is right.

>>>

Refs as KS-NNN text. Posted by agent on Peter's behalf.

**BLUF:** a `positive_data_acceptance` failure on `POST /api/did` in today's pre-merge sweep is a **systemTest harness bug, not a platform defect**. Nothing to do on the platform side; it is being fixed in KS-1680.

- **Where:** run `pre-merge-2026-10-23T13-01-26Z-slot1` (platform-k slot 1, seed `2796048272`, Schemathesis 4.32.1), check ST202 "Schema-valid request rejected", response **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Must not contain control byte U+0012".
- **Cause (verified from the request as sent):** the positive-phase body sanitizer (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/positive_sanitizer.py`, KS-472) leaves a raw control-byte key unchanged when the same object already has a `_` key: here `services[4]` carried both `"\x12"` and `"_"`. The platform's 400 is the correct KS-472 behaviour.
- It appears only when a draw generates that key pair, so it can come and go between runs.

The fix and its red→green test land on the KS-1680 branch. Thank you, Kamil.

**One more member of this class, `GET /api/platform/document-lookup` (measured 2026-10-30).**

- **Run:** `pre-merge-2026-10-30T10-03-47Z-slot1` (platform-k slot 1, Peter's Mac, Schemathesis 4.32.1, seed 881726611). The platform is `develop` `4c14143b3` unchanged; the branch it ran on, KS-1609, changes only `systemTest/` and docs.
- **Check:** ST202 `positive_data_acceptance`, case `iHOnxs`.
- **What happened:** `GET /api/platform/document-lookup?hash=` → **400** `{"success":false,"error":{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"hash or documentId query parameter is required"}}`.
- **Why it is spec-valid:** the published operation (added under KS-1773) declares both `hash` and `documentId` as optional `string` query parameters, with no `minLength` and nothing saying one of them must be sent. So `?hash=` alone is valid against the contract.
- **Same shape as** this register's 2026-09-01 note: a cross-field rule the spec doesn't express ("Either challengeId or nonce is required").
- Not in `schemathesis-baseline.json`, and not added to it.
- **Direction, as for the rest of the register:** express the rule in the contract (for example `minLength: 1` on both, plus an `anyOf` requiring one of the two), or have the handler treat an empty `hash` as absent and fall through to `documentId` as the description already says.
- The KS-1773 deploy note records that no `hash` / `documentId` request was sent, so this path was not exercised there.

KS-577.desc:
## BLUF

@kamil.kreiser **ruled 2026-08-07: rotation SHOULD revoke the prior key.** He accepts that this makes an honest bulk re-key ~1.5 weeks rather than 2 days, on the reasoning that shipping the additive version would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and look like recovery.

**The cutover window is a contract question for** @stuart.jamieson**, not a unilateral K-side call** — revoking instantly means S's in-flight anchor writes 401 until it picks up the new credential.

@peter independently reached the same conclusion on KS-480 (2026-08-06): *"if someone left a company with a grudge and used the key maliciously, the company affected would not look kindly on our solution."*

## Detail

**The defect (Finding A, verified in code).** The rotate handler has **no revoke step**: on `rotate: true` it skips the early return at `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:638-645` and goes straight to the mint. `dbSaveApiKey` (`services/security/src/index.ts:196-223`) is a plain upsert on the *new* key's own id and never touches sibling rows sharing a `connectorId`. Validation keys purely off `key_hash` → `isActive` → `expiresAt` (`services/security/src/index.ts:940-1012`), so the prior key keeps validating indefinitely.

Guardrail 1's own comment concedes it — *"it invalidates nothing by itself"* (`platform.ts:501`) — so this is known at code level. What is absent is any sign the semantics were decided deliberately for the DR case that §4/§5 of KS-480 rests on.

**Consequence:** after re-keying a lost credential, the lost credential still works. Neither half of "lose a key, re-key" has a working admin path on demo today (the other half is [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578)).

**The open decision — cutover.** Options to put to @stuart.jamieson, with the consequence stated plainly rather than softened:

1. **Instant revoke.** S's in-flight anchor writes **401 until S picks up the new credential.** Cleanest containment, hardest on S.
2. **Overlap window** (old key valid for a bounded period). Softer on S; leaves a compromised credential live for exactly that window, which is the thing being fixed.
3. **S confirms adoption, then the old key dies.** Best of both, needs an S-side acknowledgement path and a fallback for when it never arrives.

**Done when:** the cutover shape is agreed with @stuart.jamieson and recorded here; `rotate: true` deactivates the prior key per that shape; a test pins that the old key no longer validates; and [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) step 4 passes.

Sizing: decision first, then 2–3 days.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

KS-365.desc:
## Context — KS-363 follow-up (residual criticals after the base-image refresh)

After KS-363 (all built images → `node:22-alpine` / `nginx:1.29-alpine`, **0 critical across the 31 built images**), residual criticals appeared only against the two pinned third-party infra images. Investigated before assuming "major bump needed" — **major bumps buy nothing for either**, and the redis finding turned out to be a stale local scan cache, not a platform exposure.

## 1. redis — RESOLVED during triage (was a stale local image, demo never affected)

* The 6 crit / 59 high initially flagged were in a **stale local Docker cache** of `redis:7-alpine` (pre-pull digest).
* The current upstream digest `sha256:6ab0b6e7…` scans **0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH** — and it is exactly what the ACR mirror holds and what `secuura02-demo-redis` runs. Verified via `az acr import --force` (digest unchanged → ACR already current).
* `redis:8-alpine` is identical (0/0) — no major bump warranted.
* Done: local image re-pulled + container recreated; demo redis app restarted (idempotent) and Running; portals/API re-verified 200.

## 2. postgres — CVE-2025-68121, unfixable by us today (local-only surface) — the one real residual

* `postgres:15-alpine`: 1 critical = **CVE-2025-68121** (Go stdlib `crypto/tls` incorrect certificate validation, in the image's Go helper binary; fixed in Go 1.24.13 / 1.25.7).
* Present **identically in** `postgres:16-alpine` **and** `postgres:17-alpine` — a major bump does not clear it. It clears when Docker Hub rebuilds the image against a patched Go toolchain.
* Demo uses managed `secuura02-demo-pg` (PG 15 flexible server), so this container image is **local dev only**.
* **Action:** periodically re-pull `postgres:15-alpine` and re-scan; close when the upstream rebuild lands.

## 3. Systemic: pinned-tag digests go stale silently

The ACR `node:22-alpine` mirror WAS genuinely stale during KS-363 (needed `--force` re-import before the demo build), and the redis false alarm came from the same mechanism on a local cache. Alpine-based images republish the same tag with fixes; mirrors/local caches keep old digests and quietly re-accumulate CVEs — and stale caches also produce misleading scan results.

**Proposal:** a lightweight refresh routine — periodically (e.g. monthly or per deploy): `az acr import --force` for the mirrored bases (`node:22-alpine`, `nginx:1.29-alpine`, `edoburu/pgbouncer:1.22.1-p0`, `redis:7-alpine`) + `docker compose pull` locally, then re-scan. Could live in `deploy.sh` or a small script + reminder.

## Scanner note

Trivy v0.58.1; the KS-363 Docker Scout baseline rated redis 0 critical — consistent with the stale-local-cache explanation (Scout scanned a fresh rebuild).

## BLUF — periodic re-scan run 2026-09-08. **The residual has NOT cleared. Do not close.**

`postgres:15-alpine` still carries **CVE-2025-68121**, and the image has not moved at all since this ticket last recorded it.

## Measured, directly — the gate was deliberately NOT used

    digest:  sha256:fe0737ba566a2c5b2a28f34433c0a423261900ec17b9bf7ad115e1aae7e57f1b
    (identical to the digest this ticket's own comment records — the upstream
     rebuild has not happened, so there was never going to be a change to find)

    postgres:15-alpine (alpine 3.24.1)      Total: 0  (CRITICAL: 0)
    usr/local/bin/gosu (gobinary)           Total: 1  (CRITICAL: 1)

| Library | Vulnerability | Installed | Fixed in |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| stdlib | **CVE-2025-68121** | `v1.24.6` | 1.24.13, 1.25.7, 1.26.0-rc.3 |

*crypto/tls: incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption.*

**Both halves of this ticket's §2 hold exactly as written:** the alpine layer is clean (0 CRITICAL), and the one critical is the Go stdlib vendored into the image's `gosu` helper — **not something we can patch**. It clears when Docker Hub rebuilds against a patched toolchain, and the unchanged digest says that has not happened.

**Surface is unchanged too:** local dev only. The demo runs the compose stack on the VM, and this is the container image, not a managed server.

## ⚠ Why I did NOT run `base-image-watch.sh`

The watch is the right tool and it exists (merged via #786). But **the fix for its false-clear bug is on [#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793), which is open and unmerged** — and this ticket's own 2026-09-02 comment records what that bug is:

> *the gate could reach **"THE RESIDUAL CLEARED"** with no currency control running at all — an empty reference image made both control arms vanish, and that verdict is the one that sends an operator at the live registry with `az acr import --force`.*

**Running the unfixed gate to answer "has the residual cleared?" is running a check that can answer yes for the wrong reason, on exactly the question it would be wrong about.** So this re-scan is a direct trivy invocation instead: one command, one image, the CVE named in the output rather than a verdict computed from it.

## What this ticket is actually waiting on

1. **Upstream** — a Docker Hub rebuild of `postgres:15-alpine` against Go ≥1.24.13. Nothing we do moves this.
2. **[#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793)** — until it merges, the automated watch cannot be trusted for the close decision, so every check stays manual like this one.

**`In Review` remains correct** for this ticket, and for the reason its own 2026-09-02 comment gives: #793 is open and awaiting review. Not moved.

*Re-scan by s150, 2026-09-08. Nothing pulled to ACR, nothing deployed, no gate run.*

## ✅ SECOND CONDITION MET — #793 is merged. Stating it rather than leaving it to be inferred.

`develop` `27b0ee294` → **`9806be0ac9a6ebd6e86f2ba896f1f0332ba21787`** ([#793](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/793)). Tree predicted `2675f8e19` before the merge and re-derived identical from the object after; parents from the object; #905 still absent (negative control).

**This ticket was waiting on two things. One of them is now done.**

1. ✅ **#793 merged** — so `base-image-watch.sh` carries its false-clear fix, and the watch can be trusted for the close decision. **The reason I refused to run it at 14:32 no longer applies.**
2. ⏳ **Upstream** — a Docker Hub rebuild of `postgres:15-alpine` against Go ≥ 1.24.13. **Nothing we do moves this**, and today's re-scan showed the digest unchanged at `fe0737ba…` with CVE-2025-68121 still present in `gosu`'s vendored stdlib.

**So this stays a HOLD, but for one reason now instead of two.** The next re-scan can use the watch rather than a hand-rolled trivy invocation.

## Both of Kam's audit-baseline rulings are now on the trunk — verified on `develop`, not on the branch

| ruling | rows on develop |
| -- | -- |
| `earlier` (09:57) | GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g, GHSA-rgwj-5xj2-c3m3, GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx all read **`expires 2026-09-10`** — the date he chose, not the `2026-09-24` he declined |
| `add-dead` (10:35) | exactly **4** rows at **`expires 2026-09-06`** (`fast-uri`, ticket KS-763) — deliberately already expired, as ruled |

35 rows total, up from 31, **delta exactly +4 with zero develop rows lost** — the file was written once and the other 31 were not rebuilt. **No expiry date was refreshed.**

The re-triage ticket Kam asked for is **[KS-997](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-997)**.

**Moved `In Review` → `Blocked`. Nobody is reviewing this; it is waiting on Docker Hub.**

This ticket's own last comment records it as waiting on **two** conditions:

1. ✅ **#793 merged** — `base-image-watch.sh` carries its false-clear fix, so the watch can be trusted
   for the close decision.
2. ⏳ **Upstream** — a Docker Hub rebuild of the `postgres` image carrying the CVE-2025-68121 fix.

Condition 2 is **an event outside this repo and outside anyone here**. `In Review` asserts a reviewer
is holding something, and none is — every attached PR (#386, #387, #388, #390, #391, #786, #793) is
merged, #786 with Peter's approval at head.

Per the column convention on KS-854 — *before moving a ticket into a column, name the event that takes
it OUT* — the exit event here is **an upstream image rebuild**, which is exactly what `Blocked` is for.
Left in `In Review` it reads as work sitting on a colleague's desk, and it would keep surfacing in
every review sweep as if someone were sitting on it.

**Not closed**, because the CVE track is the point of the ticket and it is not resolved.

*(Disposition pass, s152.)*

>

> consolidated comment. **Critical path: B1 → A1 → E1.** Earlier revisions have been deleted rather
> than left alongside it — two files each claiming to be current is how someone picks up a stale plan.

---

## Goal

Give every OpenAPI operation at least one realistic, **runnable** example, so Schemathesis and Akto can generate meaningful test cases instead of falling back to unconstrained fuzz.

This is the prerequisite annotation work for [KS-227](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-227/schemathesis-gate-cicd-on-no-test-cases-skips-once-schema-annotation) (CI gate on coverage skips).

> **⚠ Approach changed 2026-07.** This ticket originally proposed hand-editing `example:` blocks into `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`. **That is not possible** — the spec is *generated* from Zod schemas by `scripts/generate-openapi.ts`, and `npm run check:openapi` fails the build on any hand-edit. Examples must land in the Zod source. The original approach is preserved in the issue's description history.

---

## Where examples actually live

```
services/<svc>/src/<svc>.openapi.ts     ← .openapi({ description, example }) — EDIT HERE
        │  npm run generate-openapi
        ▼
docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml           ← GENERATED. Never hand-edit.
```

The `api-gateway` image bundles the generated spec — but **how you pick a spec change up differs by target** (corrected 2026-08-19, Kamil's review §9):

* **Deployed targets** (Container Apps / the VM's built images) — the spec is baked in, so **rebuild api-gateway**.
* **Local compose** — the spec is **bind-mounted**, not baked (`docker-compose.yml:434`), and since [KS-656](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-656/api-gateway-apidocsopenapiyaml-500s-on-a-dead-spec-bind-mount-while) the gateway reads it into memory **once at boot**, so `docker restart secuura-api-gateway` is what picks it up. A rebuild works only incidentally, by recreating the container.
* **Verify by checksum, not by a 200.** The dev `fs.watch` hot-reload does not fire in the container ([KS-659](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-659/api-gateway-spec-hot-reload-never-fires-in-the-container-a-spec-regen)), and after a `git checkout` the single-file bind mount points at a dead inode — the route keeps answering **200 with the previous branch's spec**.

## Measured baseline vs current (2026-08-05)

| Metric | develop | branch |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Operations in spec | **318** | 318 |
| Named component schemas | **350** | 350 |
| …carrying an example | **14** | **344** |
| Example blocks | 23 | **354** |
| — request only | 6 | **113** |
| — response only | 4 | **172** |

**Examples-phase skips: 303 → 196.** All −107 came from the request-body examples; the 168 response examples moved it by **exactly zero**, because that phase seeds from what a caller *sends*. Detail in the 2026-08-05 comment.

### Superseded 2026-07-20 baseline (for the record)

| Metric | Value |
| -- | -- |
| Operations in spec | **310** (not 329) |
| Named component schemas | **335** |
| …carrying an example | **14** |
| Typed properties | **1,817** |
| …carrying an example | **4** |
| …carrying *any* constraint (`format`/`pattern`/`enum`/`min`/`max`) | **425 (23.4%)** |

**The last row is the real constraint on this ticket.** 76.6% of properties are declared bare `type: string`, so anything generating from the schema — example synthesis, Schemathesis, Akto — has nothing to work with. `createdAt` is a bare string.

## Correction to the original premise

`no_test_cases_generated` **does not appear anywhere in this codebase**, and is not the skip reason the report emits — our HTML report reads a free-text `skip_reason` (`src/html_report/panels/operations.py:51`). The original acceptance criterion was written against a term that does not exist in Schemathesis 4.22.4. Any criterion phrased in terms of it needs restating against the actual skip vocabulary.

---

## The approach: harvest → redact → triage → synthesise → codemod

Built as a self-contained harness in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/` (see its README). **Default OFF** behind `HARVEST_EXAMPLES`, four independent guards, zero runs in CI — the condition of Kamil's approval.

**1. Harvest.** A capture proxy sits transparently in front of the API on `:6882` while the existing test suites run, recording real request/response pairs. **platform-k only** — `config.tiers` defaults to `['platform-k']`; platform-s moved to [PS-348](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-348/harvest-openapi-example-values-from-the-platform-s-test-suite-ks-256) with its machinery retained. Reach is ~13 of 310 operations (~4%) — real traffic simply does not exercise most endpoints.

**2. Redact — in memory, before any write (R15b).** No raw capture artifact is ever written to disk. Credentials become named placeholders (`<password>`, `<accessToken>`) so a reader knows what to supply. Identifiers normalise to seed fixtures so examples stay runnable after a DB reset (R7).

**3. Triage (Gate 5a) — human, mandatory.** Unrecognised fields land as `REDACTED_UNREVIEWED` and are ineligible to publish. Only fields a human explicitly moves to `ALLOWED_FIELDS` may appear as observed. **Enforced in code**, not by convention.

**4. Synthesise.** Everything harvest cannot reach is generated deterministically from the schema — ~96% of output.

**5. Codemod (Gate 5b) — ✅ WRITTEN AND RUN (2026-08-05).** `scripts/spec-examples/apply-spec-examples.ts` — absent-only, AST-derived text splice, masking before shape-fitting, `--regenerate` round-trips byte-identical. 330 examples landed. [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) no longer gates it (merged #603, 07-29). Superseded text follows: The step that writes `.openapi({ example })` into the Zod files. **Nothing ships until this exists, and** [KS-481](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-481/published-openapi-examples-embed-a-volatile-document-id-that-404s-no) **gates it.**
