## RULED — Kam's action, not ours

**Kam, dashboard decision card, 2026-09-02 19:35 AEST** (card `secuura-ks304-ks256-bounces`), relayed with provenance by the coordinator: **"KS-256 → do your sign-off pass and close it."**

This confirms the bounce I posted earlier today, and confirms it for the reason the ticket itself gives: *"Remaining is not authoring — it is Kam's sign-off and review pass, then the pre-merge suites."* The authoring shipped in #782; what is left is the sign-off.

**The remaining actor is Kam.** Two things deliberately left alone: the **In Progress** state, which Peter set by hand at 07:25:03Z, and the assignee. Neither is mine to move while his sign-off is the open item.

One thing worth carrying into that pass, already recorded above: the baseline gate #782 ships is **inert** (KS-752) — `run.py:533` skips it whenever the sweep already passed, so criterion (a) was reported **NOT EVALUATED**, in those words.

KS-1169 (Schemathesis 4.25.2 → 4.27.1, `full` sweep, slot 2, 2026-09-14) — relevant to the inline-examples work: 4.27.1 adds "generate a positive body and isolated negatives when a spec's `examples` mismatch its schema" and "generate a valid object body in the coverage phase when all `example`/`examples`/`default` values are invalid". Measured effect: cases generated 23,559 → 24,300; 10 ops that were 400'd as "schema-compliant request rejected" now reach their handlers; `validation_mismatch` warning 64 → 49 ops; `missing_test_data` 68 → 64. Where an example disagrees with its schema the tool now compensates rather than skipping — so a bad example is less visible in the sweep than before, not more. Also: 4.27.0 ships a native `--baseline` (fail only on NEW failures); declined for now in `deliberately_unused_flags` because it would compete with this ticket's triaged baseline gate (and KS-752). Evidence on KS-1169.

## Results 2026-09-14 — one inline example locks itself out every sweep, and 4.27.1 changed what examples do

Two things from today's sweeps (slot 3, from-scratch stack; `develop` @ `64c386e04` with the 4.27.1 bump) that bear on the examples work:

**1. The `LoginRequest` example locks its own account every run.** The spec's inline example `demo.issuer@example.com` / `<your-password>` is sent by the examples/coverage phase to `POST /api/auth/login` ~34 times per run; the first five consecutive 401s trip the F-06 account lockout (5 failures per email + /24 → 15-minute lock) — auth log `lockout: threshold reached … count 5`, HAR #656–660 on `pre-merge-2026-09-14T12-56-17Z-slot3`, reproduced on every run since. Harmless (no such account), but it is five guaranteed failures charged to one key on every sweep and a fixed 401 stream from that point. Worth an RFC 2606 `.invalid` address in the example — or keep it and note it, since it is the only thing in the sweep that demonstrably exercises the lockout. (The sweep locking its *real* principal was a different mechanism — response-value reuse — fixed under KS-575.)

**2. 4.27.1 changes how invalid examples are handled** (changelog 4.27.1): *"Generate a positive body and isolated negatives when a spec's `examples` mismatch its schema"* and *"Generate a valid object body in the coverage phase when all `example`, `examples`, and `default` values are invalid."* So an example that does not validate no longer collapses coverage for that operation — the phase falls back to a generated valid body. That weakens the failure mode this ticket was filed against (`no-test-cases` skips) and strengthens the case for examples that are *correct* rather than merely present; the examples phase also now *names the parameter it cannot generate and prints its schema* (4.27.0), which is the diagnostic this ticket's triage lacked.

No change to this ticket's branch from my side. Refs as KS-NNN text.

KS-229.desc:
Umbrella tracker for the 2026-06-10 assurance review (SDLC/supply-chain, OWASP, SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001, GDPR/privacy) + full e2e across local/dev/demo. Modelled on [KS-169](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-169/tracker-2026-05-29-security-review-findings-remediation)/[KS-79](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-79/tracker-2026-05-14-audit-follow-ups-security-review-test-infra-rot). Full write-up: `Notes (MASTER)/Secuura/platform-k-assurance-gap-analysis-2026-06-10.md`.

## Headline

App-layer security is strong (argon2id+HIBP, AES-256-GCM field encryption w/ AAD, trust-header stripping, parameterised SQL, RS256 migration, CSRF). **No data-subject PII on-chain** (hashes+IDs+org-name only, with an active `@`-in-issuerName guard). Material risk clusters: a live IDOR, inert tenant RLS, CI security gates not on PR, no data-tier resilience, GDPR program architecture-ready not operational.

## E2E (all envs)

* **Local** Tier 1 API: 113 pass (2 "fails" both non-defects — 429 limiter artifact + local single-tenant `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` artifact); Tier 2 smoke: 35 pass; Tier 3: see thread.
* **Dev**: live-runner dispatched (run `12a05762…`) — tenant isolation is the real test here (MT on).
* **Demo (prod)**: read-only health/verify only — healthy.
* Test-infra: tenant-isolation specs should skip when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`; e2e-v2 tier1 hits the login limiter (cf [KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)).

## Findings

### 🔴 Urgent

* [KS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-228/urgent-idor-gdpr-exportconsentdsr-routes-lack-ownership-check-any) — IDOR on GDPR export/consent/DSR routes (any authed user reads any user's PII). *Fixed.*
  * [KS-258](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-258/testschemathesis-add-gdpr-idor-ownership-guard-regression-tests-ks-228) — Schemathesis regression test suite for [KS-228](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-228/urgent-idor-gdpr-exportconsentdsr-routes-lack-ownership-check-any) fix. Closes `idor_rbac: coverage: PARTIAL` noted in `schemathesis_tests.yaml`. *Backlog.*

### 🟠 High — new tickets

* **CI security gates not enforced on PR** — [KS-105](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-105/ks-49-phase-01-ci-orchestrator-typescript-aggregator-canonical-finding) contract gate + Trivy/Semgrep/Gitleaks/SCA(npm-audit) are `workflow_dispatch`-only. → see linked ticket.
* **Dependabot inactive** — config at dead `Blockchain/Dev/.github/` path, none at repo root. → linked.
* **No DB HA / geo-redundant backups** — HA disabled, 7-day retention, single region/pgbouncer. → linked.
* **No tested DB restore / DR runbook.** → linked.
* **Document the GDPR Art. 17 erasure-vs-on-chain-immutability position** (DPIA note). → linked.

### 🟠 High — already tracked

* RLS fail-open / per-tenant-DB isolation — [KS-160](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-160/tenant-rls-fail-open-when-appcurrent-tenant-id-is-unset-migration) ([KS-172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-172/ks-160-step-1-inventory-tenant-scoped-vs-cross-tenant-query-paths-rls)/173/174).
* JWT HS256→RS256 cutover — [KS-167](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-167/jwt-symmetric-asymmetric-signing-for-production-rs256eddsa-key-vault) ([KS-183](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-183/jwt-asym-step-e-verifiers-verify-rs256-via-public-key-gateway)/184).

### 🟡 Medium (promote to tickets as picked up)

* Per-route rate limiters use in-memory store (per-replica) → ×replica-count (extends [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)).
* Audit log: login `user_id` null + reads unaudited + not tamper-resistant (no hash-chain/WORM).
* Log Analytics retention 30d → raise to ≥90d/1yr (SOC2 window / ISO).
* MFA not mandatory for admin/privileged roles.
* Two divergent MFA-enable flows; `users.ts:707` persists secret pre-verification (cf [KS-158](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-158/mfa-totp-secrets-stored-plaintext-in-mfa-pending-setups-and-likely-in)/171).
* App ships no CSP (relies entirely on nginx) — add gateway-level fallback.
* `requireScope()` is a no-op for human users — no central deny-by-default for function-level authz.
* Cookie consent banner not wired to server-side consent API + bundled/implied consent (GDPR Art. 7).
* No KYC document-image retention policy (Art. 5(1)(e)).
* No Article 30 ROPA / sub-processor register; `Secuura-Compliance-Report.md` overstates posture (do not show customers as-is).
* Breach response not operationalised (no IR runbook / 72h trigger).
* Verify PII keys are Key-Vault-sourced in demo/prod (Art. 32).

## Measured NEGATIVE: the #785 push did NOT walk this ticket out of Backlog

Recording a prediction that **failed**, because the failure is the useful part and because a future seat finding this ticket in `Backlog` should meet the measurement rather than re-derive the theory.

### The prediction

This ticket's own record shows the GitHub integration walking it `Backlog → In Review` **five times** off pushes to [#785](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/785) — 2026-09-02 (×4, four of them reverted by hand the same day) and again on 2026-09-08, the fifth. On that basis, **before pushing** `3611f60c4` to `docs/ks-229-encryptedfield-header` today, I predicted a **sixth** walk and said I would check and restore it.

### The result

**It did not happen.** Measured immediately after the push landed, and again after a second push to a different branch in the same session:

```
state       Backlog          (unchanged)
updatedAt   2026-09-08T04:02:26Z   (unchanged — the timestamp of the last manual restore)
```

An unchanged `updatedAt` is the load-bearing half: the ticket was not touched at all, rather than walked and walked back.

### What it means, and what it does not

**It means the walk is NOT triggered by every push to a branch whose name carries the ticket id.** The standing expectation — that any push to this branch moves the ticket — is **not** supported, and should not be inherited.

**It does not identify what does trigger it.** The five recorded walks cluster on 2026-09-02, four of them within about two hours, and the fifth on 09-08; today's two pushes produced none. Branch-name-carries-id is clearly not sufficient on its own. I have **not** determined the actual trigger and am not guessing at one — plausible candidates (PR open/reopen, a first push to a new branch, a linked-branch event rather than a push event) are untested.

### Why this is recorded at all

A prediction whose misses are quietly dropped is not a prediction. This one was stated in advance, in writing, with a check named — so the miss is reportable, and the negative result is worth more than a hit would have been: **it removes a belief that would otherwise have had five confirmations behind it and no disconfirmation.**

*Measured 2026-09-08 under KS-1001's disposition pass. Ticket state unchanged by this comment; it stays in `Backlog`.*

## BLUF

**PR #785 approved — the Low finding *"fix stale `encryptedField.ts` header (says not-live, is live)"* is closed on the branch.** Approved at head `3611f60c4`. Full evidence is on the PR; the short version is below.

Link: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/785

---

## What the finding was, and what closed it

The docblock on `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/encryptedField.ts` read *"THIS IS PHASE 1 … does NOT yet apply encryption to any live column"*. True when written, false for months — so a reader trusting it concluded the platform stores PII in plaintext, which is a poor thing to hand an auditor in a file called `encryptedField.ts`.

The header now states the module is **LIVE**, quotes and dates the superseded wording rather than deleting it, and enumerates what it protects so a reader can count rather than trust arithmetic: **22 `table.column` pairs over 12 tables in five services** (`auth`, `kyc`, `security`, `m365-integration`, `originate`), stated behind a written predicate so the number is re-derivable.

Two things worth recording for the tracker, because they change the risk picture rather than just the wording:

- **The blast radius is not only PII.** The same helper protects `issuer_certs.private_key`, `audit_logs.details`, `document_lifecycle_events.payload` and the `svc_m365_connections` OAuth tokens — so issuer signing keys, the audit trail and live Microsoft Graph access depend on this key model. A key-management failure here would not be confined to a privacy incident, and the GDPR framing of the old header hid that.
- **Both Phase-1 exclusions have since shipped**, in the same file: searchable encryption via an HMAC lookup column (`lookupHash` / `registerLookupHmacKey`), and the per-subject DEK envelope (`encryptFieldWithDek` / `wrapSubjectDek`).

## Review history, briefly

I held approval on 2026-09-03 for two items, both closed at `3611f60c4`: the header still listed two live controls as out of scope, and the diff carried a whole-file reformat under an evidence block that said "comment only". The first is corrected and now cited by symbol rather than line number; the second is reverted to a byte-exact quote census against the merge base. Kam's self-correction trail on this one (F-4/F-12, F-3, F8, F9, then a full citation re-derivation against develop) is genuinely careful work and is worth noting on the tracker rather than only in the PR.

## Verification, and its limits

Read-only. **The change is behaviourally a no-op**, proved two independent ways — a TypeScript AST walk (1612 vs 1612 nodes, zero differing) and a comment-stripped token-stream comparison whose only delta is six trailing commas and line-wrapping. All string and template literals hash identically across the change, so no AAD context, error message or key name moved.

**No suites run, and none needed** — there is no runtime surface for them to observe, so a run would produce evidence about the tree rather than about this change. No `.env` regeneration, no Docker slot. I re-derived the header's file and call counts (13 files exact; 41 calls against a stated 42, my grep being the cruder instrument) and spot-checked eight of the 22 pairs at source.

## One residual, not blocking the merge

The set lists `svc_webhooks.secret`, which is faithfully the AAD string — but the value is stored in `secret_v2`, the legacy `secret` column having been dropped by `migrations/008_drop_webhook_secret_legacy.sql`. That is the same "AAD names something that isn't in the schema" class as the `mfa_pending` / `mfa_pending_setups` case the header already documents. Nothing behavioural rides on it and the count is 22 either way, so it is a merge-then-fix rather than a hold — flagging it here so it is on the record rather than only in a PR thread, and it may be cleaner as its own Low than a sixth pass over this header.
